# Alert Radix-free, `getRoleColor()`-driven counterpart to the MUI `Alert`. Same `severity`/`title`/`outlined`/`onClose` API as the MUI twin; `AlertTitle`/ `AlertDescription` are also exported for fully composable usage.

Component: src/components/ui/alert.tsx::Alert
Props:
/**
 * Suppress the severity icon, e.g. when the surrounding layout already signals status.
 */
hideIcon?: boolean = false

/**
 * Renders a close button; omit to make the alert persistent (no dismiss affordance).
 */
onClose?: () => void

/**
 * Transparent fill instead of the pale status surface; the status border stays.
 */
outlined?: boolean = false

/**
 * Drives icon, colour and the ARIA `role` — error/warning render as `alert` (assertive), the rest as `status` (polite).
 */
severity: 'error' | 'warning' | 'info' | 'success'

/**
 * Muted timestamp rendered inline next to the title (the Figma Alert's date). Optional.
 */
timestamp?: React.ReactNode

/**
 * Bold title line. Omit for a single-line alert with no heading.
 */
title?: React.ReactNode

# Avatar Radix-based counterpart to the MUI `Avatar`, styled with `getRoleColor()` role tokens rather than hardcoded hex. Uses Radix's automatic image-load-failure fallback to initials. ## API parity with MUI Same `src`/`initials`/`size`/`variant`/`tone`/`status`/`badge` props as the MUI twin.
Prop types (react-docgen) 10 prop types 
Component: src/components/ui/avatar.tsx::Avatar
Props:
/**
 * Image alt text. Defaults to a generic "User Avatar" — pass a real name/role when the identity matters to the page.
 */
alt?: string = 'User Avatar'

/**
 * Arbitrary content pinned to the top-right corner, e.g. a notification count — rendered above the avatar, not inside it.
 */
badge?: React.ReactNode

className?: string

/**
 * Shown in the fallback circle while `src` is empty or fails to load.
 */
initials?: string

/**
 * Makes the avatar an interactive control: adds `role="button"`, keyboard activation (Enter/Space) and a pointer cursor.
 */
onClick?: () => void

size?: AvatarSize | LegacyAvatarSize = 'md'

/**
 * Image URL. Falls back to `initials` automatically on a failed load via Radix's `Fallback` — no manual error handling needed.
 */
src?: string

/**
 * Renders a small coloured dot in the bottom-right corner indicating presence. Omit for no indicator.
 */
status?: 'online' | 'offline' | 'away' | 'busy'

/**
 * Background/foreground pairing for the initials fallback. Has no effect when `src` resolves.
 */
tone?: 'default' | 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' = 'default'

variant?: 'circular' | 'rounded' | 'square' = 'circular'

# Badge A standalone tone-colored label pill — matches what the MDS "Text Badge" Figma node actually describes (see the note in badge.tsx about the existing MUI `Badge.tsx` only supporting the overlay-indicator pattern).
Prop types (react-docgen) 4 prop types 
Component: src/components/ui/badge.tsx::Badge
Props:
/**
 * Pill size. `md` (default) is the Figma spec; `sm` is a non-Figma dense variant.
 */
size?: 'md' | 'sm' = 'md'

/**
 * `@deprecated since 0.6.0; remove after 0.7.0 / 2026-12-23.` Use `variant`.
 * `soft` maps to `variant="soft"` and `soft={false}` to `variant="solid"`,
 * so existing call sites keep their exact appearance.
 */
soft?: boolean

/**
 * Figma "Type" property — which status color the badge represents.
 */
tone?: 'default' | 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'disabled' = 'default'

/**
 * Visual treatment. Ignored for `default` and `disabled`, which have one
 * fixed treatment each.
 * 
 * - `outline` (default) — transparent, tonal 1px border, tonal text.
 * - `soft` — light tint + tonal border + dark text (Figma "Soft background").
 * - `solid` — filled with the tone colour, light text.
 */
variant?: 'outline' | 'soft' | 'solid'

Default story ok

Outline story ok
`outline` — the default. Transparent, so the badge sits on whatever surface it lands on (a table row, a striped row, a card) without fighting it; the border carries the tone. Note `warning`'s label is not gold. `status.warning.fg` measures 3.41:1 on white — under AA — and the gold ramp has no darker step, so the text falls back to `text.primary` and the gold border carries the tone instead.

);

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
import type { CSSProperties } from 'react';
import { StatCard } from '../../components/ui/stat-card';
import { Bubble, BubbleContent } from '../../components/ui/bubble';
import { Marker } from '../../components/ui/marker';

/**
 * # Border Contrast — health check
 *
 * The shared `--border` CSS variable (src/index.css) fails WCAG
 * non-text contrast (3:1) in BOTH modes: 1.40:1 light (#dadada on white),
 * 1.84:1 dark (#404040 on #101010). It's the default border color for the whole primitive layer — at least 6 real components reference it
 * directly (StatCard, Bubble, Marker, Drawer, MessageScroller,
 * Questionnaire), likely more implicitly.
 *
 * MDS's own `border.default` role already resolves to a working value —
 * `neutral500` / `#878787`, deliberately used **unchanged in both modes**
 * (marked `// pivot — unchanged` in semantic-tokens.ts: 3.59:1 light,
 * 5.30:1 dark). `--input`'s own code comment even says `MDS: border.default`
 * already — it was just never actually set to that role's real value. This
 * page renders real components side by side: **current** (broken) vs
 * **proposed** (border.default's real value) — same HSL both modes, not two
 * different ones. The proposed zones override `--border` locally via inline
 * style — nothing in index.css is touched by this story.
 */
const meta: Meta = {
  title: 'Health/Border Contrast',
  parameters: {
    layout: 'fullscreen',
    a11y: {
      config: {
        rules: [
        {
          // The scrollable element axe flags here is <body> itself: this
          // story renders a tall, entirely static block, so the Storybook
          // canvas scrolls while containing nothing focusable. That's a
          // property of previewing one section in isolation, not of the
          // component — on the real page it sits among headers, links and
          // buttons, and the body scroll is reachable by keyboard through
          // them. Scoped to this story only, so the rule still guards
          // genuinely scrollable containers elsewhere (it caught real bugs
          // in CarouselSection, ExpertiseCards, ScrollArea and Attachment).
          id: 'scrollable-region-focusable',
          enabled: false,
        },
        {
          // This page renders light and dark side by side for comparison, which
          // the token architecture cannot actually support: getRoleColor()
          // resolves against a `dark` class on <html>, so components inside a
          // LOCAL `.dark` wrapper still receive light-mode values. The dark
          // zone therefore shows the correct borders (the thing being compared,
          // set explicitly) on an approximated background, and axe reads the
          // mismatch as a contrast failure — #000f47 on #0f0f0f.
          //
          // That's a real limitation worth knowing, not a defect in any
          // component: a genuine dark-mode preview needs the story's
          // `globals: { colorMode: 'dark' }`, which switches the whole canvas
          // and so can't produce a side-by-side. Scoped to this health page
          // only; the rule still guards every real component.
          id: 'color-contrast',
          enabled: false,
        },
        ],
      },
    },
  },
};
export default meta;
type Story = StoryObj;

const zoneBase: CSSProperties = { padding: 24, minHeight: 320 };

function Swatch({ label, extraClass = '' }: { label: string; extraClass?: string }) {
  return (
    <div className={`rounded border border-border bg-background p-4 text-sm text-foreground ${extraClass}`}>
      {label}
    </div>
  );
}

function ComponentSet() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
      <StatCard label="Total Revenue" value="$1,250.00" change="+12.5%" trend="up" trendDescription="Trending up this month" description="Visitors for the last 6 months" />

      <Bubble variant="outline" align="start">
        <BubbleContent>Outline bubble — border-border on bubble-content</BubbleContent>
      </Bubble>

      <div className="rounded-md border border-border bg-background p-4">
        <Marker variant="border">Marker — variant=&quot;border&quot; (border-b border-border)</Marker>
      </div>

      <div className="rounded-md border border-border bg-background p-4">
        <Marker variant="separator">before/after separator</Marker>
      </div>

      {/* Drawer/MessageScroller/Questionnaire aren't easily mountable
          standalone (portal + open-state, scroll container, form context
          respectively) — swatches below use their exact class combination
          instead, so the border weight shown is authentic even though the
          full component isn't mounted. */}
      <Swatch label="Questionnaire choice pill (border border-border)" />
      <div className="flex h-14 w-14 items-center justify-center rounded-full border border-border bg-background text-foreground shadow-md">
        ↓
      </div>
      <div className="rounded-t-xl border-t border-border bg-background p-4 text-sm text-foreground">
        Drawer content edge (border-border)
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

export const Comparison: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <div className="grid grid-cols-1 gap-px bg-neutral-300 md:grid-cols-2">
      {/* LIGHT — current */}
      <div style={zoneBase} className="bg-white">
        <p className="mb-4 font-mono text-xs uppercase tracking-wide text-neutral-500">
          Light · current (--border: 0 0% 85% · #dadada · 1.40:1)
        </p>
        <ComponentSet />
      </div>

      {/* LIGHT — proposed: neutral500 (#878787), the SAME value border.default
          already uses successfully in both modes ("pivot — unchanged" in
          semantic-tokens.ts) — not a new color choice. */}
      <div style={{ ...zoneBase, ['--border' as string]: '0 0% 53%' }} className="bg-white">
        <p className="mb-4 font-mono text-xs uppercase tracking-wide text-neutral-500">
          Light · proposed (--border: 0 0% 53% · neutral500 · #878787 · 3.59:1)
        </p>
        <ComponentSet />
      </div>

      {/* DARK — current */}
      <div style={zoneBase} className="dark bg-[#101010]">
        <p className="mb-4 font-mono text-xs uppercase tracking-wide text-neutral-400">
          Dark · current (--border: 0 0% 25% · #404040 · 1.84:1)
        </p>
        <ComponentSet />
      </div>

      {/* DARK — proposed: same neutral500 value as light, not a separate
          dark-mode step — border.default's own design already proved a
          single value works in both directions (3.59:1 light, 5.30:1 dark). */}
      <div style={{ ...zoneBase, ['--border' as string]: '0 0% 53%' }} className="dark bg-[#101010]">
        <p className="mb-4 font-mono text-xs uppercase tracking-wide text-neutral-400">
          Dark · proposed (--border: 0 0% 53% · neutral500, same value · #878787 · 5.30:1)
        </p>
        <ComponentSet />
      </div>
    </div>
  ),
};

components-button · ./src/components/ui/button.stories.tsx
# Button — Figma V3 Compliant **EXACT API MATCH** with MUI Button for seamless migration. ## Key Features - ✅ All Figma V3 variants (Primary, Primary Alt, Secondary, Tertiary) - ✅ Destructive state (turns ANY variant red) - ✅ Inverse mode for dark backgrounds - ✅ Icon support (startIcon, endIcon, iconOnly) - ✅ Loading state with spinner - ✅ Size variants (sm=32px, md=48px, lg=56px) - ✅ Legacy variant aliases (accent, outline, ghost) - ✅ Typography matching MUI exactly ## Migration Status - ✅ Component API identical to MUI Button - ✅ All props supported - ✅ All states implemented - ⏳ Side-by-side testing in progress
see: [Migration Status](../../../docs/SHADCN_MIGRATION_STATUS.md)
Prop types (react-docgen) 12 prop types 
Component: src/components/ui/button.tsx::Button
Props:
/**
 * Radix Slot composition
 */
asChild?: boolean = false

/**
 * Destructive/danger state - changes colors to red for ALL variants
 */
destructive?: boolean = false

endIcon?: React.ReactNode

/**
 * Stretch the button to fill its container
 */
fullWidth?: boolean = false

/**
 * Icon node for icon-only usage. Required for anything to render when `iconOnly` is set and neither `startIcon` nor `endIcon` is passed.
 */
icon?: React.ReactNode

/**
 * Icon-only button: renders a square button showing ONLY
 * `icon ?? startIcon ?? endIcon` — `children` is discarded entirely,
 * even text. If you've passed text as `children` and it isn't
 * rendering, this is why; pass the icon via `icon`/`startIcon` instead.
 */
iconOnly?: boolean = false

/**
 * Adjusts styling for use on dark backgrounds (e.g. Hero banners)
 */
inverse?: boolean = false

/**
 * Whether the button is in a loading state
 */
loading?: boolean = false

/**
 * Design sizes mapped to Figma: sm/small (32px), md/medium (48px), lg/large (56px)
 */
size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'small' | 'medium' | 'large'

/**
 * Optional leading/trailing icon nodes
 */
startIcon?: React.ReactNode

/**
 * Legacy tone alias. `danger` maps to `destructive`
 */
tone?: 'default' | 'danger' | 'success' = 'default'

/**
 * Visual style aligned to Figma V3 design system:
 * - **primary**: Midnight Blue filled (#000f47) - For dashboards & standard CTAs
 * - **primaryAlt**: Gold filled (#ffbf00) - For hero banners & marketing CTAs
 * - **secondary**: Outline with midnight blue border - Secondary actions
 * - **tertiary**: Transparent/minimal - Tertiary actions
 * 
 * Legacy aliases (backward compatible):
 * - **accent** → maps to primaryAlt
 * - **outline** → maps to secondary
 * - **ghost** → maps to tertiary
 */
variant?: 'primary' | 'primaryAlt' | 'secondary' | 'tertiary' | 'accent' | 'outline' | 'ghost' = 'secondary'

## Figma V3 Mapping — EXACT MATCH with MUI Button This Button has identical API and behavior to the MUI Button, enabling seamless migration component-by-component. ### Figma Property Mapping | Figma Property | Component Prop | Value | |----------------|----------------|-------| | Type = "Primary" | variant | "primary" | | Type = "Primary Alt" | variant | "primaryAlt" | | Type = "Secondary" | variant | "secondary" | | Type = "Tertiary" | variant | "tertiary" | | Size = "Small" | size | "sm" or "small" | | Size = "Default" | size | "md" or "medium" | | Size = "Large" | size | "lg" or "large" | | Destructive = "Yes" | destructive | true | | State = "Disabled" | disabled | true | | State = "Loading" | loading | true | | Has Left Icon | startIcon | React.ReactNode | | Has Right Icon | endIcon | React.ReactNode | | Icon Only = "Yes" | iconOnly + icon | true + React.ReactNode | | On Dark BG | inverse | true | ### Color Specifications (Figma V3) - **Primary**: #000f47 (Midnight Blue) fill, #ceecff text - **Primary Alt**: #ffbf00 (Gold) fill, #000f47 text - **Secondary**: Transparent, 2px #000f47 border - **Tertiary**: Transparent, #000f47 text, subtle tint on hover - **Destructive**: #c53532 (Red) replaces primary colors - **Inverse Primary**: White fill, #000f47 text - **Inverse Secondary**: Transparent, #ceecff border/text - **Inverse Tertiary**: Transparent, white text

components-buttongroup · ./src/components/ui/button-group.stories.tsx
# ButtonGroup Joins related buttons into one visual unit: adjacent buttons share a single border and the corners between them flatten, so the group reads as one control rather than several placed side by side. **Use it for actions that belong to the same decision** — alignment, undo/redo, a split action with its menu, an input with its affix. **Don't use it to save space.** Unrelated actions crammed into a group imply a relationship that isn't there. If the buttons wouldn't share a sentence ("align left, centre, or right"), they shouldn't share a border. ## Accessibility The container is `role="group"`, which tells assistive tech the buttons belong together — but a group with no name announces nothing useful. **Give it an `aria-label`** unless the relationship is already obvious from a visible heading or the button labels themselves. ## Sizing There is **no `size` prop on the group** — upstream shadcn has none either, in the React or the Vue port. A group's height is simply the height of what it contains, so set `size` on the child `Button`s (`sm` / `md` / `lg`) and the group follows. See the **Sizes** and **IconSizes** stories. ## Related - `ToggleGroup` — when the buttons represent *state* (pressed / not pressed), not one-off actions. A text-alignment control that shows which alignment is currently active is a ToggleGroup; one that just applies an alignment is a ButtonGroup. - `InputGroup` — when the unit is built around an input rather than buttons.

Sizes story ok
**Size comes from the buttons, not the group.** `ButtonGroup` has no `size` prop — upstream shadcn doesn't have one either, in the React or Vue port. Set `size` on each child `Button` and the group adopts that scale, because its own height is just the height of what it contains. Keep one size per group. Mixing them makes the shared border step mid-row and the unit stops reading as one control.
const Sizes = () => (
  <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-4">
    <ButtonGroup aria-label="Small">
      <Button variant="outline" size="sm">Small</Button>
      <Button variant="outline" size="sm">Small</Button>
      <Button variant="outline" size="sm">Small</Button>
    </ButtonGroup>
    <ButtonGroup aria-label="Default">
      <Button variant="outline" size="md">Default</Button>
      <Button variant="outline" size="md">Default</Button>
      <Button variant="outline" size="md">Default</Button>
    </ButtonGroup>
    <ButtonGroup aria-label="Large">
      <Button variant="outline" size="lg">Large</Button>
      <Button variant="outline" size="lg">Large</Button>
      <Button variant="outline" size="lg">Large</Button>
    </ButtonGroup>
  </div>
);

const DisabledState = () => (
  <div style={{ padding: '24px' }}>
    <Card
      variant="outlined"
      sx={{
        width: '100%',
        minWidth: '280px',
        maxWidth: 'clamp(18rem, 60vw, 26rem)',
        borderRadius: 3,
        // 0.6 faded the copy to 2.68:1. WCAG 1.4.3's exemption for inactive
        // components genuinely applies here — the card is labelled
        // non-interactive and holds a disabled Button — but a fade that deep
        // makes the state unreadable rather than merely de-emphasised. 0.85
        // still reads clearly as disabled while keeping the text legible.
        opacity: 0.85,

      <CardContent sx={{ p: 3 }}>
        <Stack spacing={2}>

With Slide Counter story ok 
const WithSlideCounter = () => {
  const [api, setApi] = useState<CarouselApi>();
  const [current, setCurrent] = useState(1);
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!api) return;
    setCount(api.scrollSnapList().length);
    setCurrent(api.selectedScrollSnap() + 1);
    api.on('select', () => setCurrent(api.selectedScrollSnap() + 1));
  }, [api]);

  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-xs">
      <Carousel setApi={setApi}>
        <CarouselContent>
          {Array.from({ length: 6 }, (_, i) => (
            <CarouselItem key={i}>
              <Slide n={i + 1} />
            </CarouselItem>
          ))}
        </CarouselContent>
        <CarouselPrevious />
        <CarouselNext />
      </Carousel>
      <p className="mt-2 text-center text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        Slide {current} of {count}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
};

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
import { Area, AreaChart, Bar, BarChart, CartesianGrid, Cell, Line, LineChart, Pie, PieChart, XAxis, YAxis } from 'recharts';
import { getRoleColor } from '@/theme/roles';
import { ChartContainer, ChartLegend, ChartLegendContent, ChartTooltip, ChartTooltipContent, type ChartConfig } from './chart';

/**
 * # Chart
 *
 * No MDS/Figma spec exists for this component — built directly on
 * Recharts with a `ChartConfig` wrapper, following this repo's
 * `dataviz` skill. Series default to `--chart-1`..`--chart-5` — five brand
 * hues (green, blue, gold, purple, red) validated for CVD-safe adjacency in
 * both light and dark mode via `node scripts/validate_palette.js`. That
 * order is load-bearing — don't reassign it.
 *
 * Every example ships a tooltip + legend by default (identity is never
 * color-alone) and uses recessive grid/axis lines.
 */
const meta: Meta = {
  title: 'Components/Chart',
  tags: ['autodocs'],
  parameters: {
    layout: 'padded',
  },
};

export default meta;

const premiumByMonth = [
  { month: 'Jan', property: 4200, liability: 2800 },
  { month: 'Feb', property: 3800, liability: 3100 },
  { month: 'Mar', property: 5100, liability: 2600 },
  { month: 'Apr', property: 4700, liability: 3400 },
  { month: 'May', property: 5600, liability: 3900 },
  { month: 'Jun', property: 6100, liability: 4200 },
];

const twoSeriesConfig: ChartConfig = {
  property: { label: 'Property' },
  liability: { label: 'Liability' },
};

export const LineChartExample: StoryObj = {
  render: () => (
    <ChartContainer config={twoSeriesConfig} className="h-[300px] w-full max-w-2xl">
      <LineChart data={premiumByMonth}>
        <CartesianGrid strokeDasharray="3 3" stroke={getRoleColor('border.default')} vertical={false} />
        <XAxis dataKey="month" stroke={getRoleColor('fg.neutral.subtle')} tickLine={false} axisLine={false} />
        <YAxis stroke={getRoleColor('fg.neutral.subtle')} tickLine={false} axisLine={false} />
        <ChartTooltip content={<ChartTooltipContent />} />
        <ChartLegend content={<ChartLegendContent />} />
        <Line type="monotone" dataKey="property" stroke="var(--color-property)" strokeWidth={2} dot={{ r: 4 }} />
        <Line type="monotone" dataKey="liability" stroke="var(--color-liability)" strokeWidth={2} dot={{ r: 4 }} />
      </LineChart>
    </ChartContainer>
  ),
};

export const BarChartExample: StoryObj = {
  render: () => (
    <ChartContainer config={twoSeriesConfig} className="h-[300px] w-full max-w-2xl">
      <BarChart data={premiumByMonth}>
        <CartesianGrid strokeDasharray="3 3" stroke={getRoleColor('border.default')} vertical={false} />
        <XAxis dataKey="month" stroke={getRoleColor('fg.neutral.subtle')} tickLine={false} axisLine={false} />
        <YAxis stroke={getRoleColor('fg.neutral.subtle')} tickLine={false} axisLine={false} />
        <ChartTooltip content={<ChartTooltipContent />} />
        <ChartLegend content={<ChartLegendContent />} />
        <Bar dataKey="property" fill="var(--color-property)" radius={[4, 4, 0, 0]} />
        <Bar dataKey="liability" fill="var(--color-liability)" radius={[4, 4, 0, 0]} />
      </BarChart>
    </ChartContainer>
  ),
};

export const AreaChartExample: StoryObj = {
  render: () => (
    <ChartContainer config={twoSeriesConfig} className="h-[300px] w-full max-w-2xl">
      <AreaChart data={premiumByMonth}>
        <CartesianGrid strokeDasharray="3 3" stroke={getRoleColor('border.default')} vertical={false} />
        <XAxis dataKey="month" stroke={getRoleColor('fg.neutral.subtle')} tickLine={false} axisLine={false} />
        <YAxis stroke={getRoleColor('fg.neutral.subtle')} tickLine={false} axisLine={false} />
        <ChartTooltip content={<ChartTooltipContent />} />
        <ChartLegend content={<ChartLegendContent />} />
        <Area type="monotone" dataKey="property" stroke="var(--color-property)" fill="var(--color-property)" fillOpacity={0.2} strokeWidth={2} />
        <Area type="monotone" dataKey="liability" stroke="var(--color-liability)" fill="var(--color-liability)" fillOpacity={0.2} strokeWidth={2} />
      </AreaChart>
    </ChartContainer>
  ),
};

const claimsByType = [
  { type: 'property', value: 42 },
  { type: 'auto', value: 28 },
  { type: 'liability', value: 18 },
  { type: 'cyber', value: 8 },
  { type: 'workers-comp', value: 4 },
];

const claimsConfig: ChartConfig = {
  property: { label: 'Property' },
  auto: { label: 'Auto' },
  liability: { label: 'Liability' },
  cyber: { label: 'Cyber' },
  'workers-comp': { label: 'Workers Comp' },
};

export const PieChartExample: StoryObj = {
  render: () => (
    <ChartContainer config={claimsConfig} className="h-[300px] w-full max-w-md">
      <PieChart>
        <ChartTooltip content={<ChartTooltipContent hideLabel />} />
        <ChartLegend content={<ChartLegendContent />} />
        <Pie data={claimsByType} dataKey="value" nameKey="type" innerRadius={50} outerRadius={90} paddingAngle={2}>
          {claimsByType.map((entry) => (
            <Cell key={entry.type} fill={`var(--color-${entry.type})`} stroke={getRoleColor('bg.default')} strokeWidth={2} />
          ))}
        </Pie>
      </PieChart>
    </ChartContainer>
  ),
};

export const SingleSeriesNoLegend: StoryObj = {
  render: () => (
    <ChartContainer config={{ property: { label: 'Property premium' } }} className="h-[240px] w-full max-w-xl">
      <LineChart data={premiumByMonth}>
        <CartesianGrid strokeDasharray="3 3" stroke={getRoleColor('border.default')} vertical={false} />
        <XAxis dataKey="month" stroke={getRoleColor('fg.neutral.subtle')} tickLine={false} axisLine={false} />
        <YAxis stroke={getRoleColor('fg.neutral.subtle')} tickLine={false} axisLine={false} />
        <ChartTooltip content={<ChartTooltipContent />} />
        <Line type="monotone" dataKey="property" stroke="var(--color-property)" strokeWidth={2} dot={{ r: 4 }} />
      </LineChart>
    </ChartContainer>
  ),
};

/**
 * A chart with no error state renders an empty plot area, which a reader
 * interprets as **zero** rather than "this failed to load" — the same
 * "looks like an answer" failure the tables had.
 */
export const DataStates: StoryObj = {
  render: () => (
    <div className="grid gap-6 lg:grid-cols-3">
      <div>
        <p className="mb-2 text-xs font-medium text-muted-foreground">loading</p>
        <ChartContainer config={{ v: { label: 'Value' } }} loading>
          <LineChart data={[]} />
        </ChartContainer>
      </div>
      <div>
        <p className="mb-2 text-xs font-medium text-muted-foreground">loadError</p>
        <ChartContainer config={{ v: { label: 'Value' } }} loadError onRetry={() => {}}>
          <LineChart data={[]} />
        </ChartContainer>
      </div>
      <div>
        <p className="mb-2 text-xs font-medium text-muted-foreground">empty</p>
        <ChartContainer config={{ v: { label: 'Value' } }} isEmpty>
          <LineChart data={[]} />
        </ChartContainer>
      </div>
    </div>
  ),
};

Selectable Group story ok 
const SelectableGroup = () => {
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string[]>(['auto']);
  const options = [
    { value: 'auto', label: 'Auto' },
    { value: 'home', label: 'Home' },
    { value: 'life', label: 'Life' },
    { value: 'travel', label: 'Travel' },
  ];
  const toggle = (value: string) =>
    setSelected((prev) => (prev.includes(value) ? prev.filter((v) => v !== value) : [...prev, value]));

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
      {options.map((opt) => (
        <Chip
          key={opt.value}
          label={opt.label}
          tone="primary"
          selectable
          selected={selected.includes(opt.value)}
          onClick={() => toggle(opt.value)}
        />
      ))}
    </div>
  );
};

Command Palette story ok 
const CommandPalette = () => {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

  useEffect(() => {
    const handler = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
      if (e.key === 'k' && (e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey)) {
        e.preventDefault();
        setOpen((o) => !o);
      }
    };
    document.addEventListener('keydown', handler);
    return () => document.removeEventListener('keydown', handler);
  }, []);

  return (
    <>
      <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Open command palette (⌘K)</Button>
      <CommandDialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
        <CommandInput placeholder="Type a command or search..." />
        <CommandList>
          <CommandEmpty>No results found.</CommandEmpty>
          <CommandGroup heading="Navigation">
            <CommandItem>Go to Dashboard</CommandItem>
            <CommandItem>Go to Policies</CommandItem>
            <CommandItem>Go to Claims</CommandItem>
          </CommandGroup>
        </CommandList>
      </CommandDialog>
    </>
  );
};

components-error-state · ./src/components/ui/error-state.stories.tsx
# Error State The failure state for a data surface. The root is `role="alert"`, so a dead fetch is *announced* rather than silently reading as "No data yet" — indistinguishable from a genuinely empty result, the worst dashboard failure mode. The title is a `<div>`, never a heading, so dropping one into a table or card at any depth can't break heading order. Pass `title` / `description` / `onRetry` for the standard `DataError` composition shown here; use the slot components (`ErrorStateHeader`, `ErrorStateMedia`, …) when you need full control.

components-datagrid · ./src/components/ui/data-grid.stories.tsx
# DataGrid The composable grid. `DataTable` is the batteries-included preset over exactly these parts — reach for these directly when you need to own the table instance, read its state, or arrange the pieces differently. The consumer builds the table with `useTable` and the repo's own `dataGridFeatures`, so every slice of state (sorting, filters, selection) is theirs to read and control. That is the thing `DataTable` cannot do: its state is private, so a consumer literally cannot find out which rows are selected.

components-datagrid-celleditor · ./src/components/ui/data-grid-cell-edit.stories.tsx
The in-cell editor used by DataGrid's spreadsheet mode. Deliberately dumb: it holds draft text and reports it. Parsing, validation and "is this actually a change?" all belong to the caller, which is the only thing that knows the column's type. Only `text` and `textarea` exist, matching the `cellEdit.control` contract. A number or date column does not need a different *control* — it needs a different *parse* on commit, which is the caller's job. Exported so a consumer can build a custom grid cell with the same keyboard contract. Inside `DataGrid` you never render it directly.

components-datastate · ./src/components/ui/data-state.stories.tsx
# Data states Every data surface has four states, and a dashboard is mostly the states around the data rather than the data itself. Before this contract, measured across the 75 modules in `src/components/ui/`: **3** accepted `loading` (under 4 names), **3** accepted an empty state (under 3 names and 2 types), and **0** could express a failed fetch. So a dead API rendered as "No data yet" — indistinguishable from a genuinely empty result, which is the worst available failure mode because it looks like an answer. Precedence is fixed: **loading > error > empty > ready**.

components-datatable · ./src/components/ui/data-table.stories.tsx
# DataTable No MDS/Figma spec exists for this component — built matching the standard TanStack-Table-based recipe (`@tanstack/react-table`), reusing this repo's own `Checkbox`/`Pagination`/`Input`/`DropdownMenu` atoms rather than duplicating them. This is a separate, more powerful sibling to `table.tsx`'s hand-rolled `Table` — reach for `Table` for the common case, `DataTable` when you need column filtering/visibility toggling on top of sorting/selection/ pagination.

Select All Results story ok
**"Select all" must never be ambiguous.** The header checkbox selects the PAGE — it says so, because that is what it does. Selecting every record matching the current filters is a separate, explicit act, and the banner states which scope is in force at all times. This matters most in server mode: the client holds one page, so "all 1,284" cannot be a set of selected rows — there are no row objects for the other 1,279. It is a flag about the QUERY. A bulk action must branch on `allFilteredRowsSelected` and send the filter state, not `selectedRowIds`. Note each checkbox is named after its record ("Select Commercial Auto"), not its position: position changes under sorting and filtering.
const SelectAllResults = function Render() {
  const [selection, setSelection] = useState<SelectionState | null>(null);
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
      <DataTable
        columns={[createSelectColumn<Policy>({ getRowLabel: (p) => p.name }), ...baseColumns]}
        data={policyData}
        enableRowSelection
        selectionNoun="policy"
        selectionNounPlural="policies"
        pageSize={3}
        onSelectionChange={setSelection}
      />
      <pre className="rounded-lg p-3 text-xs" style={{ background: 'var(--role-bg-neutral-subtle)' }}>
{JSON.stringify(
{
  selectedRowIds: selection?.selectedRowIds ?? [],
  selectedVisibleRows: selection?.selectedVisibleRows ?? 0,
  allFilteredRowsSelected: selection?.allFilteredRowsSelected ?? false,
  totalFilteredCount: selection?.totalFilteredCount ?? 0,
},
null,
2
)}
      </pre>
    </div>
  );
};
Bulk Actions story ok
**Bulk actions (§10).** Selection exists to enable an operation; until this landed, it enabled reporting that one *could* happen. The actions live inside the selection banner rather than a bar of their own, because the first requirement is that the count context is not hidden from the button that acts on it. Three things here are easy to leave out and are why this is a component: - **Scope in the confirmation.** Escalate to "all results" and the dialog changes from "Delete 3 selected policies?" to "Delete all N policies matching the current filters?". The copy is generated from the live selection, so it cannot drift from what the handler receives. - **Partial success.** "Assign" here fails one record on purpose. Bulk operations half-fail routinely, and a success toast after that is a lie. - **Permissions.** "Delete" is disabled with a reason, rather than absent.
const BulkActions = function Render() {
  const [log, setLog] = useState<string>('No action run yet.');
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
      <DataTable
        columns={[createSelectColumn<Policy>({ getRowLabel: (p) => p.name }), ...baseColumns]}
        data={policyData}
        enableRowSelection
        selectionNoun="policy"
        selectionNounPlural="policies"
        pageSize={3}
        bulkActions={[
          {
            id: 'export',
            label: 'Export',
            onAction: (s) =>
              setLog(
                s.allFilteredRowsSelected
                  ? `Export requested for all ${s.totalFilteredCount} filtered policies (send the FILTERS to the server, not the ids).`
                  : `Export requested for ${s.selectedRowIds.length} ids: ${s.selectedRowIds.join(', ')}`
              ),
          },
          {
            id: 'assign',
            label: 'Assign',
            onAction: (s) => {
              setLog(`Assign ran against ${s.selectedRowIds.length} policies.`);
              return { succeeded: Math.max(s.selectedRowIds.length - 1, 0), failed: [{ id: 'POL-2', reason: 'Locked by another user' }] };
            },
          },
          {
            id: 'delete',
            label: 'Delete',

            disabled: true,

Row Actions story ok
**Row actions (§11).** Most of that section is about restraint: do not overload every row with visible buttons, promote at most one common action, and move the rest into overflow. So: one `View` button, everything else behind the menu, destructive items separated and confirmed. Each control is named after its record — "More actions for Commercial Auto", not forty buttons called "More actions". And acting on a row does not fire `onRowClick`: §34 lists that conflict explicitly, and this column is the case that breaks it if the markup drifts.
const RowActions = function Render() {
  const [log, setLog] = useState('No action run yet.');
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
      <DataTable
        columns={[
          ...baseColumns,
          createActionsColumn<Policy>({
            getRowLabel: (p) => p.name,
            primary: { label: 'View', onAction: (p) => setLog(`Viewing ${p.name}`) },
            actions: [
              { id: 'edit', label: 'Edit', onAction: (p) => setLog(`Editing ${p.name}`) },
              {
                id: 'renew',
                label: 'Renew',
                disabled: (p) => p.status !== 'Active',
                disabledReason: 'Only active policies can be renewed',
                onAction: (p) => setLog(`Renewing ${p.name}`),
              },
              {
                id: 'delete',
                label: 'Delete',
                destructive: true,
                onAction: (p) => setLog(`Deleted ${p.name}`),
              },
            ],
          }),
        ]}
        data={policyData}
        pageSize={4}
        onRowClick={(row) => setLog(`Row opened: ${row.original.name} (NOT fired by the action buttons)`)}
      />
      <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground" data-testid="log">{log}</p>
    </div>
  );
};

# Dialog / Modal Radix `Dialog` is composable by design — you assemble header/body/footer yourself via `DialogHeader`/`DialogTitle`/`DialogDescription`/`DialogFooter`, rather than being locked into MUI's fixed title/content/actions slots. That's the primary, recommended API here. `Modal` (bottom of this file) is a thin convenience wrapper over the same primitives for teams migrating from the MUI `Modal`'s `open`/`onClose`/`title`/`footer` prop shape.

DSButton

legacy-mui-button · ./src/components/Button/Button.stories.tsx
Design System Button — Figma V3 compliant **Figma V3 Variants:** - **Primary**: Midnight Blue filled (#000f47) - For dashboards & standard CTAs - **Primary Alt (primaryAlt)**: Gold filled (#ffbf00) - For hero banners & marketing CTAs - **Secondary**: Outline with midnight blue border - Secondary actions - **Tertiary**: Transparent/ghost - Minimal actions
example: ```tsx // Primary - Midnight Blue filled (dashboards) <DSButton variant="primary" size="lg">Save Changes</DSButton> // Primary Alt - Gold CTA (hero/marketing) <DSButton variant="primaryAlt" size="lg">Download Report</DSButton> // Secondary - Outline <DSButton variant="secondary" size="md">Learn More</DSButton> // Tertiary - Ghost/minimal <DSButton variant="tertiary" size="md">Cancel</DSButton> // Destructive state <DSButton variant="primary" destructive>Delete</DSButton> // Inverse for dark backgrounds <DSButton variant="secondary" inverse>Learn More</DSButton> ```

 */

/**
 * Visual style aligned to Figma V3 design system:
 * - **primary**: Midnight Blue filled (#000f47) - For dashboards & standard CTAs
 * - **primaryAlt**: Gold filled (#ffbf00) - For hero banners & marketing CTAs (Figma: Primary Alt)
 * - **secondary**: Outline with midnight blue border - Secondary actions
 * - **tertiary**: Transparent/minimal - Tertiary actions
 * 
 * Legacy aliases (backward compatible):
 * - **accent** → maps to primaryAlt
 * - **outline** → maps to secondary
 * - **ghost** → maps to tertiary
 */
variant?: 'primary' | 'primaryAlt' | 'secondary' | 'tertiary' | 'accent' | 'outline' | 'ghost' = 'secondary'

Default story ok
The default primary button - most common call-to-action
const Default = (args) => {
  const { iconOnly, leadingIcon, trailingIcon, children, startIcon, endIcon, ...rest } = args;
  const resolvedStartIcon = leadingIcon ? <SaveIcon /> : startIcon;
  const resolvedEndIcon = trailingIcon ? <ArrowForwardIcon /> : endIcon;
  const iconNode = resolvedStartIcon ?? resolvedEndIcon ?? <SaveIcon />;

  return (
    <DSButton
      {...rest}
      iconOnly={iconOnly}
      icon={iconOnly ? iconNode : undefined}
      startIcon={iconOnly ? undefined : resolvedStartIcon}
      endIcon={iconOnly ? undefined : resolvedEndIcon}
      aria-label={iconOnly ? 'Action button' : undefined}
    >
      {iconOnly ? null : children}
    </DSButton>
  );
};

  const [count, setCount] = React.useState(0);
  const { iconOnly, leadingIcon, trailingIcon, children, startIcon, endIcon, ...rest } = args;
  const resolvedStartIcon = leadingIcon ? <SaveIcon /> : startIcon;
  const resolvedEndIcon = trailingIcon ? <ArrowForwardIcon /> : endIcon;
  const iconNode = resolvedStartIcon ?? resolvedEndIcon ?? <SaveIcon />;
  return (
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', alignItems: 'center', gap: 12 }}>
      <DSButton
        {...rest}
        iconOnly={iconOnly}
        icon={iconOnly ? iconNode : undefined}
        startIcon={iconOnly ? undefined : resolvedStartIcon}
        endIcon={iconOnly ? undefined : resolvedEndIcon}
        onClick={() => setCount(c => c + 1)}
        data-testid="ds-button"
        aria-label={iconOnly ? 'Save action' : undefined}
      >
        {iconOnly ? null : children}
      </DSButton>
      <Typography variant="caption" component="div" data-testid="click-count" sx={{ fontFamily: 'monospace', color: 'fg.neutral.subtle' }}>
        Clicks: {count}
      </Typography>
    </div>
  );
};

Responsive story ok
Responsive button sizes
const Responsive = () => (
  <Box sx={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: 2 }}>
    <Typography variant="caption" color="fg.neutral.subtle" sx={{ mb: 1 }}>
      Resize your browser to see size changes
    </Typography>
    {/*
      DSButton's `size` prop is a single fixed value, not a responsive
      breakpoint object — MUI's sx-style `{xs, sm, md}` shorthand doesn't
      apply to arbitrary component props. Achieving "small on mobile,
      medium on tablet, large on desktop" honestly means rendering one
      button per breakpoint and toggling visibility, not passing an
      object where a string is expected.
    */}
    <Box sx={{ display: { xs: 'block', sm: 'none' } }}>
      <DSButton variant="primary" startIcon={<SaveIcon />} size="sm">Responsive Button</DSButton>
    </Box>
    <Box sx={{ display: { xs: 'none', sm: 'block', md: 'none' } }}>
      <DSButton variant="primary" startIcon={<SaveIcon />} size="md">Responsive Button</DSButton>
    </Box>
    <Box sx={{ display: { xs: 'none', md: 'block' } }}>
      <DSButton variant="primary" startIcon={<SaveIcon />} size="lg">Responsive Button</DSButton>
    </Box>
  </Box>
);

Interactive Example story ok 
const InteractiveExample = () => {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [message, setMessage] = useState('');
  const [severity, setSeverity] = useState<'success' | 'error' | 'warning' | 'info'>('info');

  const show = (msg: string, sev: 'success' | 'error' | 'warning' | 'info') => {
    setSeverity(sev);
    setMessage(msg);
    setOpen(true);
  };

  const showSuccess = (msg: string) => show(msg, 'success');
  const showError = (msg: string) => show(msg, 'error');
  const showWarning = (msg: string) => show(msg, 'warning');
  const showInfo = (msg: string) => show(msg, 'info');
  const hideSnackbar = () => setOpen(false);

  return (
    <Stack spacing={2}>
      <Button variant="contained" color="success" onClick={() => showSuccess('Operation successful!')}>
        Show Success
      </Button>
      <Button variant="contained" color="error" onClick={() => showError('An error occurred!')}>
        Show Error
      </Button>
      {/* MUI's default `color="warning"` is white on #ed6c02 = 3.98:1 (fails AA).
          White on the DS warning (#c25600) is still only 4.29:1, so warning takes
          the system's dark-text-on-pale pattern instead — the same treatment the
          Snackbar itself uses for the warning severity. */}
      <Button
        variant="contained"
        onClick={() => showWarning('Warning message!')}
        sx={{
          backgroundColor: getRoleColor('bg.warning.subtle'),
          color: getRoleColor('fg.on-light'),
          '&:hover': { backgroundColor: getRoleColor('bg.warning.subtle') },
        }}
      >
        Show Warning
      </Button>
      <Button variant="contained" color="info" onClick={() => showInfo('Information message!')}>
        Show Info
      </Button>

      <DSSnackbar
        open={open}
        message={message}
        severity={severity}
        onClose={hideSnackbar}
      />
    </Stack>
  );
};
With Action Example story ok 
const WithActionExample = () => {
  const [snackbar, setSnackbar] = useState({
    open: false,
    message: '',
    severity: 'info' as 'success' | 'error' | 'warning' | 'info',
  });

  const showSnackbar = (message: string, severity: 'success' | 'error' | 'warning' | 'info') => {
    setSnackbar({ open: true, message, severity });
  };

  const hideSnackbar = () => {
    setSnackbar(prev => ({ ...prev, open: false }));
  };

  const handleUpload = () => {
    showSnackbar('File uploaded successfully', 'success');
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Button variant="contained" onClick={handleUpload}>
        Upload File
      </Button>

      <DSSnackbar
        open={snackbar.open}
        message={snackbar.message}
        severity={snackbar.severity}
        onClose={hideSnackbar}
        actionText="VIEW"
        onAction={() => alert('Viewing file...')}
      />
    </>
  );
};

components-filterbar · ./src/components/ui/filter-bar.stories.tsx
# FilterBar The page-level filter row. Four bespoke filter rows shipped in this repo sharing nothing, and **none of them showed the user what was currently filtering their view**. A dashboard that silently hides rows is one people stop trusting — "where did my policy go?" had no answer on screen. `FilterBarChips` is the part that fixes that. **FilterBar vs DataTable's faceted filters** — not alternatives. FilterBar filters the *dataset* and drives the query; `facetedFilters` filter *within* the rows already fetched, per column, with counts. Using both for the same field gives you two controls that disagree.
Prop types (react-docgen) 4 prop types 
Component: src/components/ui/filter-bar.tsx::FilterBar
Props:
/**
 * Names the search landmark. Defaults to "Filters".
 * 
 * **Give each bar a distinct name when a page has more than one.** Two
 * unnamed `role="search"` landmarks fail axe's `landmark-unique` rule, and
 * more to the point a screen-reader user navigating by landmark gets two
 * identically-named regions with no way to tell them apart.
 */
aria-label?: string = 'Filters'

/**
 * Disables "Clear all" when nothing is active.
 */
hasActiveFilters?: boolean = true

/**
 * Renders a "Clear all" button at the end of the row.
 */
onClearAll?: () => void

/**
 * Size for every control in the row. Cascades through context, so a filter
 * bar is height-consistent by construction rather than by the author
 * remembering to pass `size` four times.
 */
size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'

Default story ok
The whole pattern, wired up — filter, see what is applied, remove it.
const Default = () => {
  const [q, setQ] = React.useState('');
  const [region, setRegion] = React.useState<string | number | undefined>();
  const [status, setStatus] = React.useState<string | number | undefined>();
  const [range, setRange] = React.useState<DateRange | undefined>();

  const active: ActiveFilter[] = [
    q && { id: 'q', label: 'Search', value: q },
    region && { id: 'region', label: 'Region', value: REGIONS.find((r) => r.value === region)!.label },
    status && { id: 'status', label: 'Status', value: STATUSES.find((s) => s.value === status)!.label },
    range?.from && { id: 'range', label: 'Period', value: 'Custom range' },
  ].filter(Boolean) as ActiveFilter[];

  const clear = (id: string) => {
    if (id === 'q') setQ('');
    if (id === 'region') setRegion(undefined);
    if (id === 'status') setStatus(undefined);
    if (id === 'range') setRange(undefined);
  };

  const clearAll = () => {
    setQ('');
    setRegion(undefined);
    setStatus(undefined);
    setRange(undefined);
  };

  return (
    <Stack gap={4}>
      <FilterBar onClearAll={clearAll} hasActiveFilters={active.length > 0}>
        <FilterBarSearch label="Policy" value={q} onChange={setQ} placeholder="Policy number…" />
        <FilterBarSelect label="Region" options={REGIONS} value={region} onChange={setRegion} placeholder="All regions" />
        <FilterBarSelect label="Status" options={STATUSES} value={status} onChange={setStatus} placeholder="Any status" />
        <FilterBarDateRange value={range} onChange={setRange} />
      </FilterBar>
      <FilterBarChips filters={active} onRemove={clear} onClearAll={clearAll} />
    </Stack>
  );
};
Active Filters story ok
The chips alone. Without them a filtered view is indistinguishable from an empty one — which is the same "looks like an answer" problem the data states solve for failed fetches.

    { id: 'region', label: 'Region', value: 'EMEA' },
    { id: 'status', label: 'Status', value: 'Open' },
    { id: 'period', label: 'Period', value: 'Last 30 days' },
  ]);
  return (
    <Stack gap={4}>
      <FilterBarChips
        filters={filters}
        onRemove={(id) => setFilters((f) => f.filter((x) => x.id !== id))}
        onClearAll={() => setFilters([])}
      />
      {filters.length === 0 && (
        <Button variant="secondary" size="sm" onClick={() => setFilters([
          { id: 'region', label: 'Region', value: 'EMEA' },
          { id: 'status', label: 'Status', value: 'Open' },
        ])}>
          Reset the demo
        </Button>
      )}
    </Stack>
  );
};

import { Badge, Button, FilterChip, FilterChipMenu, FilterChipSet, Stack } from '@antoniopezzella/marsh-design-system';
import { Briefcase, Globe } from 'lucide-react';
Default story ok 
const Default = () => <FilterChip label="Active" selected={false} />;
Filter Bar story ok
The canonical case: a row of filters over a dataset, with the applied count and a way out. The whole row is **one tab stop** — arrows move between chips.
const FilterBar = function Render() {
  const [applied, setApplied] = React.useState<string[]>(['Active']);
  const toggle = (s: string, on: boolean) =>
    setApplied((prev) => (on ? [...prev, s] : prev.filter((p) => p !== s)));

  return (
    <Stack gap={3}>
      <FilterChipSet label="Filter policies by status">
        {STATUSES.map((s) => (
          <FilterChip
            key={s}
            label={s}
            selected={applied.includes(s)}
            onSelectedChange={(on) => toggle(s, on)}
          />
        ))}
        <FilterChip label="Region: EMEA" hasMenu icon={<Globe />} />
      </FilterChipSet>
      <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {applied.length === 0
          ? 'Showing all 128 policies'
          : `Showing policies matching ${applied.length} filter${applied.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}`}
      </p>
      {applied.length > 0 && (
        <div>
          <Button variant="tertiary" size="sm" onClick={() => setApplied([])}>
            Clear all
          </Button>
        </div>
      )}
    </Stack>
  );
};
Selection Is Obvious story ok
Selection must survive without colour. A selected chip gains a **checkmark** and `aria-pressed="true"`; the fill is reinforcement, not the signal. This is the story that would have caught the previous implementation, whose selected state was a 2px inset ring — visually indistinguishable from focus, and invisible to assistive technology.
const SelectionIsObvious = () => (
  <Stack gap={4}>
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
      <FilterChip label="Unselected" selected={false} />
      <FilterChip label="Selected" selected />
      <FilterChip label="Unselected, icon" icon={<Briefcase />} />
      <FilterChip label="Selected, icon" icon={<Briefcase />} selected />
    </div>
    <p className="max-w-prose text-sm text-muted-foreground">
      The leading icon slot is shared: when a chip is selected the checkmark
      takes it, because the selection state matters more than the category
      icon and two leading glyphs read as clutter.
    </p>
  </Stack>
);
With Value Menu story ok
A chip that opens a **real menu** of values rather than toggling on and off. `hasMenu` on its own only draws the chevron — it opens nothing. That is a promise the control cannot keep, so the common case is wrapped up in `FilterChipMenu`, which composes the existing `DropdownMenu` (inheriting its focus trapping, type-ahead and Escape handling) with the chip as trigger. The chip's label summarises what is applied — "Region" when nothing is, "Region: EMEA" for one value, "Region: 3" beyond that — so the user never has to open it to find out what it is doing.
const WithValueMenu = function Render() {
  const [region, setRegion] = React.useState<string[]>(['emea']);
  const [line, setLine] = React.useState<string[]>([]);
  return (
    <FilterChipSet label="Filter by attribute">
      <FilterChipMenu
        label="Region"
        value={region}
        onValueChange={setRegion}
        options={[
          { value: 'emea', label: 'EMEA', count: 48 },
          { value: 'amer', label: 'Americas', count: 62 },
          { value: 'apac', label: 'APAC', count: 18 },
        ]}
      />
      <FilterChipMenu
        label="Line of business"
        value={line}
        onValueChange={setLine}
        options={[
          { value: 'property', label: 'Property', count: 31 },
          { value: 'casualty', label: 'Casualty', count: 44 },
          { value: 'cyber', label: 'Cyber', count: 12 },
          { value: 'marine', label: 'Marine', disabled: true },
        ]}
      />
    </FilterChipSet>
  );
};

Not A Badge story ok
**FilterChip is not a Badge.** They look similar and mean opposite things. | | Badge | FilterChip | | --- | --- | --- | | element | `<span>` — never focusable | `<button>` with `aria-pressed` | | job | states a fact | changes what you are looking at | | user can act on it | no | yes | If it does not filter something, it is a Badge. This distinction is the reason this component exists.

        <FilterChip label="Expired" />

Keyboard-only operation, asserted rather than described. A filter bar with fifteen chips must not cost fifteen Tab presses to skip. `FilterChipSet` is a `role="toolbar"` with roving focus: Tab enters at the active chip, arrows move within, Tab leaves.

import * as React from 'react';
import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
import { expect, screen, userEvent, waitFor, within } from 'storybook/test';

import { FilterBoolean, FilterNumberRange } from './filter-controls';
import { FilterChipMenu, FilterChipSet } from './filter-chip';
import { Badge } from './badge';
import { Button } from './button';
import { DataTable } from './data-table';
import { Stack } from './stack';
import { collectApplied, type FilterField } from './filter-schema';
import { formatCurrency } from '@/lib/format';
import type { DataGridColumnDef } from './data-grid-features';

const meta: Meta = {
  title: 'Components/Filter controls',
  tags: ['autodocs'],
  parameters: {
    layout: 'padded',
    docs: {
      description: {
        component: [
          'The two filter controls the system was missing: **number range** and **boolean**.',
          '',
          '`inNumberRange` had been registered on the grid the whole time with no UI able to',
          'produce a value for it, and every product that needed a yes/no filter invented its own',
          'two-option select.',
          '',
          'Both are driven by a [`FilterField`](/docs/foundations-choosing-a-table--docs) from the',
          'filter schema, so the control, the chip label and the row matcher cannot disagree.',
        ].join('\n'),
      },
    },
  },
};
export default meta;

interface Policy {
  id: number;
  name: string;
  status: string;
  premium: number;
  bound: boolean;
}

const policies: Policy[] = [
  { id: 1, name: 'Commercial Auto', status: 'Active', premium: 12400, bound: true },
  { id: 2, name: 'General Liability', status: 'Active', premium: 8200, bound: true },
  { id: 3, name: 'Cyber Liability', status: 'Pending', premium: 15900, bound: false },
  { id: 4, name: 'Property', status: 'Active', premium: 22000, bound: true },
  { id: 5, name: 'Workers Comp', status: 'Expired', premium: 9600, bound: false },
  { id: 6, name: 'Marine Cargo', status: 'Pending', premium: 4100, bound: false },
];

const FIELDS: FilterField[] = [
  {
    id: 'status',
    label: 'Status',
    type: 'multi',
    options: [
      { value: 'Active', label: 'Active', count: 3 },
      { value: 'Pending', label: 'Pending', count: 2 },
      { value: 'Expired', label: 'Expired', count: 1 },
    ],
  },
  { id: 'premium', label: 'Premium', type: 'numberRange', unit: 'currency' },
  { id: 'bound', label: 'Bound', type: 'boolean', trueLabel: 'Bound', falseLabel: 'Unbound' },
];

const columns: DataGridColumnDef<Policy>[] = [
  { accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Policy' },
  {
    accessorKey: 'status',
    header: 'Status',
    cell: ({ getValue }) => {
      const v = getValue<string>();
      return (
        <Badge tone={v === 'Active' ? 'success' : v === 'Expired' ? 'danger' : 'warning'} size="sm">
          {v}
        </Badge>
      );
    },
  },
  {
    accessorKey: 'premium',
    header: 'Premium',
    meta: { type: 'currency' },
    // decimals: 0 — whole premiums, so a column of ".00" is noise in a
    // scan-heavy table. Precision stays available where it matters (§48).
    cell: ({ getValue }) => formatCurrency(getValue<number>(), { decimals: 0 }),
  },
  {
    accessorKey: 'bound',
    header: 'Bound',
    meta: { type: 'boolean' },
    cell: ({ getValue }) => (getValue<boolean>() ? 'Yes' : 'No'),
  },
];

export const NumberRange: StoryObj = {
  render: function Render() {
    const [value, setValue] = React.useState<{ min?: number; max?: number } | undefined>();
    return (
      <Stack gap={3}>
        <FilterNumberRange
          field={FIELDS[1] as Extract<FilterField, { type: 'numberRange' }>}
          value={value}
          onValueChange={setValue}
        />
        <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground" data-testid="value">
          {value ? JSON.stringify(value) : 'No range applied'}
        </p>
      </Stack>
    );
  },
  play: async ({ canvasElement, step }) => {
    const canvas = within(canvasElement);
    await step('the unit is in the label, not only a placeholder', async () => {
      await userEvent.click(canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Premium' }));
      // `screen`, not `canvas`: the popover is portalled to document.body, so
      // it is outside canvasElement entirely. A placeholder would also
      // disappear the moment the user types, taking the only statement of
      // what the number means with it — hence a real label.
      await expect(await screen.findByLabelText('Minimum Premium')).toBeInTheDocument();
    });
    await step('leave the UI at rest', async () => {
      await userEvent.keyboard('{Escape}');
      await waitFor(() => expect(screen.queryByLabelText('Minimum Premium')).toBeNull());
    });
  },
};

/**
 * **The whole filter row, driving a real table.**
 *
 * One `FilterField[]` produces the controls, the applied-filter summary and the
 * row matching — so the chip that says “Premium: over $10,000” and the rows you
 * are looking at cannot disagree.
 *
 * Note the summary line: chips tell you *what* is filtered, a count tells you
 * whether it did anything.
 */
export const WithATable: StoryObj = {
  render: function Render() {
    const [values, setValues] = React.useState<Record<string, unknown>>({});
    const set = (id: string, v: unknown) => setValues((prev) => ({ ...prev, [id]: v }));

    const applied = collectApplied(FIELDS, values);

    const rows = policies.filter((p) => {
      const status = values.status as string[] | undefined;
      if (status?.length && !status.includes(p.status)) return false;
      const premium = values.premium as { min?: number; max?: number } | undefined;
      if (premium?.min !== undefined && p.premium < premium.min) return false;
      if (premium?.max !== undefined && p.premium > premium.max) return false;
      if (values.bound !== undefined && p.bound !== values.bound) return false;
      return true;
    });

    return (
      <Stack gap={4}>
        <FilterChipSet label="Filter policies">
          <FilterChipMenu
            label="Status"
            value={(values.status as string[]) ?? []}
            onValueChange={(v) => set('status', v)}
            options={(FIELDS[0] as Extract<FilterField, { type: 'multi' }>).options}
          />
          <FilterNumberRange
            field={FIELDS[1] as Extract<FilterField, { type: 'numberRange' }>}
            value={values.premium as { min?: number; max?: number } | undefined}
            onValueChange={(v) => set('premium', v)}
          />
          <FilterBoolean
            field={FIELDS[2] as Extract<FilterField, { type: 'boolean' }>}
            value={values.bound as boolean | undefined}
            onValueChange={(v) => set('bound', v)}
          />
        </FilterChipSet>

        <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3 text-sm">
          <span data-testid="summary">
            {applied.length === 0 ? (
              <>Showing all <strong>{policies.length}</strong> policies</>
            ) : (
              <>
                <strong>{rows.length}</strong> of {policies.length} policies —{' '}
                {applied.map((a) => `${a.field.label}: ${a.description}`).join(' · ')}
              </>
            )}
          </span>
          {applied.length > 0 && (
            <Button variant="tertiary" size="sm" onClick={() => setValues({})}>
              Clear all
            </Button>
          )}
        </div>

        <DataTable columns={columns} data={rows} pageSize={6} pinFirstColumn={false} />
      </Stack>
    );
  },
  play: async ({ canvasElement, step }) => {
    const canvas = within(canvasElement);
    await step('the summary counts, it does not only list', async () => {
      await expect(canvas.getByTestId('summary')).toHaveTextContent('Showing all 6 policies');
    });
    await step('a boolean filter can ask for the FALSE rows', async () => {
      const { screen } = await import('storybook/test');
      // Scoped: the table's own "Bound" column header is a button too.
      const bar = canvas.getByRole('toolbar', { name: 'Filter policies' });
      await userEvent.click(within(bar).getByRole('button', { name: 'Bound' }));
      await userEvent.click(await screen.findByRole('menuitemradio', { name: 'Unbound' }));
      await expect(canvas.getByTestId('summary')).toHaveTextContent('3 of 6 policies');
      await expect(canvas.getByTestId('summary')).toHaveTextContent('Bound: Unbound');
    });
    await step('leave the UI at rest', async () => {
      // axe runs after the play function. While a Radix menu is open it marks
      // the rest of the page aria-hidden, and hidden content containing
      // focusable buttons is an aria-hidden-focus violation — a true
      // statement about a transient state, not a defect in the page. Waiting
      // for the overlay to clear is the play function's job.
      await waitFor(() =>
        expect(canvas.getByRole('toolbar', { name: 'Filter policies' })).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden')
      );
    });
  },
};

FilterFieldControl

components-filterfieldcontrol · ./src/components/ui/filter-field-control.stories.tsx
One `FilterField` definition in, the right control out. This is the piece that lets a filter be defined **once**. Before it, the two filter systems each decided independently which control a field got: `DataGridToolbar` took `facetedFilters` and `dateFilters` as separate props keyed by column id, and `FilterBar` took hand-placed children. Adding a field meant editing both, in different shapes, and neither could tell you what the complete filter set was. It is deliberately dumb: it holds **no state** and knows nothing about tables. The caller owns the value and decides what a change means — a local `setState`, a column filter, a server query, a URL parameter. That is what makes one definition usable in all four places. ### Choosing between this and `components/ui/filters` This is a **value model**: a field and a value, with no operator. It cannot express "is not", "is any of" or "between", and cannot represent `A AND (B OR C)` at all. Reach for the query system in `components/ui/filters` when you need operators or a nested tree — that is also what lets it serialise to a URL.

**The whole point.** One query drives the bar and the rows, through the pure predicate adapter (§31) — the visual layer never sees the data.
const WithADataTable = function Render() {

Shareable Link story ok
**A filtered view you can send to someone (§37).** The query lives in the URL, so "look at this" is a link rather than "apply these six filters yourself" — which is how two people end up reading different numbers off the same screen. The structure stays readable: `,` is AND, `|` is OR, parentheses group. Values are JSON so a text field holding `123` comes back as the string `"123"` and not the number.
const ShareableLink = function Render() {
  const [query, setQuery] = React.useState<FilterQuery>(() =>
    createFilterQuery([createFilterRule(['status'], { operator: 'is', value: 'Active' })])
  );
  // Shown decoded, which is what a browser puts in the address bar.
  const link = decodeURIComponent(`/policies?${filterQueryToSearchParams(query).toString()}`);
  const rows = applyFilterQuery(policies, query, FIELDS);
  return (
    <Stack gap={4}>
      <Filters fields={FIELDS} query={query} onQueryChange={setQuery} />
      <code
        data-testid="link"
        className="block overflow-x-auto rounded-md px-3 py-2 text-xs"
        style={{
          backgroundColor: getRoleColor('bg.neutral.subtle'),
          color: getRoleColor('fg.neutral.subtle'),
        }}
      >
        {link}
      </code>
      <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground" data-testid="count">
        {rows.length} of {policies.length} policies
      </p>
    </Stack>
  );
};
Stale Link story ok
**A link made last quarter, opened today.** The schema moved on: one field was removed, and one is now a number so `contains` no longer applies. Both are **dropped and reported** rather than repaired — showing the recipient a repaired query would show them different rows than the sender saw.
const StaleLink = function Render() {
  // `ghost` no longer exists; `premium` is a number, so `contains` is gone.
  const incoming = 'status:is:"Active",ghost:is:"1",premium:contains:"10"';
  const parsed = parseFilterQuery(incoming, FIELDS);
  const rows = applyFilterQuery(policies, parsed.query, FIELDS);
  return (
    <Stack gap={4}>
      <code
        className="block overflow-x-auto rounded-md px-3 py-2 text-xs"
        style={{
          backgroundColor: getRoleColor('bg.neutral.subtle'),
          color: getRoleColor('fg.neutral.subtle'),
        }}
      >
        ?filter={incoming}
      </code>
      <Filters fields={FIELDS} defaultQuery={parsed.query} />
      {!parsed.ok && (
        <p className="text-sm" data-testid="dropped" style={{ color: getRoleColor('fg.neutral.subtle') }}>
          {parsed.dropped.length} filter(s) from this link could not be applied:{' '}
          {parsed.dropped.map((d) => d.reason).join(', ')}.
        </p>
      )}
      <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground" data-testid="count">
        {rows.length} of {policies.length} policies
      </p>
    </Stack>
  );
};
In The Data Table Toolbar story ok
**The integration (§56).** `Filters` sits in the toolbar's `filters` slot, and `useFilterQuery` turns the query into the rows passed as `data` — the whole wiring is two lines. A slot rather than a schema prop, because the query system owns its own state, drives rows through a pure predicate and serializes to a URL. None of that is the grid's business, and a prop here would mean the toolbar re-deriving all of it from a schema it does not own.
const InTheDataTableToolbar = function Render() {
  const { query, setQuery, rows, count } = useFilterQuery(policies, { fields: FIELDS });
  return (
    <Stack gap={4}>
      <DataTable
        columns={columns}
        data={rows}
        pageSize={5}
        pinFirstColumn={false}
        filters={<Filters fields={FIELDS} query={query} onQueryChange={setQuery} />}
      />
      <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground" data-testid="count">
        {rows.length} of {policies.length} policies, {count} filter(s) applied
      </p>
    </Stack>
  );
};

Depth Limit Reached story ok
At the limit, `Add group` is disabled and carries its reason.
const DepthLimitReached = () => <FiltersBuilder fields={FIELDS} maxDepth={1} />;
Read Only story ok
The structure stays readable; every mutation control is gone (§39).
const ReadOnly = () => (
  <FiltersBuilder
    fields={FIELDS}
    readOnly
    defaultQuery={createFilterQuery([
      createFilterRule(['status'], { operator: 'is', value: 'Active' }),
      createFilterGroup('or', [
        createFilterRule(['location', 'country'], { operator: 'is', value: 'BR' }),
        createFilterRule(['location', 'country'], { operator: 'is', value: 'MX' }),
      ]),
    ])}
  />
);
Grouping Changes The Result story ok
**Grouping changes the answer, and you can see it.** `Active AND (Brazil OR Mexico)` matches three rows; the same three conditions flattened to all-AND would match none, which is exactly why §24 refuses to flatten.
const GroupingChangesTheResult = function Render() {
  const [query, setQuery] = React.useState<FilterQuery>(() =>
    createFilterQuery([
      createFilterRule(['status'], { operator: 'is', value: 'Active' }),
      createFilterGroup('or', [
        createFilterRule(['location', 'country'], { operator: 'is', value: 'BR' }),
        createFilterRule(['location', 'country'], { operator: 'is', value: 'MX' }),
      ]),
    ])
  );
  const rows = applyFilterQuery(policies, query, FIELDS);
  return (
    <Stack gap={4}>
      <FiltersBuilder fields={FIELDS} query={query} onQueryChange={setQuery} />
      <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground" data-testid="count">
        {rows.length} of {policies.length} policies
      </p>
      <ul className="text-sm">
        {rows.map((r) => (
          <li key={r.id}>
            {r.name} — {r.location.country}
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </Stack>
  );
};

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
import * as React from 'react';

import { Input } from './input';
import { Textarea } from './textarea';
import { DSSelect } from './select';
import { Combobox } from './combobox';
import { DatePicker } from './date-picker';
import { Button } from './button';
import { ButtonGroup } from './button-group';
import { DSCheckbox } from './checkbox';
import { Switch } from './switch';
import { Stack, Inline } from './stack';

/**
 * # Form Controls
 *
 * Every text-entry control in the system, side by side, at every size.
 *
 * This page exists to make inconsistency *visible*. A design system's form
 * controls have one hard requirement that is easy to break and hard to spot
 * one component at a time: **a control and a button of the same declared size
 * must be the same height**, because they constantly sit next to each other
 * in a row. Nothing enforces that automatically, so it is checked here by eye
 * and by the rendered measurement under each control.
 */
const meta: Meta = {
  title: 'Components/Form Controls',
  tags: ['autodocs'],
  parameters: {
    layout: 'padded',
    docs: {
      description: {
        component:
          'All text-entry controls at every size, with measured heights, so cross-component inconsistency is visible rather than something you discover in a layout.',
      },
    },
  },
};

export default meta;
type Story = StoryObj;

const SELECT_OPTIONS = [
  { value: 'property', label: 'Property' },
  { value: 'liability', label: 'Liability' },
  { value: 'cyber', label: 'Cyber' },
];

const COMBOBOX_OPTIONS = [
  { value: 'beacon', label: 'Beacon Capital' },
  { value: 'northwind', label: 'Northwind Logistics' },
];

/** Measures and labels its child's rendered height, so claims are checkable. */
function Measured({ label, children }: { label: string; children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const ref = React.useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const [h, setH] = React.useState<number | null>(null);

  React.useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const el = ref.current?.firstElementChild;
    if (!el) return;
    // The control itself, not the wrapper — a wrapper may include a label.
    const target = el.querySelector('input,textarea,button,[role=combobox]') ?? el;
    setH(Math.round(target.getBoundingClientRect().height));
  }, []);

  return (
    <Stack gap={1}>
      <span className="text-xs font-medium text-muted-foreground">
        {label}
        {h !== null && <span className="ml-2 font-mono">{h}px</span>}
      </span>
      <div ref={ref}>{children}</div>
    </Stack>
  );
}

const SIZES = ['sm', 'md', 'lg'] as const;

/**
 * The core check: each control beside a Button of the same declared size.
 * Any height mismatch shows immediately as a step in the row.
 */
export const AgainstButton: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <Stack gap={8}>
      {SIZES.map((size) => (
        <Stack key={size} gap={3}>
          <h3 className="text-sm font-semibold">
            size=&quot;{size}&quot;
          </h3>
          <Inline gap={3} align="end" wrap={false} className="overflow-x-auto pb-2">
            <Measured label="Input">
              <Input size={size} placeholder="Policy number" aria-label="Policy number" />
            </Measured>
            <Measured label="Select">
              <DSSelect options={SELECT_OPTIONS} size={size} placeholder="Coverage" aria-label="Coverage type" />
            </Measured>
            <Measured label="Button">
              <Button size={size} variant="primary">
                Search
              </Button>
            </Measured>
          </Inline>
        </Stack>
      ))}
    </Stack>
  ),
};

/** Every text-entry control at every size, to compare padding and type scale. */
export const AllControls: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <Stack gap={8}>
      {SIZES.map((size) => (
        <Stack key={size} gap={3}>
          <h3 className="text-sm font-semibold">size=&quot;{size}&quot;</h3>
          <div className="grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3">
            <Measured label="Input">
              <Input size={size} placeholder="Policy number" aria-label="Policy number" />
            </Measured>
            <Measured label="Select">
              <DSSelect options={SELECT_OPTIONS} size={size} placeholder="Coverage" aria-label="Coverage type" />
            </Measured>
            <Measured label="Combobox">
              <Combobox options={COMBOBOX_OPTIONS} size={size} placeholder="Client" aria-label="Client" />
            </Measured>
            <Measured label="DatePicker">
              <DatePicker size={size} placeholder="Effective date" />
            </Measured>
            <Measured label="Textarea">
              <Textarea size={size} placeholder="Loss description" rows={2} aria-label="Loss description" />
            </Measured>
          </div>
        </Stack>
      ))}
    </Stack>
  ),
};

/**
 * Grouped controls. `ButtonGroup` and `InputGroup` take a `size` and cascade
 * it through context, so every child matches without the author repeating it
 * — and a group with a mismatched child is not expressible by accident.
 *
 * This is where a height mismatch is unmissable, because the controls share
 * edges: before the shared scale, a 40px Input beside a 48px Button left a
 * visible step in something meant to read as one unit. `items-stretch` could
 * not save it, since both children set explicit heights.
 */
export const GroupedControls: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <Stack gap={8}>
      {SIZES.map((size) => (
        <Stack key={size} gap={3}>
          <h3 className="text-sm font-semibold">
            &lt;ButtonGroup size=&quot;{size}&quot;&gt; — children inherit
          </h3>
          <ButtonGroup size={size} aria-label={`Policy search, ${size}`}>
            <Input placeholder="Policy number" aria-label="Policy number" />
            <DSSelect options={SELECT_OPTIONS} placeholder="Coverage" aria-label="Coverage type" />
            <Button variant="primary">Search</Button>
          </ButtonGroup>
        </Stack>
      ))}

      <Stack gap={1}>
        <h3 className="text-sm font-semibold">
          A child&apos;s own size still wins
        </h3>
        <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
          Deliberately mismatched, to show precedence: the group says{' '}
          <code>sm</code> and the button overrides with <code>lg</code>. This is
          the escape hatch, not a recommended pattern — a group normally reads
          as one unit.
        </p>
        <ButtonGroup size="sm" aria-label="Override example" className="mt-2">
          <Input placeholder="Inherits sm" aria-label="Inherits sm" />
          <Button variant="primary" size="lg">
            Explicit lg
          </Button>
        </ButtonGroup>
      </Stack>
    </Stack>
  ),
};

/**
 * Boolean controls sit on their own scale — they are glyphs, not text boxes,
 * so they do not take the text-control heights. Shown for completeness.
 */
export const BooleanControls: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <Inline gap={6} align="center">
      <DSCheckbox label="Include expired" />
      <Switch label="Auto-renew" />
    </Inline>
  ),
};

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';

const meta = {
  title: '_health/Grid',
  parameters: { layout: 'fullscreen' },
} satisfies Meta;

export default meta;
type Story = StoryObj;

export const GridPresent: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <div className="mds-legacy-container" style={{ padding: 8 }}>
      <div className="mds-legacy-row gap-2" data-testid="row">
        <div className="mds-legacy-col-6" style={{ background: '#eef6ff', padding: 8 }}>A</div>
        <div className="mds-legacy-col-6" style={{ background: '#eef6ff', padding: 8 }}>B</div>
      </div>
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    const row = canvasElement.querySelector('[data-testid="row"]') as HTMLElement | null;
    if (!row) throw new Error('row not found');
    const styles = getComputedStyle(row);
    if (!styles.display.includes('grid')) {
      throw new Error(`expected display:grid, got ${styles.display}`);
    }
    const template = styles.gridTemplateColumns || '';
    if (!template) {
      throw new Error('grid-template-columns is empty');
    }
  }
};

HeroBanner

website-herobanner · ./src/components/sections/HeroBanner/HeroBanner.stories.tsx
Hero Banner Component - Full-width hero section with content + image/video split Design Pattern: - Full viewport height (100vh) section - Two-column layout: Content (50%) | Media (50%) - Supports video background OR static image - GSAP entrance animations (fade up + stagger) - Parallax scroll effect - Responsive: Stacks on mobile - Dark variant uses Marsh Midnight Blue background (#000f47)
example: ```tsx <HeroBanner eyebrow="Corporate" title="Four powerful brand legacies coming together" subtitle="Heading 2" description="Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet..." primaryCta={{ text: "Download Report", onClick: handleDownload }} secondaryCta={{ text: "Talk to Our Experts", onClick: handleContact }} vimeoId="123456789" imageSrc="/hero-image.jpg" imageAlt="Aerial city view" variant="dark" disableAnimations={false} /> ```
