Props:
/**
 * Whether video/vimeo media autoplays on mount. Default `true` (today's behavior,
 * unchanged for existing callers). Pass `false` for a "click to play" treatment.
 */
autoPlayVideo?: boolean = true

/**
 * Extra content rendered in the content column, after the description and before CTAs — e.g. a search bar or chip row that doesn't fit the eyebrow/title/subtitle/description/CTA slots.
 */
children?: React.ReactNode

/**
 * Body paragraph text
 */
description?: string

/**
 * Disable GSAP animations (for accessibility/testing)
 */
disableAnimations?: boolean = false

/**
 * Small eyebrow text above headline (e.g., "Corporate")
 */
eyebrow?: string

/**
 * Custom height (default: 100vh)
 */
height?: string = '100vh'

/**
 * Alt text for hero image
 */
imageAlt?: string = 'Hero background'

/**
 * Image/Video position: 'left' | 'right' (default: 'right')
 */
imagePosition?: 'left' | 'right' = 'right'

/**
 * Hero image source URL (fallback when no video). Also the fallback shown
 * if a Vimeo embed fails to load (blocked/restricted/deleted video) — when
 * using vimeoId, always pass this too, or a failed embed renders nothing.
 */
imageSrc?: string

/**
 * Layout style: 'split' (side-by-side) or 'background' (media spans entire background)
 */
layout?: 'split' | 'background' = 'split'

/**
 * Character limit for the description (truncates with ellipsis)
 */
maxDescriptionChars?: number

/**
 * Character limit for the title (truncates with ellipsis)
 */
maxTitleChars?: number

/**
 * Extra content rendered alongside the play/pause button (only relevant when
 * that button is shown) — e.g. a duration label, source attribution, or a
 * "Silent film" badge, without HeroBanner needing to know what those are.
 */
mediaControlsSlot?: React.ReactNode

/**
 * CSS object-position for image/video cropping
 */
mediaObjectPosition?: string = 'center'

/**
 * Gates the entrance timeline. Defaults to `true` (plays immediately on
 * mount, the original behavior). Pass `false` to hold the whole entrance
 * (media reveal, M-logo, eyebrow, title, subtitle, description, CTAs)
 * paused at its hidden starting state, then flip to `true` once ready —
 * e.g. synced to `IntroLoader`'s `onComplete`, so the entrance doesn't
 * play out invisibly behind that overlay and finish before it's ever seen.
 */
play?: boolean = true

/**
 * Primary CTA button - Use variant="primaryAlt" (gold) for hero/marketing or variant="primary" (blue) for dashboards
 */
primaryCta?: HeroBannerCTA

/**
 * Secondary CTA button (outline style)
 */
secondaryCta?: HeroBannerCTA

/**
 * Display character counts over the text (Useful for CMS preview mode)
 */
showCmsHints?: boolean = false

/**
 * Renders the Marsh "M" mark centered over the media column (split layout
 * only), formed from two GSAP-animated halves sliding in from opposite
 * sides — the same motion language as the M-forming animations elsewhere
 * in the app (see `MArrowAnimationTest.tsx` / `heroIntro.ts`), adapted to
 * the single `/images/M-logo.svg` asset's two path subpaths instead of
 * two separate SVG files.
 */
showMLogoOverlay?: boolean = false

/**
 * Shows the play/pause control for video/vimeo media even in `layout="background"`
 * (previously `split`-only, since only split had a natural corner for it). Default `false`
 * — no behavior change for existing `background`-layout callers.
 */
showPlayButton?: boolean = false

/**
 * Optional H2 subtitle below headline
 */
subtitle?: string

/**
 * Main H1 headline
 */
title: string

/**
 * Optional second clause, rendered italic immediately after `title` and
 * participating in the same per-word entrance stagger — matches the
 * "signature emphasis" pattern of the brand's newer marketing pages
 * (regular clause, then an italicized second clause).
 */
titleEmphasis?: string

/**
 * Overrides the title's line-height (defaults to `var(--typo-hero-h1-line-height)`). Use for tighter display headlines without affecting the shared token's other consumers.
 */
titleLineHeight?: string | number

/**
 * Background variant: dark (midnight blue) or light
 */
variant?: 'dark' | 'light' = 'dark'

/**
 * Poster image for video (shown before video loads)
 */
videoPoster?: string

/**
 * Hero video source URL (takes priority over imageSrc)
 */
videoSrc?: string

/**
 * Vimeo video ID (e.g., "123456789") - takes priority over videoSrc
 */
vimeoId?: string

HeroBannerGrid

website-herobannergrid · ./src/components/sections/HeroBannerGrid/HeroBannerGrid.stories.tsx
Hero Banner (Grid build) — MUI/Emotion-free rebuild of `HeroBanner` (src/components/sections/HeroBanner/HeroBanner.tsx), same spec/behavior, styled entirely through the MDS Grid (`src/styles/_grid.scss`, Bootstrap- class-compatible) plus HeroBannerGrid.module.scss — a real, standalone stylesheet meant to be portable/shareable on its own. Prop-for-prop and behavior-for-behavior parity with `HeroBanner` is intentional — this is a parallel build for review, not a redesign. The two deliberate differences are documented inline where they occur: the single `HERO_BREAKPOINT_LG` constant (see above) and the fixed `#ffb700` eyebrow dash color (the source `.module.scss` this was ported from had it transposed to `#ffbf00`).

foundations-icons · ./src/components/ui/icon.stories.tsx
# Icons Google **Material Symbols** (Outlined), self-hosted as a variable font — no CDN, works offline and in the published package. Pick a glyph by its **ligature name** (`info`, `check_circle`, `warning`); browse the full set at [fonts.google.com/icons](https://fonts.google.com/icons). The icon inherits `currentColor`, so colour it on a wrapper (or via a role), not on the icon. It renders decorative (`aria-hidden`) by default; pass `aria-label` for a standalone meaningful icon.

# InputOTP Wraps the `input-otp` package's `OTPInput`. No MDS/Figma spec exists for this component yet — built to the standard reference implementation (`InputOTP` / `InputOTPGroup` / `InputOTPSlot` / `InputOTPSeparator`) directly, styled with `getRoleColor()` role tokens. Each slot reads its active/filled state from `input-otp`'s `OTPInputContext` React Context and reuses the `--tw-ring-color` focus-ring trick from `input.tsx`.

Controlled With Completion story ok
Controlled example showing the entered value echoed back, and a completion callback firing once all digits are filled — the shape used for a real verify-code flow guarding a policy document download.
const ControlledWithCompletion = () => {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('');
  const [status, setStatus] = useState<'idle' | 'complete'>('idle');

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-center gap-3">
      <InputOTP
        maxLength={6}
        pattern={REGEXP_ONLY_DIGITS}
        value={value}
        onChange={(next) => {
          setValue(next);
          setStatus('idle');
        }}
        onComplete={() => setStatus('complete')}
      >
        <InputOTPGroup>
          <InputOTPSlot index={0} />
          <InputOTPSlot index={1} />
          <InputOTPSlot index={2} />
        </InputOTPGroup>
        <InputOTPSeparator />
        <InputOTPGroup>
          <InputOTPSlot index={3} />
          <InputOTPSlot index={4} />
          <InputOTPSlot index={5} />
        </InputOTPGroup>
      </InputOTP>
      <p className="text-xs opacity-60">
        {status === 'complete' ? 'Code verified' : `${value.length}/6 digits entered`}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
};

# List `getRoleColor()`-driven counterpart to the MUI `List`. Built against the real `items`-array API — the MDS `List.figma.tsx` mapping's `<List.Item>` compound-component example doesn't match any prop the actual MUI component accepts.

Component: src/components/ui/list.tsx::List
Props:
className?: string

dense?: boolean = false

dividers?: boolean = true

emptyAction?: React.ReactNode

emptyDescription?: React.ReactNode

/**
 * Why the result is empty. `no-results` means a filter excluded everything,
 * which is a different message and a different recovery action from having
 * no data at all.
 */
emptyReason?: 'no-data' | 'no-results'

/**
 * Full override of the empty branch. The canonical name across the system.
 */
emptyState?: React.ReactNode

/**
 * Copy-only overrides, for the common case that just wants different words.
 */
emptyTitle?: React.ReactNode

errorState?: React.ReactNode

items: ListItemConfig[]

/**
 * The fetch failed. **Not form validation** — see the note on naming below.
 * Accepts a boolean, an Error, or a node to render as the description.
 */
loadError?: React.ReactNode | Error | boolean | null

/**
 * A request is in flight. Already the repo's only spelling for this.
 */
loading?: boolean

/**
 * Full overrides of the other two branches.
 */
loadingState?: React.ReactNode

/**
 * Allow more than one row selected at once. Ignored when `selectable` is false.
 */
multiSelect?: boolean = false

/**
 * Clears the filters that produced a `no-results` empty.
 */
onClearFilters?: () => void

/**
 * Re-run the failed load. Renders "Try again"; omitted entirely when absent.
 */
onRetry?: () => void

/**
 * Fires with the full set of selected `id`s on every selection change, not just the item that was toggled.
 */
onSelectionChange?: (selectedIds: string[]) => void

/**
 * Items become clickable/checkable rows with selected-state styling. Required for `onSelectionChange` to do anything.
 */
selectable?: boolean = false

style?: React.CSSProperties

subheader?: string

import { ManageTeam, TeamsProvider } from '@antoniopezzella/marsh-design-system';
import { MemoryRouter, Route, Routes } from 'react-router-dom';
Default story ok 
const Default = () => <ManageTeam />;
Row Actions Are Named story ok
Every row carries a visible delete control, named for its own member. It spent a round behind an overflow menu, because `primary` rendered icon AND label and printed "Remove from team" down the whole column. `primary` takes `iconOnly` now, so the action is the trash icon the source screen shows — and the menu trigger it replaced was rendering as an EMPTY button anyway (see the fix in data-grid-row-actions.tsx).
const RowActionsAreNamed = () => <ManageTeam />;
Unbuilt Tabs story ok
The still-unbuilt tabs say so rather than showing invented content. Team Setup has since been built (it now renders `<TeamSetup>`), so Delegate is the remaining placeholder — that's what this pins.
const UnbuiltTabs = () => <ManageTeam />;
Remove member dialog story ok
**Removing a member is a choice, not a confirmation.** Two outcomes — keep their client allocations or clear them — so a plain "are you sure?" would be a speed bump in front of the question that actually matters. No Cancel button, per the design. Escape and the X still dismiss — and because BOTH footer buttons are destructive, focus opens on the dialog itself rather than the first action, so Enter does not destroy anything the instant it appears.
const RemoveMemberDialogStory = () => <ManageTeam />;
Add Members story ok
**Add members** — search the MMC-wide directory, tick as many as you want, review the queue, commit once. Four changes from the live screen: no nested "Search Workday Directory" panel (the modal title and the field label already say it twice); someone already on the team is shown and disabled rather than hidden; one selection indicator instead of a tick *and* a checkbox; and arrow keys work.
const AddMembers = () => <ManageTeam />;

/**
 * ISO 4217 currency for every money value. Defaults to `USD`.
 */
currency?: string = 'USD'

/**
 * Non-null renders the error state in place of the table.
 */
error?: Error | null = null

/**
 * Swap for your own fetch state.
 */

/**
 * BCP-47 locale for every formatted value. Defaults to `en-US`.
 */
locale?: string = 'en-US'

onRetry?: () => void
Imports 
import { MarshDashboard } from '@antoniopezzella/marsh-design-system';
Default story ok 
const Default = () => <MarshDashboard />;
Different Locale story ok
The provider is not decoration. Changing `locale`/`currency` re-renders every formatted value — this story is what stops the provider being reinstated as a no-op that passes its own test.
const DifferentLocale = () => <MarshDashboard locale="de-DE" currency="EUR" />;
Loading story ok
Every surface in a loading state at once — skeletons, not a spinner.
const Loading = () => <MarshDashboard loading />;
Load Failed story ok
A failed fetch. The distinction this makes is the point: an empty result and a failed request are different things, and a table that renders "no rows" for both hides the error.
const LoadFailed = () => <MarshDashboard error={new Error('The policy service did not respond.')} />;

legacy-mui-datagrid · ./src/components/DataGrid/DataGrid.stories.tsx
MDSDataGrid Thin, themed wrapper around `@mui/x-data-grid` that applies MDS role-based colours, border, and typography — so every table in the platform shares the same visual language without repeating sx overrides. All standard DataGrid props are forwarded; pass `sx` to extend or override the MDS defaults per-instance.
example: ```tsx import { MDSDataGrid } from 'components/DataGrid'; import type { GridColDef } from 'components/DataGrid'; const columns: GridColDef[] = [ { field: 'id', headerName: 'ID', width: 80 }, { field: 'name', headerName: 'Name', flex: 1 }, ]; <MDSDataGrid rows={rows} columns={columns} /> ```

# Menubar Radix-based horizontal application menu bar — File/Edit/View style — with the same real menu semantics as `DropdownMenu` (roving tabindex, arrow-key navigation between top-level menus, submenu support), just laid out as a row of menus instead of a single trigger.

  MenubarSeparator,
  MenubarShortcut,
  MenubarSub,
  MenubarSubContent,
  MenubarSubTrigger,
  MenubarTrigger,
} from '@antoniopezzella/marsh-design-system';

# MessageScroller ``` pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add message-scroller ``` The core of the chat-components family — anchored turns, scroll-to-end controls, and visibility tracking, built on `@shadcn/react`'s real scroll-state primitive (not a styling-only wrapper). Pre-existing in this repo and already used by a real consumer (AIAssistantChat), but had no Storybook story until now, so it was effectively invisible here. **Complete** (below) is the flagship demo, matching the full streaming chat interface shadcn's own docs site leads with above its Installation section. The remaining demos cover the same ground as the rest of shadcn's docs examples — an empty-state new chat, a multi-participant thread, and two demos built directly on the headless hooks (`useMessageScrollerScrollable`, `useMessageScrollerVisibility`, `useMessageScroller`) rather than just styling: a live scroll-position readout, and a "load earlier messages" flow that prepends content without visually jumping the reader's place in the thread.

NotificationsDrawer

components-notificationsdrawer · ./src/components/ui/notifications-drawer.stories.tsx
The risk-notification panel — a `Sheet` listing weather, catastrophe and policy alerts against insured locations. Rebuilt from the MUI `NotificationsDrawer` on `Sheet` rather than MUI `Drawer`. Severity colours go through `getRoleColor()` and so adapt to dark mode, which the MUI original's static per-severity hex map does not — that is a deliberate improvement, not just a port. ### Severity is approximated, on purpose The role system has no "watch" or "advisory" tier, so each severity maps to the nearest existing `status.*` role. `watch` is the one to know about: its foreground is `text.onLight`, **not** `status.warning.fg` — warning gold on warning background measures 3.34:1, which is fine as an accent and unreadable as text.

PageShell

components-pageshell · ./src/components/ui/page-shell.stories.tsx
# PageShell The dashboard page **template** — slots only, no business data. It exists because the scaffold is genuinely easy to get wrong. The sidebar is `fixed` with a scrim below `lg` and `static` above it, and there is a `min-w-0` chain that must run down *every* flex ancestor between the page and a wide table. Miss one link in that chain and the whole page scrolls sideways — a bug that presents as a table bug and isn't. Pair it with `PageHeading` for the title / description / actions row.
Prop types (react-docgen) 7 prop types 
Component: src/components/ui/page-shell.tsx::PageShell
Props:
/**
 * Constrain the main column to the 1540px MDS container. Defaults to `true`.
 */
contained?: boolean = true

/**
 * Rendered above everything, full width. Typically `<Header />`.
 */
header?: React.ReactNode

/**
 * Id of the main region, used as the skip-link target.
 */
mainId?: string = 'main-content'

/**
 * Called when the mobile scrim is clicked.
 */
onSidebarClose?: () => void

/**
 * Rendered beside the main column. Becomes an overlay drawer below `lg`,
 * where `sidebarOpen` controls it.
 */
sidebar?: React.ReactNode

/**
 * Mobile drawer state. Ignored at `lg` and above, where the sidebar is static.
 */
sidebarOpen?: boolean = false

/**
 * Renders a "Skip to main content" link as the first focusable element.
 * On by default.
 * 
 * A dashboard puts a header and a full side navigation ahead of the
 * content, so a keyboard user otherwise tabs through every nav item on
 * every page before reaching anything. This is the fix for the one
 * accessibility claim on the product page that the codebase could not
 * substantiate — skip links existed in two marketing pages and nowhere in
 * the dashboard product itself.
 */
skipLink?: boolean = true

Default story ok
The full arrangement: header, sidebar, heading and content.
const Default = () => {
  const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false);
  return (
    <PageShell
      sidebarOpen={open}
      onSidebarClose={() => setOpen(false)}
      header={<Header sidebarOpen={open} onToggleSidebar={() => setOpen((v) => !v)} />}
      sidebar={
        <SideNavigation
          items={NAV_ITEMS}
          currentPath="/"
          onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
          className="fixed inset-y-0 left-0 z-50 w-72 shrink-0 lg:static lg:z-auto lg:w-auto"
        />
      }
    >
      <PageHeading
        title="Overview"
        description="Your portfolio at a glance."
        actions={
          <Button variant="primary" size="sm">
            New claim
          </Button>
        }
      />
      {/*
        The sr-only <h2> is load-bearing, not decoration. `StatCard` renders
        its label as an <h3> and offers no way to change that, so placing a
        stats grid directly under the <h1> from PageHeading skips a level
        and fails the axe heading-order rule — which is exactly how this
        story failed the first time it ran.

        A visually hidden section heading fixes the document outline without
        touching the visual design, and gives screen-reader users a real
        landmark to navigate to. Model this on any page that groups cards.
      */}
      <section className="mb-8">
        <h2 className="sr-only">Key metrics</h2>
        <div className="grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4">
          <StatCard label="Active policies" value="24" />
          <StatCard label="Open claims" value="3" />
          <StatCard label="Renewals due" value="7" />
          <StatCard label="Total premium" value="$1.2M" />
        </div>
      </section>
      <Card>
        <CardContent className="p-6">
          <Stack gap={2}>
            <span className="text-sm font-semibold">Recent activity</span>
            <span className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
              Content sits inside the shell&apos;s contained main column.
            </span>
          </Stack>
        </CardContent>
      </Card>
    </PageShell>
  );
};

/**
 * # Progress
 *
 * `CircularProgress` (hand-rolled SVG — Radix has no circular primitive) and
 * `LinearProgress` (built on `@radix-ui/react-progress`), both styled with

 * `DSLinearProgress` twins.

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
import type { CSSProperties } from 'react';
import { ResizablePanelGroup, ResizablePanel, ResizableHandle } from './resizable';

/**
 * # Resizable
 *
 * Wraps `react-resizable-panels`. No MDS/Figma spec exists for this
 * component yet — built to the standard reference implementation
 * (`ResizablePanelGroup` / `ResizablePanel` / `ResizableHandle`), styled
 * with `getRoleColor()` role tokens rather than hardcoded hex.
 *
 * Note: the installed `react-resizable-panels` is v4, which renamed its
 * `PanelGroup`/`Panel`/`PanelResizeHandle` exports to `Group`/`Panel`/
 * `Separator` (and `direction` to `orientation`) — see the comment at the
 * top of `resizable.tsx` for details. The public component names here still
 * match the classic headless-UI recipe.
 */
const meta: Meta<typeof ResizablePanelGroup> = {
  title: 'Components/Resizable',
  tags: ['autodocs'],
  parameters: {
    layout: 'centered',
    docs: {
      description: {
        component: 'Split layout with draggable dividers, for panes users can resize to taste.',
      },
    },
    a11y: {
      config: {
        rules: [
          {
            // Upstream limitation in react-resizable-panels 4.12.2, not
            // something this wrapper can fix — see the long note on
            // ResizablePanel in resizable.tsx. Each Panel's scroll container
            // is an inner div the library exposes no props for, so it cannot
            // be made focusable. Scoped off HERE (not globally) so the rule
            // still guards every other component, and so this shows up as a
            // deliberate, explained exception rather than a silent pass.
            id: 'scrollable-region-focusable',
            enabled: false,
          },
        ],
      },
    },
  },
};

export default meta;

const boxStyle: CSSProperties = {
  display: 'flex',
  height: '100%',
  alignItems: 'center',
  justifyContent: 'center',
  fontSize: '0.875rem',
};

export const Default: StoryObj = {
  render: () => (
    <ResizablePanelGroup orientation="horizontal" className="h-[240px] w-[500px] rounded-md border">
      <ResizablePanel defaultSize={50}>
        <div style={boxStyle}>Panel One</div>
      </ResizablePanel>
      <ResizableHandle />
      <ResizablePanel defaultSize={50}>
        <div style={boxStyle}>Panel Two</div>
      </ResizablePanel>
    </ResizablePanelGroup>
  ),
};

export const WithHandle: StoryObj = {
  render: () => (
    <ResizablePanelGroup orientation="horizontal" className="h-[240px] w-[500px] rounded-md border">
      <ResizablePanel defaultSize={50}>
        <div style={boxStyle}>Panel One</div>
      </ResizablePanel>
      <ResizableHandle withHandle />
      <ResizablePanel defaultSize={50}>
        <div style={boxStyle}>Panel Two</div>
      </ResizablePanel>
    </ResizablePanelGroup>
  ),
};

export const Vertical: StoryObj = {

      </ResizablePanel>

 * When the scrollbar is visible. Radix default is `'hover'` (shown
 * while scrolling or hovering the area) — `'always'` suits a surface

components-select · ./src/components/ui/select.stories.tsx
# Select Radix `Select` renders a real custom-styled listbox — not a native `<select>` — with proper keyboard nav, typeahead, and viewport-aware positioning. That's a materially better foundation than MUI's Select, so the composable primitives are the primary API here. `DSSelect` (bottom of this file) is a convenience wrapper matching MUI's `options`/`label`/`helperText`/`error`/`tone` prop shape for migration.

      <SelectGroup>

        </SelectItem>
      </SelectGroup>
    </SelectContent>

Component: src/components/ui/side-navigation.tsx::SideNavigation
Props:
ariaLabel?: string = 'Primary'

className?: string

/**
 * Icon-only rail (§ collapse-to-icons).
 * 
 * Controlled, because the collapsed width has to agree with whatever
 * layout the page is running — a rail that collapsed itself would leave a
 * `lg:w-64` grid column holding a 64px rail. Pair with
 * `onCollapsedChange`.
 * 
 * Collapsing HIDES sub-items rather than shrinking them: there is no room
 * to show hierarchy at 64px, and a tree with its indentation removed reads
 * as a flat list of unrelated things. Activating a group while collapsed
 * expands the rail first.
 */
collapsed?: boolean = false

colorScheme?: 'primary' | 'secondary' = 'primary'

currentPath?: string

/**
 * Initializes every group with subItems already expanded, instead of collapsed. Default false (today's behavior, unchanged).
 */
defaultOpenAll?: boolean = false

/**
 * Content pinned above the nav list — a team switcher, a logo, a search box.
 * 
 * The rail had no way to carry any of these, so every app that wanted one
 * hand-rolled a wrapper and the divider ended up in a different place each
 * time. Rendered above the existing divider, so an app that passes nothing
 * looks exactly as it did.
 */
header?: React.ReactNode

/**
 * Hides the "Need help? / Contact support" footer box. Default false (today's behavior, unchanged).
 */
hideSupportCta?: boolean = false

items: SideNavItem[]

/**
 * Also navigates to a group header's own `path` (if set) when clicked, instead of only toggling it open/closed. Default false (today's behavior, unchanged).
 */
navigateOnGroupClick?: boolean = false

onClose?: () => void

onCollapsedChange?: (collapsed: boolean) => void

onNavigate?: (path: string) => void

onSupport?: () => void

variant?: 'dark' | 'light' = 'dark'

components-slider · ./src/components/ui/slider.stories.tsx
# Slider Radix-based `Slider`. No MDS/Figma spec exists for this component yet — built to the standard reference implementation directly, styled with `getRoleColor()` role tokens rather than hardcoded hex, following the same pattern established by Switch and Progress. Track fill uses `interactive.primary`; thumb hover/active states are tracked via local React state (same technique as `switch.tsx`) since the color can't be expressed as a Tailwind `hover:` class at build time.

const CoverageLimitAdjuster = () => {
  const [value, setValue] = useState([250000]);
  const formatted = new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', {
    style: 'currency',
    currency: 'USD',
    maximumFractionDigits: 0,
  }).format(value[0]);

  return (
    <div className="w-[360px] space-y-3">
      <div className="flex items-center justify-between">
        <span className="text-sm font-medium">Coverage limit</span>
        <span className="text-sm font-semibold">{formatted}</span>
      </div>
      <Slider value={value} onValueChange={setValue} min={50000} max={1000000} step={25000} aria-label="Coverage amount" />
      <div className="flex justify-between text-xs opacity-60">
        <span>$50,000</span>
        <span>$1,000,000</span>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
};

Sparkline

components-sparkline · ./src/components/ui/sparkline.stories.tsx
# Sparkline A tiny inline trend line for KPI tiles. It is always `aria-hidden` — the trend is carried by the delta text beside it, not the SVG, so it adds no screen-reader noise. `sentiment` picks the stroke colour from the status roles (or pass an explicit `color`). Width always fills the container; set `height` in px. A flat series draws down the middle rather than vanishing.
Prop types (react-docgen) 4 prop types

 * Explicit stroke colour, overriding `sentiment`.
 */

/**
 * The series. Fewer than two points renders nothing — a line needs two.
 */
data: number[]

/**
 * Rendered height in px. Width always fills the container.
 */
height?: number = 40

/**
 * Drives the stroke colour via the status roles.
 */

# Spinner Minimal loading indicator (lucide `Loader2` + `animate-spin`). It already carries `role="status"` and `aria-label="Loading"`, so it is announced to assistive tech. Stack

components-stack · ./src/components/ui/stack.stories.tsx
# Stack / Inline The layout atoms. `Stack` is vertical, `Inline` is horizontal and wraps. Their job is to make the spacing scale a **type**. `gap` accepts only steps that exist in `src/spacing.ts`, so `gap={7}` (28px — off-scale) is a TypeScript error instead of a silently slightly-wrong layout. That is the whole reason to prefer them over hand-writing `flex flex-col gap-6`. For two-dimensional layout, use the grid utilities in **Foundations → Grid System** instead — a Stack is one-dimensional by design.
Prop types (react-docgen) 4 prop types 
Component: src/components/ui/stack.tsx::Stack

 * Cross-axis alignment.

/**

 */
asChild?: boolean = false

/**
 * Spacing between children, on the DS scale. Off-scale values are a type error.
 */

components-statcard · ./src/components/ui/stat-card.stories.tsx
StatCard — the dashboard KPI tile.
example: ```tsx <StatCard label="Total premium" value={1250000} format="currency" formatOptions={{ compact: true }} delta={12.5} trendDescription="vs last quarter" sparkline={[8, 12, 10, 14, 16]} /> // Down is good here — fewer open claims. <StatCard label="Open claims" value={3} delta={-2} deltaFormat="number" deltaPolarity="down-is-good" /> ```
Prop types (react-docgen) 27 prop types 
Component: src/components/ui/stat-card.tsx::StatCard
Props:
/**
 * Element for `label`. Defaults to `'p'` — **a KPI label is not a section
 * heading**, and the section containing the row of tiles is. This used to be
 * a hardcoded `<h3>`, which broke heading order under a page `<h1>` and
 * forced callers to add a visually-hidden `<h2>` to compensate.
 */
as?: 'h2' | 'h3' | 'h4' | 'h5' | 'h6' | 'p' = 'p'

/**
 * Pre-formatted change string.
 * @deprecated since 0.7.0; remove after 0.8.0 / 2026-12-23.
 *  Use `delta` — it derives direction from the sign.
 */
change?: string

className?: string

/**
 * Label for a secondary comparison value, e.g. "At Renewal".
 */
comparisonLabel?: string

/**
 * Value for the secondary comparison. Formatted with the same `format`.
 */
comparisonValue?: number | string | Date | null | undefined

/**
 * Change versus the comparison period. **Direction is derived from the
 * sign** — there is no way to state a delta that disagrees with its arrow.
 * 
 * Percentage *points*, not a ratio: `delta={12.5}` renders "+12.5%",
 * matching `formatPercent`.
 */
delta?: number

/**
 * How to render `delta`. Defaults to a percentage.
 */
deltaFormat?: 'percent' | 'number' | 'currency' = 'percent'

/**
 * Which direction is good news. Defaults to up-is-good.
 */
deltaPolarity?: 'up-is-good' | 'down-is-good' | 'neutral' = 'up-is-good'

/**
 * Secondary description below trend.
 */
description?: string

emptyAction?: React.ReactNode

emptyDescription?: React.ReactNode

/**
 * Why the result is empty. `no-results` means a filter excluded everything,
 * which is a different message and a different recovery action from having
 * no data at all.
 */
emptyReason?: 'no-data' | 'no-results'

/**
 * Full override of the empty branch. The canonical name across the system.
 */
emptyState?: React.ReactNode

/**
 * Copy-only overrides, for the common case that just wants different words.
 */
emptyTitle?: React.ReactNode

errorState?: React.ReactNode

/**
 * How to render `value`. Omit for strings; pass a name or a function for numbers.
 */
format?: FormatKind | ((value: Formattable) => string)

/**
 * Per-card overrides of locale/currency/decimals.
 */
formatOptions?: CurrencyFormatOptions & DateFormatOptions

/**
 * Main label/title of the metric.
 */
label: React.ReactNode

/**
 * The fetch failed. **Not form validation** — see the note on naming below.
 * Accepts a boolean, an Error, or a node to render as the description.
 */
loadError?: React.ReactNode | Error | boolean | null

/**
 * A request is in flight. Already the repo's only spelling for this.
 */
loading?: boolean

/**
 * Full overrides of the other two branches.
 */
loadingState?: React.ReactNode

/**
 * Clears the filters that produced a `no-results` empty.
 */
onClearFilters?: () => void

/**
 * Re-run the failed load. Renders "Try again"; omitted entirely when absent.
 */
onRetry?: () => void

/**
 * Series for an inline trend line. Colour follows the delta's sentiment.
 */
sparkline?: number[]

/**
 * Explicit trend direction.
 * @deprecated since 0.7.0; remove after 0.8.0 / 2026-12-23.
 *  Use `delta` (direction is derived) with `deltaPolarity`.
 * Kept because it can contradict the number it sits beside, which is a bug
 * this component has shipped — see the note on `deltaSentiment` below.
 */
trend?: 'up' | 'down' | 'neutral'

/**
 * Trend description text, e.g. "faster than last quarter".
 */
trendDescription?: string

/**
 * The metric. **Pass a number and let the card format it** — that is the
 * point of `format`.
 * 
 * Widened from `string`, which was the root cause of this repo shipping
 * `$1,250.00`, `$12,400`, `$2.4M` and `$13.362B` side by side: the type
 * pushed formatting onto every consumer, so every consumer invented its
 * own. Strings still pass through untouched, so existing call sites are
 * unaffected.
 */
value: number | string | Date | null | undefined

Delta Polarity story ok
**Direction is derived from the delta's sign, and colour from direction × polarity.** These are different functions, and collapsing them is a bug this component shipped: a `-2 days` change with `trend="down"` rendered red beside a caption reading "faster than last quarter".

      delta={4}

    />

);

components-stepper · ./src/components/ui/stepper.stories.tsx
# Stepper `getRoleColor()`-driven counterpart to the MUI `Stepper`. Built against the real `steps: StepConfig[]` API (per-step `status`) — the `Stepper.figma.tsx` mapping's `steps: string[]` example doesn't match any prop the actual MUI component accepts. Visual language is ported from reui's Stepper ([reui.io/components/stepper](https://reui.io/components/stepper)) — 24px filled numbered indicators, 2px separators, `text-sm leading-none font-medium` titles — with their raw upstream CSS vars mapped onto this repo's role tokens. The stories below reproduce all 15 of reui's demos through this component's `indicator` / `labelPlacement` / `labelAlign` / `showSeparator` / `showStatusBadge` / `showStepEyebrow` / `completedTone` props, and are labelled with the reui demo they mirror.
Prop types (react-docgen) 14 prop types 
Component: src/components/ui/stepper.tsx::Stepper
Props:
/**
 * Index of the active step (MUI-parity API). When provided, drives each
 * step's completed/active/pending status by position — a step's own
 * explicit `status` still wins if set, so both APIs compose.
 */
activeStep?: number

className?: string

/**
 * Fill color for completed steps. reui's demos use both. Defaults to `'primary'`.
 */
completedTone?: 'primary' | 'success' = 'primary'

/**
 * How step `content` is displayed. `'inline'` (default) renders every
 * step's content under that step. `'active-only'` renders a single shared
 * panel below the step row showing just the active step's content
 * (reui's `StepperPanel`/`StepperContent` pattern), in either orientation.
 */
contentMode?: 'inline' | 'active-only' = 'inline'

/**
 * Indicator shape — see `StepIndicatorStyle`. Defaults to `'numbered'`.
 */
indicator?: | 'numbered'
/** 20px 2px-bordered circle, filled dot when active (reui demo 3). */
| 'outlined'
/** 32px circle holding the step's own `icon` (reui demo 7). */
| 'icon'
/** Full-width progress bar segment instead of a circle (reui demos 11/12). */
| 'bar' = 'numbered'

/**
 * Label alignment for `labelPlacement="below"`. Defaults to `'center'`.
 */
labelAlign?: 'center' | 'start' = 'center'

/**
 * Label position. Defaults to `'below'` for horizontal and `'inline'` for
 * vertical — the two layouts reui's demos actually use per orientation.
 * `indicator="bar"` always stacks labels below the bar.
 */
labelPlacement?: | 'none'
/** Beside the indicator (reui demos 9/10/13/15). */
| 'inline'
/** Stacked under the indicator (reui demos 5/6/8/11). */
| 'below'

onStepClick?: (stepIndex: number) => void

orientation?: 'vertical' | 'horizontal' = 'vertical'

/**
 * Draws the connector between steps. On by default; reui demos 6/11/12 turn it off.
 */
showSeparator?: boolean = true

/**
 * Renders a status pill per step (reui demo 7's In Progress/Completed/Pending). Off by default.
 */
showStatusBadge?: boolean = false

/**
 * Renders a small uppercase "STEP N" eyebrow above the title (reui demo 7). Off by default.
 */
showStepEyebrow?: boolean = false

steps: StepConfig[]

variant?: 'default' | 'compact' = 'default'

# Switch Radix-based counterpart to the MUI `DSSwitch`, styled with `getRoleColor()` role tokens rather than hardcoded hex, following the same pattern established by Checkbox, Radio, and now Switch. ## API parity with MUI `label`, `tone`, `labelPlacement`, `disabled` all match the MUI twin. `checked`/`onCheckedChange` replace MUI's `checked`/`onChange` (Radix's boolean-first convention, same divergence already established by Checkbox).

/**
 * Class name applied to the option wrapper.
 */
className?: string

/**
 * Class name applied to the Radix switch root.
 */
controlClassName?: string

/**
 * Disables the switch and its label.
 */
disabled?: boolean = false

/**
 * Unique id for the switch control; generated automatically when omitted.
 */
id?: string

/**
 * Visible label content rendered next to the switch.
 */
label?: React.ReactNode

/**
 * Class name applied to the label element.
 */
labelClassName?: string

/**
 * Label position relative to the switch.
 */
labelPlacement?: 'end' | 'start' = 'end'

/**
 * Tone: danger applies red styling for destructive toggles.
 */
tone?: 'default' | 'danger' = 'default'

# Table Radix-free, `getRoleColor()`-driven counterpart to the MUI `Table`. Covers the core feature set — columns, sorting, row selection, loading skeletons, pagination (via the `Pagination`) — matching the MUI twin's API for those props. The more exotic scroll-shadow / sticky-first-column polish from the MUI version isn't ported in this first pass.

defaultSortDirection?: 'asc' | 'desc' | null = null

/**
 * @deprecated since 0.7.0; remove after 0.8.0 / 2026-12-23.
 *  Use `emptyState`, which takes a ReactNode and is the name
 * every other data surface uses. Still honoured: passing a string here is
 * equivalent to `emptyState={<string>}`.
 */

 */

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
import { Button } from './button';
import { Toaster, showSnackbar } from './toaster';
import { toast } from './use-toast';

/**
 * # Toast
 *
 * Radix `Toast` is a queue/viewport system — call `toast()` from anywhere
 * and it stacks into a shared `<Toaster />`, each with its own auto-dismiss
 * timer and swipe-to-dismiss. That's a materially better architecture than
 * MUI's `Snackbar`, which is one controlled instance per call site (no
 * stacking, `open` state managed manually everywhere it's used).
 *
 * `showSnackbar()` is a convenience wrapper matching MUI's
 * `message`/`severity`/`actionText`/`onAction`/`autoHideDuration` shape, for
 * teams migrating from `DSSnackbar` — but it still fires into the same
 * shared queue underneath.
 *
 * `<Toaster />` should be mounted once near your app root; each story below
 * mounts its own copy since Storybook stories are isolated.
 */
const meta: Meta = {
  title: 'Components/Toast',
  tags: ['autodocs'],
  parameters: {
    layout: 'centered',
  },
};

export default meta;

export const Composable: StoryObj = {
  render: () => (
    <>
      <button
        className="rounded border px-3 py-1.5 text-sm"
        onClick={() =>
          toast({
            title: 'Scheduled: Catch up',
            description: 'Friday, February 10 at 5:57 PM',
          })
        }
      >
        Show toast
      </button>
      <Toaster />
    </>
  ),
};

export const Tones: StoryObj = {
  render: () => (
    <>
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => toast({ tone: 'default', description: 'Default toast' })}>
          Default
        </Button>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => toast({ tone: 'success', description: 'Saved successfully' })}>
          Success
        </Button>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => toast({ tone: 'warning', description: 'Storage almost full' })}>
          Warning
        </Button>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => toast({ tone: 'danger', description: 'Failed to save changes' })}>
          Danger
        </Button>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => toast({ tone: 'info', description: 'A new version is available' })}>
          Info
        </Button>
      </div>
      <Toaster />
    </>
  ),
};

/**
 * The full Figma Toast anatomy — leading status icon + bold title + body +
 * a muted timestamp, with the tone's accent on the icon and the left bar.
 * `timestamp` is opt-in: toasts without it render exactly as before.
 */

  render: () => (
    <>
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
        <Button
          variant="outline"
          size="sm"
          onClick={() =>
            toast({
              tone: 'success',
              title: 'Policy saved',
              description: 'Your changes are live for all reviewers.',
              timestamp: 'May 12, 2025',
            })
          }
        >
          Success
        </Button>
        <Button
          variant="outline"
          size="sm"
          onClick={() =>
            toast({
              tone: 'warning',
              title: 'Storage almost full',
              description: 'You are using 92% of your available space.',
              timestamp: 'May 12, 2025',
            })
          }
        >
          Warning
        </Button>
      </div>
      <Toaster />
    </>
  ),
};

      <button
        className="rounded border px-3 py-1.5 text-sm"

import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
import { LiveProvider, LivePreview, LiveError } from 'react-live';
import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';

const meta: Meta = { title: 'Generated/Voice Canvas' };
export default meta;

// Design system components set by .storybook/preview.tsx via:
//   window.__STORY_UI_DESIGN_SYSTEM__ = YourDesignSystemModule;
// Works with any React component library (Mantine, Chakra, MUI, shadcn, etc.)
const designSystem = window.__STORY_UI_DESIGN_SYSTEM__ || {};

// Module-level scope — created once, never recreated, so react-live
// does not re-transpile on every parent re-render.
const scope = {
  React,
  useState: React.useState,
  useEffect: React.useEffect,
  useCallback: React.useCallback,
  useMemo: React.useMemo,
  useRef: React.useRef,
  useReducer: React.useReducer,
  useContext: React.useContext,
  ...designSystem,
};

// Optional themed provider set in preview.tsx via:
//   window.__STORY_UI_CANVAS_PROVIDER__ = ({ children }) => <Provider>{children}</Provider>;
// Falls back to a passthrough if not configured.
const CanvasProvider: React.ComponentType<{ children: React.ReactNode }> =
  window.__STORY_UI_CANVAS_PROVIDER__ ||
  (({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) => React.createElement(React.Fragment, null, children));

// The placeholder used a hardcoded #868e96, which is 3.32:1 on white — under
// AA, and not an MDS token either. var(--role-fg-neutral-subtle) is published by
// RoleVarsProvider (mounted in .storybook/preview.tsx), so it resolves inside
// the react-live preview and follows the theme.
const PLACEHOLDER = `const Canvas = () => (
  <div style={{ padding: '24px', textAlign: 'center', color: 'var(--role-fg-neutral-subtle)' }}>
    Voice Canvas is ready — describe what you want to build
  </div>
);
render(<Canvas />);`;

export const Default: StoryObj = {
  render: () => {
    // Read from localStorage on mount for the initial code delivery.
    // The parent panel writes code to localStorage just before mounting
    // the iframe, since postMessage can't work until our listener is ready.
    const [code, setCode] = useState(() => {
      try {
        const saved = localStorage.getItem('__voice_canvas_code__');
        if (saved && saved.trim()) return saved;
      } catch {}
      return PLACEHOLDER;
    });

    useEffect(() => {
      const handler = (e: MessageEvent) => {
        if (e.origin !== window.location.origin) return;
        if (e.data?.type === 'VOICE_CANVAS_UPDATE' && typeof e.data.code === 'string') {
          setCode(e.data.code);
        }
      };
      window.addEventListener('message', handler);
      return () => window.removeEventListener('message', handler);
    }, []);

    return (
      <CanvasProvider>
        <LiveProvider code={code} scope={scope} noInline>
          <LivePreview />
          <LiveError style={{ color: 'red', fontFamily: 'monospace', fontSize: '12px', padding: '8px', whiteSpace: 'pre-wrap' }} />
        </LiveProvider>
      </CanvasProvider>
    );
  },
};

const Default = () => {
  // Read from localStorage on mount for the initial code delivery.
  // The parent panel writes code to localStorage just before mounting
  // the iframe, since postMessage can't work until our listener is ready.
  const [code, setCode] = useState(() => {
    try {
      const saved = localStorage.getItem('__voice_canvas_code__');
      if (saved && saved.trim()) return saved;
    } catch {}
    return PLACEHOLDER;
  });

  useEffect(() => {
    const handler = (e: MessageEvent) => {
      if (e.origin !== window.location.origin) return;
      if (e.data?.type === 'VOICE_CANVAS_UPDATE' && typeof e.data.code === 'string') {
        setCode(e.data.code);
      }
    };
    window.addEventListener('message', handler);
    return () => window.removeEventListener('message', handler);
  }, []);

  return (
    <CanvasProvider>
      <LiveProvider code={code} scope={scope} noInline>
        <LivePreview />
        <LiveError style={{ color: 'red', fontFamily: 'monospace', fontSize: '12px', padding: '8px', whiteSpace: 'pre-wrap' }} />

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
import type { CSSProperties } from 'react';
import { StatCard } from '../../components/ui/stat-card';
import { Bubble, BubbleContent } from '../../components/ui/bubble';
import { Marker } from '../../components/ui/marker';

/**
 * # Border Contrast — health check
 *
 * The shared `--border` CSS variable (src/index.css) fails WCAG
 * non-text contrast (3:1) in BOTH modes: 1.40:1 light (#dadada on white),
 * 1.84:1 dark (#404040 on #101010). It's the default border color for the whole primitive layer — at least 6 real components reference it
 * directly (StatCard, Bubble, Marker, Drawer, MessageScroller,
 * Questionnaire), likely more implicitly.
 *
 * MDS's own `border.default` role already resolves to a working value —
 * `neutral500` / `#878787`, deliberately used **unchanged in both modes**
 * (marked `// pivot — unchanged` in semantic-tokens.ts: 3.59:1 light,
 * 5.30:1 dark). `--input`'s own code comment even says `MDS: border.default`
 * already — it was just never actually set to that role's real value. This
 * page renders real components side by side: **current** (broken) vs
 * **proposed** (border.default's real value) — same HSL both modes, not two
 * different ones. The proposed zones override `--border` locally via inline
 * style — nothing in index.css is touched by this story.
 */
const meta: Meta = {
  title: 'Health/Border Contrast',
  parameters: {
    layout: 'fullscreen',
    a11y: {
      config: {
        rules: [
        {
          // The scrollable element axe flags here is <body> itself: this
          // story renders a tall, entirely static block, so the Storybook
          // canvas scrolls while containing nothing focusable. That's a
          // property of previewing one section in isolation, not of the
          // component — on the real page it sits among headers, links and
          // buttons, and the body scroll is reachable by keyboard through
          // them. Scoped to this story only, so the rule still guards
          // genuinely scrollable containers elsewhere (it caught real bugs
          // in CarouselSection, ExpertiseCards, ScrollArea and Attachment).
          id: 'scrollable-region-focusable',
          enabled: false,
        },
        {
          // This page renders light and dark side by side for comparison, which
          // the token architecture cannot actually support: getRoleColor()
          // resolves against a `dark` class on <html>, so components inside a
          // LOCAL `.dark` wrapper still receive light-mode values. The dark
          // zone therefore shows the correct borders (the thing being compared,
          // set explicitly) on an approximated background, and axe reads the
          // mismatch as a contrast failure — #000f47 on #0f0f0f.
          //
          // That's a real limitation worth knowing, not a defect in any
          // component: a genuine dark-mode preview needs the story's
          // `globals: { colorMode: 'dark' }`, which switches the whole canvas
          // and so can't produce a side-by-side. Scoped to this health page
          // only; the rule still guards every real component.
          id: 'color-contrast',
          enabled: false,
        },
        ],
      },
    },
  },
};
export default meta;
type Story = StoryObj;

const zoneBase: CSSProperties = { padding: 24, minHeight: 320 };

function Swatch({ label, extraClass = '' }: { label: string; extraClass?: string }) {
  return (
    <div className={`rounded border border-border bg-background p-4 text-sm text-foreground ${extraClass}`}>
      {label}
    </div>
  );
}

function ComponentSet() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
      <StatCard label="Total Revenue" value="$1,250.00" change="+12.5%" trend="up" trendDescription="Trending up this month" description="Visitors for the last 6 months" />

      <Bubble variant="outline" align="start">
        <BubbleContent>Outline bubble — border-border on bubble-content</BubbleContent>
      </Bubble>

      <div className="rounded-md border border-border bg-background p-4">
        <Marker variant="border">Marker — variant=&quot;border&quot; (border-b border-border)</Marker>
      </div>

      <div className="rounded-md border border-border bg-background p-4">
        <Marker variant="separator">before/after separator</Marker>
      </div>

      {/* Drawer/MessageScroller/Questionnaire aren't easily mountable
          standalone (portal + open-state, scroll container, form context
          respectively) — swatches below use their exact class combination
          instead, so the border weight shown is authentic even though the
          full component isn't mounted. */}
      <Swatch label="Questionnaire choice pill (border border-border)" />
      <div className="flex h-14 w-14 items-center justify-center rounded-full border border-border bg-background text-foreground shadow-md">
        ↓
      </div>
      <div className="rounded-t-xl border-t border-border bg-background p-4 text-sm text-foreground">
        Drawer content edge (border-border)
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

export const Comparison: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <div className="grid grid-cols-1 gap-px bg-neutral-300 md:grid-cols-2">
      {/* LIGHT — current */}
      <div style={zoneBase} className="bg-white">
        <p className="mb-4 font-mono text-xs uppercase tracking-wide text-neutral-500">
          Light · current (--border: 0 0% 85% · #dadada · 1.40:1)
        </p>
        <ComponentSet />
      </div>

      {/* LIGHT — proposed: neutral500 (#878787), the SAME value border.default
          already uses successfully in both modes ("pivot — unchanged" in
          semantic-tokens.ts) — not a new color choice. */}
      <div style={{ ...zoneBase, ['--border' as string]: '0 0% 53%' }} className="bg-white">
        <p className="mb-4 font-mono text-xs uppercase tracking-wide text-neutral-500">
          Light · proposed (--border: 0 0% 53% · neutral500 · #878787 · 3.59:1)
        </p>
        <ComponentSet />
      </div>

      {/* DARK — current */}
      <div style={zoneBase} className="dark bg-[#101010]">
        <p className="mb-4 font-mono text-xs uppercase tracking-wide text-neutral-400">
          Dark · current (--border: 0 0% 25% · #404040 · 1.84:1)
        </p>
        <ComponentSet />
      </div>

      {/* DARK — proposed: same neutral500 value as light, not a separate
          dark-mode step — border.default's own design already proved a
          single value works in both directions (3.59:1 light, 5.30:1 dark). */}
      <div style={{ ...zoneBase, ['--border' as string]: '0 0% 53%' }} className="dark bg-[#101010]">
        <p className="mb-4 font-mono text-xs uppercase tracking-wide text-neutral-400">
          Dark · proposed (--border: 0 0% 53% · neutral500, same value · #878787 · 5.30:1)
        </p>
        <ComponentSet />
      </div>
    </div>
  ),
};

        Dark · current (--border: 0 0% 25% · #404040 · 1.84:1)
      </p>
      <ComponentSet />
    </div>

    {/* DARK — proposed: same neutral500 value as light, not a separate
        dark-mode step — border.default's own design already proved a
        single value works in both directions (3.59:1 light, 5.30:1 dark). */}
    <div style={{ ...zoneBase, ['--border' as string]: '0 0% 53%' }} className="dark bg-[#101010]">
      <p className="mb-4 font-mono text-xs uppercase tracking-wide text-neutral-400">
        Dark · proposed (--border: 0 0% 53% · neutral500, same value · #878787 · 5.30:1)

);

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
import { Area, AreaChart, Bar, BarChart, CartesianGrid, Cell, Line, LineChart, Pie, PieChart, XAxis, YAxis } from 'recharts';
import { getRoleColor } from '@/theme/roles';
import { ChartContainer, ChartLegend, ChartLegendContent, ChartTooltip, ChartTooltipContent, type ChartConfig } from './chart';

/**
 * # Chart
 *
 * No MDS/Figma spec exists for this component — built directly on
 * Recharts with a `ChartConfig` wrapper, following this repo's
 * `dataviz` skill. Series default to `--chart-1`..`--chart-5` — five brand
 * hues (green, blue, gold, purple, red) validated for CVD-safe adjacency in
 * both light and dark mode via `node scripts/validate_palette.js`. That
 * order is load-bearing — don't reassign it.
 *
 * Every example ships a tooltip + legend by default (identity is never
 * color-alone) and uses recessive grid/axis lines.
 */
const meta: Meta = {
  title: 'Components/Chart',
  tags: ['autodocs'],
  parameters: {
    layout: 'padded',
  },
};

export default meta;

const premiumByMonth = [
  { month: 'Jan', property: 4200, liability: 2800 },
  { month: 'Feb', property: 3800, liability: 3100 },
  { month: 'Mar', property: 5100, liability: 2600 },
  { month: 'Apr', property: 4700, liability: 3400 },
  { month: 'May', property: 5600, liability: 3900 },
  { month: 'Jun', property: 6100, liability: 4200 },
];

const twoSeriesConfig: ChartConfig = {
  property: { label: 'Property' },
  liability: { label: 'Liability' },
};

export const LineChartExample: StoryObj = {
  render: () => (
    <ChartContainer config={twoSeriesConfig} className="h-[300px] w-full max-w-2xl">
      <LineChart data={premiumByMonth}>
        <CartesianGrid strokeDasharray="3 3" stroke={getRoleColor('border.default')} vertical={false} />
        <XAxis dataKey="month" stroke={getRoleColor('fg.neutral.subtle')} tickLine={false} axisLine={false} />
        <YAxis stroke={getRoleColor('fg.neutral.subtle')} tickLine={false} axisLine={false} />
        <ChartTooltip content={<ChartTooltipContent />} />
        <ChartLegend content={<ChartLegendContent />} />
        <Line type="monotone" dataKey="property" stroke="var(--color-property)" strokeWidth={2} dot={{ r: 4 }} />
        <Line type="monotone" dataKey="liability" stroke="var(--color-liability)" strokeWidth={2} dot={{ r: 4 }} />
      </LineChart>
    </ChartContainer>
  ),
};

export const BarChartExample: StoryObj = {

        <XAxis dataKey="month" stroke={getRoleColor('fg.neutral.subtle')} tickLine={false} axisLine={false} />

        <Bar dataKey="liability" fill="var(--color-liability)" radius={[4, 4, 0, 0]} />
      </BarChart>

export const AreaChartExample: StoryObj = {

import * as React from 'react';
import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
import { expect, screen, userEvent, waitFor, within } from 'storybook/test';

import { FilterBoolean, FilterNumberRange } from './filter-controls';
import { FilterChipMenu, FilterChipSet } from './filter-chip';
import { Badge } from './badge';
import { Button } from './button';
import { DataTable } from './data-table';
import { Stack } from './stack';
import { collectApplied, type FilterField } from './filter-schema';
import { formatCurrency } from '@/lib/format';
import type { DataGridColumnDef } from './data-grid-features';

const meta: Meta = {
  title: 'Components/Filter controls',
  tags: ['autodocs'],
  parameters: {
    layout: 'padded',
    docs: {
      description: {
        component: [
          'The two filter controls the system was missing: **number range** and **boolean**.',
          '',
          '`inNumberRange` had been registered on the grid the whole time with no UI able to',
          'produce a value for it, and every product that needed a yes/no filter invented its own',
          'two-option select.',
          '',
          'Both are driven by a [`FilterField`](/docs/foundations-choosing-a-table--docs) from the',
          'filter schema, so the control, the chip label and the row matcher cannot disagree.',
        ].join('\n'),
      },
    },
  },
};
export default meta;

interface Policy {
  id: number;
  name: string;
  status: string;
  premium: number;
  bound: boolean;
}

const policies: Policy[] = [
  { id: 1, name: 'Commercial Auto', status: 'Active', premium: 12400, bound: true },
  { id: 2, name: 'General Liability', status: 'Active', premium: 8200, bound: true },
  { id: 3, name: 'Cyber Liability', status: 'Pending', premium: 15900, bound: false },
  { id: 4, name: 'Property', status: 'Active', premium: 22000, bound: true },
  { id: 5, name: 'Workers Comp', status: 'Expired', premium: 9600, bound: false },
  { id: 6, name: 'Marine Cargo', status: 'Pending', premium: 4100, bound: false },
];

const FIELDS: FilterField[] = [
  {
    id: 'status',
    label: 'Status',
    type: 'multi',
    options: [
      { value: 'Active', label: 'Active', count: 3 },
      { value: 'Pending', label: 'Pending', count: 2 },
      { value: 'Expired', label: 'Expired', count: 1 },
    ],
  },
  { id: 'premium', label: 'Premium', type: 'numberRange', unit: 'currency' },
  { id: 'bound', label: 'Bound', type: 'boolean', trueLabel: 'Bound', falseLabel: 'Unbound' },
];

const columns: DataGridColumnDef<Policy>[] = [
  { accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Policy' },
  {
    accessorKey: 'status',
    header: 'Status',
    cell: ({ getValue }) => {
      const v = getValue<string>();
      return (
        <Badge tone={v === 'Active' ? 'success' : v === 'Expired' ? 'danger' : 'warning'} size="sm">
          {v}
        </Badge>
      );
    },
  },
  {
    accessorKey: 'premium',
    header: 'Premium',
    meta: { type: 'currency' },
    // decimals: 0 — whole premiums, so a column of ".00" is noise in a
    // scan-heavy table. Precision stays available where it matters (§48).
    cell: ({ getValue }) => formatCurrency(getValue<number>(), { decimals: 0 }),
  },
  {
    accessorKey: 'bound',
    header: 'Bound',
    meta: { type: 'boolean' },
    cell: ({ getValue }) => (getValue<boolean>() ? 'Yes' : 'No'),
  },
];

export const NumberRange: StoryObj = {
  render: function Render() {
    const [value, setValue] = React.useState<{ min?: number; max?: number } | undefined>();
    return (
      <Stack gap={3}>
        <FilterNumberRange
          field={FIELDS[1] as Extract<FilterField, { type: 'numberRange' }>}
          value={value}
          onValueChange={setValue}
        />
        <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground" data-testid="value">
          {value ? JSON.stringify(value) : 'No range applied'}
        </p>
      </Stack>
    );
  },
  play: async ({ canvasElement, step }) => {
    const canvas = within(canvasElement);
    await step('the unit is in the label, not only a placeholder', async () => {
      await userEvent.click(canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Premium' }));
      // `screen`, not `canvas`: the popover is portalled to document.body, so
      // it is outside canvasElement entirely. A placeholder would also
      // disappear the moment the user types, taking the only statement of
      // what the number means with it — hence a real label.
      await expect(await screen.findByLabelText('Minimum Premium')).toBeInTheDocument();
    });
    await step('leave the UI at rest', async () => {
      await userEvent.keyboard('{Escape}');
      await waitFor(() => expect(screen.queryByLabelText('Minimum Premium')).toBeNull());
    });
  },
};

export const Boolean_: StoryObj = {
  name: 'Boolean (tri-state)',
  render: function Render() {
    const [value, setValue] = React.useState<boolean | undefined>();
    return (
      <Stack gap={3}>
        <FilterBoolean
          field={FIELDS[2] as Extract<FilterField, { type: 'boolean' }>}
          value={value}
          onValueChange={setValue}
        />
        <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
          {value === undefined ? 'Any' : value ? 'Bound only' : 'Unbound only'}
        </p>
        <p className="max-w-prose text-sm text-muted-foreground">
          Three states, not two. A toggle that only turns <em>on</em> cannot ask for the
          rows where the value is <code>false</code> — and “show unbound policies” is a
          real question. <code>undefined</code> is not the same as <code>false</code>.
        </p>
      </Stack>
    );
  },
};

/**
 * **The whole filter row, driving a real table.**
 *
 * One `FilterField[]` produces the controls, the applied-filter summary and the
 * row matching — so the chip that says “Premium: over $10,000” and the rows you
 * are looking at cannot disagree.
 *
 * Note the summary line: chips tell you *what* is filtered, a count tells you
 * whether it did anything.
 */
export const WithATable: StoryObj = {
  render: function Render() {
    const [values, setValues] = React.useState<Record<string, unknown>>({});
    const set = (id: string, v: unknown) => setValues((prev) => ({ ...prev, [id]: v }));

    const applied = collectApplied(FIELDS, values);

    const rows = policies.filter((p) => {
      const status = values.status as string[] | undefined;
      if (status?.length && !status.includes(p.status)) return false;
      const premium = values.premium as { min?: number; max?: number } | undefined;
      if (premium?.min !== undefined && p.premium < premium.min) return false;
      if (premium?.max !== undefined && p.premium > premium.max) return false;
      if (values.bound !== undefined && p.bound !== values.bound) return false;
      return true;
    });

    return (
      <Stack gap={4}>
        <FilterChipSet label="Filter policies">
          <FilterChipMenu
            label="Status"
            value={(values.status as string[]) ?? []}
            onValueChange={(v) => set('status', v)}
            options={(FIELDS[0] as Extract<FilterField, { type: 'multi' }>).options}
          />
          <FilterNumberRange
            field={FIELDS[1] as Extract<FilterField, { type: 'numberRange' }>}
            value={values.premium as { min?: number; max?: number } | undefined}
            onValueChange={(v) => set('premium', v)}
          />
          <FilterBoolean
            field={FIELDS[2] as Extract<FilterField, { type: 'boolean' }>}
            value={values.bound as boolean | undefined}
            onValueChange={(v) => set('bound', v)}
          />
        </FilterChipSet>

        <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3 text-sm">
          <span data-testid="summary">
            {applied.length === 0 ? (
              <>Showing all <strong>{policies.length}</strong> policies</>
            ) : (
              <>
                <strong>{rows.length}</strong> of {policies.length} policies —{' '}
                {applied.map((a) => `${a.field.label}: ${a.description}`).join(' · ')}
              </>
            )}
          </span>
          {applied.length > 0 && (
            <Button variant="tertiary" size="sm" onClick={() => setValues({})}>
              Clear all
            </Button>
          )}
        </div>

        <DataTable columns={columns} data={rows} pageSize={6} pinFirstColumn={false} />
      </Stack>
    );
  },
  play: async ({ canvasElement, step }) => {
    const canvas = within(canvasElement);
    await step('the summary counts, it does not only list', async () => {
      await expect(canvas.getByTestId('summary')).toHaveTextContent('Showing all 6 policies');
    });
    await step('a boolean filter can ask for the FALSE rows', async () => {
      const { screen } = await import('storybook/test');
      // Scoped: the table's own "Bound" column header is a button too.
      const bar = canvas.getByRole('toolbar', { name: 'Filter policies' });
      await userEvent.click(within(bar).getByRole('button', { name: 'Bound' }));
      await userEvent.click(await screen.findByRole('menuitemradio', { name: 'Unbound' }));
      await expect(canvas.getByTestId('summary')).toHaveTextContent('3 of 6 policies');
      await expect(canvas.getByTestId('summary')).toHaveTextContent('Bound: Unbound');
    });
    await step('leave the UI at rest', async () => {
      // axe runs after the play function. While a Radix menu is open it marks
      // the rest of the page aria-hidden, and hidden content containing
      // focusable buttons is an aria-hidden-focus violation — a true
      // statement about a transient state, not a defect in the page. Waiting
      // for the overlay to clear is the play function's job.
      await waitFor(() =>
        expect(canvas.getByRole('toolbar', { name: 'Filter policies' })).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden')
      );
    });
  },
};

With A Table story ok
**The whole filter row, driving a real table.** One `FilterField[]` produces the controls, the applied-filter summary and the row matching — so the chip that says “Premium: over $10,000” and the rows you are looking at cannot disagree. Note the summary line: chips tell you *what* is filtered, a count tells you whether it did anything.
const WithATable = function Render() {
  const [values, setValues] = React.useState<Record<string, unknown>>({});
  const set = (id: string, v: unknown) => setValues((prev) => ({ ...prev, [id]: v }));

  const applied = collectApplied(FIELDS, values);

  const rows = policies.filter((p) => {
    const status = values.status as string[] | undefined;
    if (status?.length && !status.includes(p.status)) return false;
    const premium = values.premium as { min?: number; max?: number } | undefined;
    if (premium?.min !== undefined && p.premium < premium.min) return false;
    if (premium?.max !== undefined && p.premium > premium.max) return false;
    if (values.bound !== undefined && p.bound !== values.bound) return false;
    return true;
  });

  return (
    <Stack gap={4}>
      <FilterChipSet label="Filter policies">
        <FilterChipMenu
          label="Status"
          value={(values.status as string[]) ?? []}
          onValueChange={(v) => set('status', v)}
          options={(FIELDS[0] as Extract<FilterField, { type: 'multi' }>).options}
        />
        <FilterNumberRange
          field={FIELDS[1] as Extract<FilterField, { type: 'numberRange' }>}
          value={values.premium as { min?: number; max?: number } | undefined}
          onValueChange={(v) => set('premium', v)}
        />
        <FilterBoolean
          field={FIELDS[2] as Extract<FilterField, { type: 'boolean' }>}
          value={values.bound as boolean | undefined}
          onValueChange={(v) => set('bound', v)}
        />
      </FilterChipSet>

      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3 text-sm">
        <span data-testid="summary">
          {applied.length === 0 ? (
            <>Showing all <strong>{policies.length}</strong> policies</>
          ) : (
            <>
              <strong>{rows.length}</strong> of {policies.length} policies —{' '}
              {applied.map((a) => `${a.field.label}: ${a.description}`).join(' · ')}
            </>
          )}
        </span>
        {applied.length > 0 && (
          <Button variant="tertiary" size="sm" onClick={() => setValues({})}>
            Clear all
          </Button>
        )}
      </div>

      <DataTable columns={columns} data={rows} pageSize={6} pinFirstColumn={false} />
    </Stack>
  );
};

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
import * as React from 'react';

import { Input } from './input';
import { Textarea } from './textarea';
import { DSSelect } from './select';
import { Combobox } from './combobox';
import { DatePicker } from './date-picker';
import { Button } from './button';
import { ButtonGroup } from './button-group';
import { DSCheckbox } from './checkbox';
import { Switch } from './switch';
import { Stack, Inline } from './stack';

/**
 * # Form Controls
 *
 * Every text-entry control in the system, side by side, at every size.
 *
 * This page exists to make inconsistency *visible*. A design system's form
 * controls have one hard requirement that is easy to break and hard to spot
 * one component at a time: **a control and a button of the same declared size
 * must be the same height**, because they constantly sit next to each other
 * in a row. Nothing enforces that automatically, so it is checked here by eye
 * and by the rendered measurement under each control.
 */
const meta: Meta = {
  title: 'Components/Form Controls',
  tags: ['autodocs'],
  parameters: {
    layout: 'padded',
    docs: {
      description: {
        component:
          'All text-entry controls at every size, with measured heights, so cross-component inconsistency is visible rather than something you discover in a layout.',
      },
    },
  },
};

export default meta;
type Story = StoryObj;

const SELECT_OPTIONS = [
  { value: 'property', label: 'Property' },
  { value: 'liability', label: 'Liability' },
  { value: 'cyber', label: 'Cyber' },
];

const COMBOBOX_OPTIONS = [
  { value: 'beacon', label: 'Beacon Capital' },
  { value: 'northwind', label: 'Northwind Logistics' },
];

/** Measures and labels its child's rendered height, so claims are checkable. */
function Measured({ label, children }: { label: string; children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const ref = React.useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const [h, setH] = React.useState<number | null>(null);

  React.useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const el = ref.current?.firstElementChild;
    if (!el) return;
    // The control itself, not the wrapper — a wrapper may include a label.
    const target = el.querySelector('input,textarea,button,[role=combobox]') ?? el;
    setH(Math.round(target.getBoundingClientRect().height));
  }, []);

  return (
    <Stack gap={1}>
      <span className="text-xs font-medium text-muted-foreground">
        {label}
        {h !== null && <span className="ml-2 font-mono">{h}px</span>}
      </span>
      <div ref={ref}>{children}</div>
    </Stack>
  );
}

const SIZES = ['sm', 'md', 'lg'] as const;

/**
 * The core check: each control beside a Button of the same declared size.
 * Any height mismatch shows immediately as a step in the row.
 */
export const AgainstButton: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <Stack gap={8}>
      {SIZES.map((size) => (
        <Stack key={size} gap={3}>
          <h3 className="text-sm font-semibold">
            size=&quot;{size}&quot;
          </h3>
          <Inline gap={3} align="end" wrap={false} className="overflow-x-auto pb-2">
            <Measured label="Input">
              <Input size={size} placeholder="Policy number" aria-label="Policy number" />
            </Measured>
            <Measured label="Select">
              <DSSelect options={SELECT_OPTIONS} size={size} placeholder="Coverage" aria-label="Coverage type" />
            </Measured>
            <Measured label="Button">
              <Button size={size} variant="primary">
                Search
              </Button>
            </Measured>
          </Inline>
        </Stack>
      ))}
    </Stack>
  ),
};

/** Every text-entry control at every size, to compare padding and type scale. */
export const AllControls: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <Stack gap={8}>
      {SIZES.map((size) => (
        <Stack key={size} gap={3}>
          <h3 className="text-sm font-semibold">size=&quot;{size}&quot;</h3>
          <div className="grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3">
            <Measured label="Input">
              <Input size={size} placeholder="Policy number" aria-label="Policy number" />
            </Measured>
            <Measured label="Select">
              <DSSelect options={SELECT_OPTIONS} size={size} placeholder="Coverage" aria-label="Coverage type" />
            </Measured>
            <Measured label="Combobox">
              <Combobox options={COMBOBOX_OPTIONS} size={size} placeholder="Client" aria-label="Client" />
            </Measured>
            <Measured label="DatePicker">
              <DatePicker size={size} placeholder="Effective date" />
            </Measured>
            <Measured label="Textarea">
              <Textarea size={size} placeholder="Loss description" rows={2} aria-label="Loss description" />
            </Measured>
          </div>
        </Stack>
      ))}
    </Stack>
  ),
};

/**
 * Grouped controls. `ButtonGroup` and `InputGroup` take a `size` and cascade
 * it through context, so every child matches without the author repeating it
 * — and a group with a mismatched child is not expressible by accident.
 *
 * This is where a height mismatch is unmissable, because the controls share
 * edges: before the shared scale, a 40px Input beside a 48px Button left a
 * visible step in something meant to read as one unit. `items-stretch` could
 * not save it, since both children set explicit heights.
 */
export const GroupedControls: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <Stack gap={8}>
      {SIZES.map((size) => (
        <Stack key={size} gap={3}>
          <h3 className="text-sm font-semibold">
            &lt;ButtonGroup size=&quot;{size}&quot;&gt; — children inherit
          </h3>
          <ButtonGroup size={size} aria-label={`Policy search, ${size}`}>
            <Input placeholder="Policy number" aria-label="Policy number" />
            <DSSelect options={SELECT_OPTIONS} placeholder="Coverage" aria-label="Coverage type" />
            <Button variant="primary">Search</Button>
          </ButtonGroup>
        </Stack>
      ))}

      <Stack gap={1}>
        <h3 className="text-sm font-semibold">
          A child&apos;s own size still wins
        </h3>
        <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
          Deliberately mismatched, to show precedence: the group says{' '}
          <code>sm</code> and the button overrides with <code>lg</code>. This is
          the escape hatch, not a recommended pattern — a group normally reads
          as one unit.
        </p>
        <ButtonGroup size="sm" aria-label="Override example" className="mt-2">
          <Input placeholder="Inherits sm" aria-label="Inherits sm" />
          <Button variant="primary" size="lg">
            Explicit lg
          </Button>
        </ButtonGroup>
      </Stack>
    </Stack>
  ),
};

/**
 * Boolean controls sit on their own scale — they are glyphs, not text boxes,
 * so they do not take the text-control heights. Shown for completeness.
 */
export const BooleanControls: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <Inline gap={6} align="center">
      <DSCheckbox label="Include expired" />
      <Switch label="Auto-renew" />
    </Inline>
  ),
};

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';

const meta = {
  title: '_health/Grid',
  parameters: { layout: 'fullscreen' },
} satisfies Meta;

export default meta;
type Story = StoryObj;

export const GridPresent: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <div className="mds-legacy-container" style={{ padding: 8 }}>
      <div className="mds-legacy-row gap-2" data-testid="row">
        <div className="mds-legacy-col-6" style={{ background: '#eef6ff', padding: 8 }}>A</div>
        <div className="mds-legacy-col-6" style={{ background: '#eef6ff', padding: 8 }}>B</div>
      </div>
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    const row = canvasElement.querySelector('[data-testid="row"]') as HTMLElement | null;
    if (!row) throw new Error('row not found');
    const styles = getComputedStyle(row);
    if (!styles.display.includes('grid')) {
      throw new Error(`expected display:grid, got ${styles.display}`);
    }
    const template = styles.gridTemplateColumns || '';
    if (!template) {
      throw new Error('grid-template-columns is empty');
    }
  }
};

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { CircularProgress, LinearProgress } from './progress';

/**
 * # Progress
 *
 * `CircularProgress` (hand-rolled SVG — Radix has no circular primitive) and
 * `LinearProgress` (built on `@radix-ui/react-progress`), both styled with
 * `getRoleColor()` role tokens rather than hardcoded hex.
 *
 * ## API parity with MUI
 * Same `value`/`variant`/`tone` props as the MUI `DSCircularProgress` /
 * `DSLinearProgress` twins.
 */
const meta: Meta = {
  title: 'Components/Progress',
  tags: ['autodocs'],
  parameters: {
    layout: 'centered',
  },
};

export default meta;

export const CircularIndeterminate: StoryObj<typeof CircularProgress> = {
  render: (args) => <CircularProgress {...args} />,
  args: {
    variant: 'indeterminate',
  },
};

export const CircularDeterminate: StoryObj<typeof CircularProgress> = {
  render: (args) => <CircularProgress {...args} />,
  args: {
    variant: 'determinate',
    value: 65,
  },
};

    <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
      <CircularProgress variant="determinate" value={70} tone="default" />
      <CircularProgress variant="determinate" value={70} tone="success" />
      <CircularProgress variant="determinate" value={70} tone="danger" />
    </div>
  ),
};

  render: () => (
    <div className="flex items-end gap-6">
      <CircularProgress size={24} variant="determinate" value={50} />
      <CircularProgress size={40} variant="determinate" value={50} />
      <CircularProgress size={64} variant="determinate" value={50} />

        <LinearProgress variant="determinate" value={value} />
        <CircularProgress variant="determinate" value={value} />
