import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
import type { CSSProperties } from 'react';
import { ResizablePanelGroup, ResizablePanel, ResizableHandle } from './resizable';

/**
 * # Resizable
 *
 * Wraps `react-resizable-panels`. No MDS/Figma spec exists for this
 * component yet — built to the standard reference implementation
 * (`ResizablePanelGroup` / `ResizablePanel` / `ResizableHandle`), styled
 * with `getRoleColor()` role tokens rather than hardcoded hex.
 *
 * Note: the installed `react-resizable-panels` is v4, which renamed its
 * `PanelGroup`/`Panel`/`PanelResizeHandle` exports to `Group`/`Panel`/
 * `Separator` (and `direction` to `orientation`) — see the comment at the
 * top of `resizable.tsx` for details. The public component names here still
 * match the classic headless-UI recipe.
 */
const meta: Meta<typeof ResizablePanelGroup> = {
  title: 'Components/Resizable',
  tags: ['autodocs'],
  parameters: {
    layout: 'centered',
    docs: {
      description: {
        component: 'Split layout with draggable dividers, for panes users can resize to taste.',
      },
    },
    a11y: {
      config: {
        rules: [
          {
            // Upstream limitation in react-resizable-panels 4.12.2, not
            // something this wrapper can fix — see the long note on
            // ResizablePanel in resizable.tsx. Each Panel's scroll container
            // is an inner div the library exposes no props for, so it cannot
            // be made focusable. Scoped off HERE (not globally) so the rule
            // still guards every other component, and so this shows up as a
            // deliberate, explained exception rather than a silent pass.
            id: 'scrollable-region-focusable',
            enabled: false,
          },
        ],
      },
    },
  },
};

export default meta;

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
import { Button } from './button';
import { Toaster, showSnackbar } from './toaster';
import { toast } from './use-toast';

/**
 * # Toast
 *
 * Radix `Toast` is a queue/viewport system — call `toast()` from anywhere
 * and it stacks into a shared `<Toaster />`, each with its own auto-dismiss
 * timer and swipe-to-dismiss. That's a materially better architecture than
 * MUI's `Snackbar`, which is one controlled instance per call site (no
 * stacking, `open` state managed manually everywhere it's used).
 *
 * `showSnackbar()` is a convenience wrapper matching MUI's
 * `message`/`severity`/`actionText`/`onAction`/`autoHideDuration` shape, for
 * teams migrating from `DSSnackbar` — but it still fires into the same
 * shared queue underneath.
 *
 * `<Toaster />` should be mounted once near your app root; each story below
 * mounts its own copy since Storybook stories are isolated.
 */
const meta: Meta = {
  title: 'Components/Toast',
  tags: ['autodocs'],
  parameters: {
    layout: 'centered',
  },
};

export default meta;

export const Composable: StoryObj = {
  render: () => (
    <>
      <button
        className="rounded border px-3 py-1.5 text-sm"
        onClick={() =>
          toast({
            title: 'Scheduled: Catch up',
            description: 'Friday, February 10 at 5:57 PM',
          })
        }
      >
        Show toast
      </button>
      <Toaster />
    </>
  ),
};

export const Tones: StoryObj = {
  render: () => (
    <>
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => toast({ tone: 'default', description: 'Default toast' })}>
          Default
        </Button>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => toast({ tone: 'success', description: 'Saved successfully' })}>
          Success
        </Button>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => toast({ tone: 'warning', description: 'Storage almost full' })}>
          Warning
        </Button>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => toast({ tone: 'danger', description: 'Failed to save changes' })}>
          Danger
        </Button>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => toast({ tone: 'info', description: 'A new version is available' })}>
          Info
        </Button>
      </div>
      <Toaster />
    </>
  ),
};

import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
import { LiveProvider, LivePreview, LiveError } from 'react-live';
import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';

const meta: Meta = { title: 'Generated/Voice Canvas' };
export default meta;

// Design system components set by .storybook/preview.tsx via:
//   window.__STORY_UI_DESIGN_SYSTEM__ = YourDesignSystemModule;
// Works with any React component library (Mantine, Chakra, MUI, shadcn, etc.)
const designSystem = window.__STORY_UI_DESIGN_SYSTEM__ || {};

// Module-level scope — created once, never recreated, so react-live
// does not re-transpile on every parent re-render.
const scope = {
  React,
  useState: React.useState,
  useEffect: React.useEffect,
  useCallback: React.useCallback,
  useMemo: React.useMemo,
  useRef: React.useRef,
  useReducer: React.useReducer,
  useContext: React.useContext,
  ...designSystem,
};

// Optional themed provider set in preview.tsx via:
//   window.__STORY_UI_CANVAS_PROVIDER__ = ({ children }) => <Provider>{children}</Provider>;
// Falls back to a passthrough if not configured.
const CanvasProvider: React.ComponentType<{ children: React.ReactNode }> =
  window.__STORY_UI_CANVAS_PROVIDER__ ||
  (({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) => React.createElement(React.Fragment, null, children));

// The placeholder used a hardcoded #868e96, which is 3.32:1 on white — under
// AA, and not an MDS token either. var(--role-fg-neutral-subtle) is published by
// RoleVarsProvider (mounted in .storybook/preview.tsx), so it resolves inside
// the react-live preview and follows the theme.
const PLACEHOLDER = `const Canvas = () => (
  <div style={{ padding: '24px', textAlign: 'center', color: 'var(--role-fg-neutral-subtle)' }}>
    Voice Canvas is ready — describe what you want to build
  </div>
);
render(<Canvas />);`;

export const Default: StoryObj = {
  render: () => {
    // Read from localStorage on mount for the initial code delivery.
    // The parent panel writes code to localStorage just before mounting
    // the iframe, since postMessage can't work until our listener is ready.
    const [code, setCode] = useState(() => {
      try {
        const saved = localStorage.getItem('__voice_canvas_code__');
        if (saved && saved.trim()) return saved;
      } catch {}
      return PLACEHOLDER;
    });

    useEffect(() => {
      const handler = (e: MessageEvent) => {
        if (e.origin !== window.location.origin) return;
        if (e.data?.type === 'VOICE_CANVAS_UPDATE' && typeof e.data.code === 'string') {
          setCode(e.data.code);
        }
      };
      window.addEventListener('message', handler);
      return () => window.removeEventListener('message', handler);
    }, []);

    return (
      <CanvasProvider>
        <LiveProvider code={code} scope={scope} noInline>
          <LivePreview />
          <LiveError style={{ color: 'red', fontFamily: 'monospace', fontSize: '12px', padding: '8px', whiteSpace: 'pre-wrap' }} />
        </LiveProvider>
      </CanvasProvider>
    );
  },
};

# Marsh Design System Three things to know before you write any code here: 1. **Colors alw...
import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import { ContrastStatus } from './_components/ContrastStatus';

<Meta title="Foundations/Intro" />

# Marsh Design System

Three things to know before you write any code here:

1. **Colors always go through a role, never a hex value.** `getRoleColor('interactive.primary')`, not `#000f47`. This is enforced by `npm run roles:check` in CI — see [Colors](?path=/docs/foundations-colors--docs).
2. **Layout is plain Tailwind grid utilities.** `grid grid-cols-12 gap-6`, not custom CSS. There's an older, unrelated grid system still used by a handful of legacy pages — if you're building something new, you don't need it. See [Grid](?path=/docs/foundations-grid--docs).
3. **Building UI? Check for an existing component first.** Every component in the current component library — buttons, forms, dialogs, tables, everything — is browsable with live examples and "use this / not that" guidance at `/design-system` (run the app, see below). Don't build something that already exists.

## Run it

```bash
npm install
npm run dev         # the app, http://localhost:5173
npm run storybook   # this documentation, http://localhost:6006
```

## Starting a new page

1. **Check `/design-system` first.** Does what you need already exist? Does an existing component's props already cover it (a new `variant`/`tone`/`size` beats a new component)? Can you compose two or three existing ones? Only build new as a last resort.
2. **Add a route.** `src/Router.tsx` is a flat list — lazy-import your page, add one `<Route>`.
3. **Build with what's in `src/components/ui/`**, laid out with Tailwind grid, colored with roles:

```tsx
import { Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, CardContent } from '@/components/ui/card';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';
import { getRoleColor } from '@/theme/roles';

export default function HelloPage() {
  return (
    <div className="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-3 gap-6 p-6">
      <Card>
        <CardHeader>
          <CardTitle style={{ color: getRoleColor('fg.primary') }}>
            Hello
          </CardTitle>
        </CardHeader>
        <CardContent>
          <Button variant="primary">Take action</Button>
        </CardContent>
      </Card>
    </div>
  );
}
```

That's the whole pattern: components from `@/components/ui/*`, `grid`/`gap-*` for layout, `getRoleColor()` for any color that isn't already baked into the component. No `sx` prop, no CSS Modules, no hex values.

Full walkthrough, route to finish: **`docs/get-started/BUILD_YOUR_FIRST_PAGE.md`**.

## Beyond building pages

The workflow above (`components/ui/*` + roles + Tailwind grid) covers most day-to-day work. This system also does several things that aren't visible from that workflow alone — easy to miss if you only ever look at the component docs:

- **Testing** — every `.stories.tsx` file doubles as a real test, rendered in an actual Chromium browser via Playwright (`@storybook/addon-vitest`), not just a visual example — on top of the usual `jsdom` unit tests. No extra test files to write; `npm test` runs both. Full guide, including coverage and running it from Storybook's own UI: [Testing](?path=/docs/foundations-testing--docs).
- **Figma Code Connect** — real component source shown directly in Figma Dev Mode, so a designer inspecting a component in Figma sees the actual React code, not a guess. Setup and mapping files: `docs/FIGMA_CODE_CONNECT_GUIDE.md`, `src/figma/*.figma.tsx`.
- **MCP-driven Figma sync** — pulls live Figma Variables straight into an interactive session (via the Figma Desktop Bridge MCP server) and diffs them against the token values actually shipping in code — catches drift between what Figma says a color should be and what's real. Re-checkable anytime without a live Figma connection: `npm run tokens:check-figma` / `tokens:check-figma-semantic`, against the snapshots in `src/figma-variable-map.json` / `src/figma-variable-map-semantic.json`. `docs/FIGMA_PRIMITIVE_TOKEN_ASSESSMENT.md` and `docs/FIGMA_SEMANTIC_TOKEN_ASSESSMENT.md` are real worked examples of what this surfaces.
- **`agents/design-system-agent`** — a separate, unattended pipeline: point it at one Figma component node, it builds an MDS-compliant, PR-ready component headlessly — for a webhook, CI job, or scheduled sweep, not interactive use. Enforces `CLAUDE.md`'s rules structurally (per-subagent filesystem permission allowlists), not just by convention. See its own `agents/design-system-agent/README.md`.

## Where things are

- **[/design-system](http://localhost:5173/design-system)** (run `npm run dev` first) — every component in the current library, live, with guidance on which one to reach for and when. Start here for "how do I build X."
- **`docs/get-started/DEVELOPERS.md`** — the fuller written guide: project structure, conventions, how to add a new page.
- **This Storybook, `Foundations/*`** — the token, color, typography, spacing, elevation, and accessibility system in detail.
- **Root `CLAUDE.md`** — the complete rules document (written for AI coding agents, but accurate and thorough for a human reading it too).

{/*

  would be wrong within a month, and `taxonomy.test.ts` already fails if the

  manifest makes this page as current as that test.

# Composition

How the 75 component modules fit together, and which one to reach for.

## Do not build a new component

The most common failure here is not bad code — it is building the 76th thing
that already existed as a prop on the 9th. Work down this ladder and **stop at
the first step that works**:

1. **Does it exist?** Check the tiers below, or browse `/design-system`.
2. **Does a prop cover it?** A new `variant`, `tone` or `size` value is far
   cheaper than a new component. Read the component's stories before deciding
   the prop isn't there — the stories are the API documentation.
3. **Can you compose it?** `Card` + `Inline` + `Button` covers most "new"
   patterns with no new component code.
4. **Only then build one.**

## The four tiers

Classification lives in `src/components/ui/taxonomy.ts` — **not** in the folder
structure. Files stay flat in `src/components/ui/`, the way shadcn/ui, Radix,
MUI and Polaris all do it, because the atom/molecule boundary is genuinely
contested and baking a contested answer into import paths buys nothing: what
you need is to *know* that `DataTable` is an organism, not to find it at a
particular path.

<div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16, margin: '24px 0' }}>
  {Object.entries(TIERS).map(([tier, def]) => (
    <div
      key={tier}
      style={{
        border: '1px solid var(--mds-border, #dadada)',
        borderRadius: 2,
        padding: 16,
      }}
    >
      <div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'baseline', gap: 12, marginBottom: 8 }}>
        <strong style={{ fontSize: 16, textTransform: 'capitalize' }}>{tier}</strong>
        <span style={{ fontSize: 12, opacity: 0.6 }}>{byTier(tier).length} modules</span>
      </div>
      <p style={{ margin: '0 0 6px', fontSize: 14 }}>
        <strong>Test:</strong> {def.test}
      </p>
      <p style={{ margin: 0, fontSize: 14, opacity: 0.8 }}>{def.role}</p>
      <p style={{ margin: '10px 0 0', fontSize: 13, fontFamily: 'ui-monospace, monospace', opacity: 0.75 }}>
        {byTier(tier).join(' · ')}
      </p>
    </div>
  ))}
</div>

A module may export several components, and they share its tier — `stack`
exports both `Stack` and `Inline`; `page-shell` exports `PageShell` and
`PageHeading`.

**Start at molecule.** Most feature code should live there. Drop to atoms only
when you need one styled surface; reach for an organism when you need data in
and events out.

## Contested calls

These were genuinely arguable. The reasoning is recorded so nobody
relitigates them from scratch — and so that disagreeing means editing one
file, not one hundred.

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th style={{ textAlign: 'left' }}>Module</th>
      <th style={{ textAlign: 'left' }}>Tier</th>
      <th style={{ textAlign: 'left' }}>Why</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    {Object.entries(CONTESTED).map(([name, why]) => (
      <tr key={name}>
        <td style={{ fontFamily: 'ui-monospace, monospace', whiteSpace: 'nowrap', verticalAlign: 'top' }}>{name}</td>
        <td style={{ verticalAlign: 'top' }}>{TAXONOMY[name]}</td>
        <td style={{ verticalAlign: 'top' }}>{why}</td>
      </tr>
    ))}
  </tbody>
</table>

## Building a page

Start from the template — do not hand-roll the frame:

```tsx
import { PageShell, PageHeading, Stack, Button } from '@/components/ui';

<PageShell
  header={<Header sidebarOpen={open} onToggleSidebar={toggle} />}
  sidebar={<SideNavigation items={items} className="fixed inset-y-0 left-0 z-50 w-72 shrink-0 lg:static lg:z-auto lg:w-auto" />}
  sidebarOpen={open}
  onSidebarClose={close}
>
  <PageHeading title="Overview" description="Your portfolio at a glance." actions={<Button>New claim</Button>} />
  <Stack gap={6}>
    {/* sections */}
  </Stack>
</PageShell>
```

`PageShell` exists because the scaffold is easy to get subtly wrong. The
sidebar is `fixed` with a scrim below `lg` and `static` above it, and there is
a `min-w-0` chain that must run down **every** flex ancestor between the page
and a wide table — a flex item defaults to `min-width: auto` and refuses to
shrink below its content, so one missing link makes the whole page scroll
sideways. It presents as a table bug and isn't one.

## Choosing a layout tool

| Situation | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Children in one direction, even spacing | `<Stack>` / `<Inline>` |
| Two-dimensional — reflowing columns, spans, ordering | Grid utilities — see **Foundations → Grid** |
| The page frame | `<PageShell>` |

`Stack` and `Inline` take the spacing scale as a **type**: `gap={7}` (28px,
off-scale) is a compile error, where `className="gap-7"` compiles happily and
is quietly 4px wrong. Spacing rules and the CI gate that enforces them are in
**Foundations → Spacing**.

## Adding a component

`taxonomy.test.ts` fails if a module on disk is unclassified, so a new
component means a new taxonomy entry. Also required: a `.stories.tsx` covering
every variant, a `.test.tsx`, and a passing `npm run composition:check:strict`
and `npm run roles:check`.

Full checklist: the `composition` skill in `.claude/skills/composition/`.

## Semantic Tokens

Semantic tokens express *purpose*, not raw palette values. They define how color intent changes between light and dark mode. Toggle to see dark-mode values. Click any swatch to copy hex — click any token name to copy it.

<SemanticColorCards />

## Roles (Component API)

Roles are the stable interface components consume — as `var(--role-*)` CSS variables (via `roleVar('role.name')`); `getRoleColor()` is the legacy JS resolver, now residual. They resolve through semantic tokens to primitives. Components must never reference primitives or semantics directly.

<div style={{
  background: '#fff8ed',
  border: '1px solid #ffb700',
  borderRadius: 8,
  padding: '14px 16px',
  margin: '16px 0 28px',
  fontFamily: 'system-ui,sans-serif',
  fontSize: 12.5,
  color: '#5c4300',
  lineHeight: 1.6,
}}>
  <strong>Two unrelated meanings of "secondary" live on this page — easy to conflate.</strong> "Brand secondary" above (Sky Blue, <code>brandSecondary</code>) names the second color in Marsh's brand identity — an accent, not a text color. <code>fg.neutral.subtle</code> below is a completely different axis: text-hierarchy secondary, i.e. de-emphasized body text — it resolves to a muted warm grey (<code>neutral900</code>), not to Sky Blue. Same word, two independent scales (brand-identity position vs. text-emphasis level) that happen to share a name. When you see "secondary" on a role, ask which axis it's on before assuming a color.
  <br /><br />
  <strong>Confirmed intentional (2026-09-15):</strong> Figma's own <code>Text &amp; icon/Secondary</code> variable actually resolves to Gold, not Sky Blue — so Figma's "secondary" collapses both axes into one word, and MDS's split naming is the deliberate, correct departure, not a bug to reconcile. See <code>docs/FIGMA_SEMANTIC_TOKEN_ASSESSMENT.md</code> for the full comparison.

foundations-theming--docs · ./src/docs/12-Theming.mdx
# Theming — light, dark and inverse Every colour in MDS changes with the theme on its own....
import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';

<Meta title="Foundations/Theming" />

# Theming — light, dark and inverse

Every colour in MDS changes with the theme on its own. You never write a dark-mode
rule: you reference a role or an MDS class, and the value behind it is redefined
when the theme changes.

This page is about the one thing you do have to know — **what switches the theme**,
and the two places where that is not yet uniform.

---

## The rule

> **Never write `dark:` for a colour.** The variable already flips. A `dark:`
> colour class is a second, hand-maintained answer that will disagree with the
> first one eventually.

```jsx
// ✅ flips on its own
<div className="bg-default text-primary" />
<div style={{ color: roleVar('fg.critical') }} />

// ❌ two answers for one decision
<div className="bg-white dark:bg-neutral-900" />
<div style={{ color: isDark ? '#ceecff' : '#000f47' }} />
```

`dark:` is still correct for things that are *not* colour — a shadow, an opacity,
a border width you genuinely want different in dark.

---

## What switches the theme

Three mechanisms, and they do not all reach the same layers. This matters the
moment you nest one theme inside another.

| Mechanism | Where it goes | What it switches |
|---|---|---|
| `data-theme="light｜dark"` | `<html>` | The generated token layer (`--mds-color-*`) |
| `.dark` class | `<html>` | The generated layer, **plus** the role tier (`--role-*`), the shadcn variables, and Tailwind's `dark:` variant |
| `data-surface="light｜dark｜inverse"` | any element | The generated token layer only — **not** `--role-*` |

The app writes **both** `data-theme` and `.dark`, so in normal use you never think
about the difference. `ThemeModeProvider` sets them together, and `index.html`
sets them before first paint so the very first render is already correct.

### Why both

`data-theme` is the mechanism the generated layer is built on, and it is what a
nested surface needs. The `.dark` class is the contract the **published package**
ships — `darkMode: ['class']` and `@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *))` — so a
consuming app that follows our docs and sets a class gets correct colours. Drop
either one and half the system stops following the theme.

---

## Nesting a surface

A navy band inside a light page, or a light card inside that band:

```jsx
<section data-surface="dark">      {/* dark band in a light page */}
  <Card data-surface="light" />    {/* light card inside the band */}
</section>
```

Inside the band, every `--mds-color-*` resolves to its dark value, so MDS classes
(`bg-default`, `text-primary`, `border-subtle`) are correct automatically.

> **Known limitation.** `--role-*` does **not** respond to `data-surface`. The role
> tier is emitted only for `:root` and `.dark`, so inside a `data-surface` band a
> component styled with `roleVar('bg.default')` keeps the **page** theme while a
> component styled with `bg-default` takes the **band** theme. Mixing the two in
> one nested surface will not look right. Until the role tier gains the attribute,
> style nested surfaces with MDS classes.

---

## Two ways to read a colour in JS

```jsx
import { roleVar, getRoleColor } from '@/theme/roles';

style={{ color: roleVar('fg.primary') }}              // var(--role-fg-primary)
style={{ color: getRoleColor('fg.primary') }}          // '#000f47'
```

**Prefer `roleVar()`.** It emits a variable reference, so the value follows the
theme through the cascade and a consumer can retheme it.

**`getRoleColor()` bakes a literal** into the DOM. Nothing can retheme it
afterwards, and it decides the mode by reading `<html>` at render time. Reach for
it only when you need the actual string — a canvas fill, a contrast calculation —
or when you are forcing a mode on purpose:

```jsx
// The side-nav rail is dark inside a light page, so it needs the dark value
// baked in. A variable here would follow the page and turn the rail white.
getRoleColor('bg.neutral.subtle', { mode: 'dark' })
```

Those seven calls in `side-navigation.tsx` are the only `getRoleColor` left in the
published component set; everything else resolves through variables.

---

## Inverse

`[data-surface="inverse"]` is a third set of values in the token layer, carried in
the Figma export alongside Light and Dark. The CSS is live today.

The **JavaScript** side is not: `ThemeMode` is `'light' | 'dark'`, so
`getRoleColor(role, { mode: 'inverse' })` does not type-check and
`ThemeModeProvider` cannot be put into it. Inverse is usable as a nested surface,
not as a page mode.

---

## What is enforced

You do not have to remember most of this — the gates fail if it drifts.

| Check | What it would catch |
|---|---|
| `pins:check` | A pinned role whose shipped CSS disagrees with the Figma export, in either mode |
| `pkg:css:selftest` | The published stylesheet losing its `.dark` binding — which would silently give every consumer light colours |
| `dark:check` | A story that fails accessibility in dark mode and was not already failing |
| `tokens:contrast:all` | An enforced foreground/background pair dropping below its ratio in either mode |
| `roles:check:strict` | A hardcoded hex or a Tailwind palette class in `src/components/ui/` |

---

## If a colour does not flip

1. **Is it a hex?** Search the component for `#`. A literal cannot flip.
2. **Is it a `dark:` class?** Delete it and use the role or MDS class alone.
3. **Is it `getRoleColor()` without a mode?** It baked the value at render. Use
   `roleVar()` instead.
4. **Is it inside a `data-surface` band?** See the limitation above — role
   variables do not follow `data-surface`.
5. **Is it a consumer app?** Confirm the host sets `.dark` on `<html>`, not only
   `data-theme`, and that it imports the package stylesheet.

# Accessibility Accessibility is integral—not an afterthought. These guidelines summarize ...
import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';

<Meta title="Foundations/Accessibility" />

# Accessibility

Accessibility is integral—not an afterthought. These guidelines summarize baseline expectations when building components.

## Color & Contrast
- Maintain WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1 for body, 3:1 for large text / UI affordances).
- Avoid using only color to convey meaning; pair with iconography or text.
- Validate themed variants in both light & dark backgrounds.

## Focus States
- All interactive elements must show a clearly visible focus ring (minimum 2px contrast outline or equivalent offset shadow).
- Don’t remove outlines without providing an accessible replacement.

## Keyboard Navigation
- Tab order follows DOM order; avoid tabindex greater than 0.
- Provide Escape to close modals, menus, popovers.
- Use Arrow key patterns for composite widgets (menus, listboxes, tablists).

## Roles & ARIA
- Prefer native elements first (`button`, `input`, `select`) before custom roles.
- When necessary, apply correct ARIA attributes (`aria-expanded`, `aria-selected`, `aria-live`) and keep them in sync with state.
- Avoid redundant roles on native elements (e.g. `role="button"` on a `button` element).

## Motion & Reduction
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion: offer non-animated or simplified transitions.
- Avoid large parallax / continuous motion in dashboards.

## Testing Checklist
- Can all primary flows be completed with keyboard only?
- Do interactive components announce purpose, state, and changes to assistive tech?
- Are error messages programmatically associated with inputs?
- Are focus traps correctly released when layers close?

---
_Future: add live contrast checker + keyboard focus demo components._

foundations-typography--docs · ./src/docs/20-Typography.mdx
# Typography **Two expressions. The only difference is `display` and `h1`–`h6`: face and w...
import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import { TypographyTable } from './_components/TypographyTable';
import { DoDont } from './_components/DoDont';

<Meta title="Foundations/Typography" />

# Typography

**Two expressions. The only difference is `display` and `h1`–`h6`: face and
weight.** Body, UI copy and buttons are Noto Sans in both.

| | headings | body / UI |
|---|---|---|
| **Product** (dashboards, tools) | **Noto Sans 700** | Noto Sans 400 |
| **Marketing** (hero, long-form) | **Marsh Serif 400** | Noto Sans 400 |

## Pick a class

`text-h1` is Noto Sans. `text-serif-h1` is Marsh Serif. The **unmarked name is
the common case**, because most of what this system builds is product UI — mark
the exception, not the norm. `serif` also says what you get, where the earlier
`expressive` / `productive` naming had to be learned.

```tsx
<h1 className="text-h1">Portfolio overview</h1>        {/* product */}
<h1 className="text-serif-h1">A new chapter</h1>       {/* marketing */}
```

These ship in the published package, so a consumer can write them in their own
code — verified in `dist-pkg/styles.css` rather than assumed.

## `h1`–`h6`, level by level

**The two scales do not align level-for-level, and they are not meant to.**

| level | product — `text-h*` | marketing — `text-serif-h*` |
|---|---|---|
| `hero` | — | **40 → 72px**, Marsh Serif 400 |
| `h1` | **30px**, Noto Sans **700** | **28 → 36px**, Marsh Serif **400** |
| `h2` | **24px**, Noto Sans **700** | **24 → 28px**, Marsh Serif **400** |
| `h3` | **20px**, Noto Sans **700** | **20 → 24px**, Marsh Serif **400** |
| `h4` | **18px**, Noto Sans **600** | **18 → 20px**, Marsh Serif **400** |
| `h5` | **16px**, Noto Sans **600** | **16 → 18px**, Marsh Serif **400** |
| `h6` | **14px**, Noto Sans **600** | **14 → 16px**, Marsh Serif **400** |

Three differences, each deliberate:

**Weight.** Product headings are **700** at `h1`–`h3` and **600** at `h4`–`h6`;
marketing is **400** throughout. A serif at a heavy weight is a combination
nobody designed — `font-serif-expressive font-bold` is explicitly in the
Don't list below. Product headings carry hierarchy by weight because they sit
in dense, scannable UI; marketing carries it by size and whitespace.

**Fluid vs fixed.** Marketing sizes are `clamp()` between a 360px and a 1536px
viewport, so a hero headline scales with the page. Product sizes are **fixed**
steps: a dashboard heading that reflows as you resize a window makes a data
table feel unstable, and the viewport is usually a desktop anyway.

Both are `rem`-based, so both respect the browser font-size setting
(WCAG 1.4.4). At a 20px browser default every size above grows proportionally —
that is the point, not a bug.

**Where the product scale comes from.** `text-h1`…`text-h6` are the stock
Tailwind steps — `text-3xl`, `text-2xl`, `text-xl`, `text-lg`, `text-base`,
`text-sm` — with the face and weight attached. That is intentional: dashboard
pages already wrote exactly those by hand (`text-2xl font-bold` in three
places), so the classes change nothing visually and only stop the face and
weight being re-chosen each time. `text-h1` at 30px is `text-3xl`, which is why
it does not match the marketing `h1`'s 28–36px range.

`text-serif-hero` has no product counterpart on purpose. A full-bleed 72px
headline is a marketing device; a dashboard that needs one is probably a
marketing page.

**Pick by expression, not by element.** `PageHeading` renders an `<h1>` at
`text-2xl`, not `text-h1` — because that is what dashboard page titles already
render at. The element is semantics; the class is appearance.

## Four dashboard roles, and only four

A style earns a name **only when it bundles three or more decisions** you would
otherwise re-derive every time. Below that bar Tailwind's own class is better:
shorter, precise, and it tells you the size. `text-sm` beats a `text-data-cell`
that resolves to `text-sm` and *removes* information.

| class | resolves to | why it earns a name |
|---|---|---|
| `text-metric-value` | `text-3xl` + bold + tight tracking + tabular | nobody remembers tracking **and** tabular every time |
| `text-data-header` | `text-xs` + semibold + wide tracking + uppercase | consolidates **five** independent takes that existed in `card`, `list`, `notifications-drawer`, `stepper` and `toast` |
| `text-metric-delta` | `text-sm` + medium + tabular | |
| `text-data-numeric` | `text-sm` + tabular | the deliberate two-decision exception: `tabular-nums` is the most-forgotten decision in a data product |

Everything else uses the stock scale — `text-sm`, `font-medium`,
`tracking-wide`. That part should stay boring: developers already know it, and
designers can mirror the same names as Figma text styles.

## Scale (preview)

<TypographyTable />

## Guidance

- Use semantic heading levels (`<h1>`…`<h6>`) for document hierarchy, and pick
  the class by **expression**, not by element. An `<h1>` rendering at
  `text-2xl` is fine and common on dashboards.
- Line length: target 60–70ch for reading views.
- Line height: body 1.55–1.6; headings 1.1–1.45.
- Tables: use `text-data-numeric` or add `tabular-nums`, so digits align.

## Legacy — being retired

Three mechanisms predate the classes above. They still work; **do not write new
code against them.**

**`.mds-dashboard` / `[data-typography-context='dashboard']`** — an ambient
scope on a subtree root that redefined `--typo-*` for everything inside. Three
problems, all silent: `:root` was the *marketing* expression, so a product
screen that forgot the class rendered serif headings with no error; it did not
survive a Radix portal, so `notifications-drawer` had to repeat it by hand; and
it never reached the published package at all. **Removed from every
`src/components/ui/` component on 2026-10-08** (36 reads across 23 files) and
guarded by the `typo_scope_free` metric. It remains on `PageShell` only because
~117 ad-hoc headings in app *pages* still depend on it.

**`.typography-h2` / `.typography-body1` and the `apply-variant` SCSS mixin** —
in `src/styles/_typography.scss`, used by marketing CSS Modules. Zero usage in
`src/components/ui/`.

**MUI `<Typography variant="h4">` and `sx={{ typography: 'body2' }}`** — MUI is
being removed; `src/theme.ts` still reads `--typo-*` for its 56 references.

Full migration plan and remaining steps:
`docs/tasks/typography-system.md`.

## Do & Don't

<DoDont
	do={[
		{ body: <>Pick the class by expression: <code>text-h1</code> for product, <code>text-serif-h1</code> for marketing.</> },
		{ body: <>Structure content with semantic headings (one <code>h1</code> per page), then <code>h2</code>–<code>h6</code> in order.</> },
		{ body: <>Use the stock scale (<code>text-sm</code>, <code>font-medium</code>) for anything that is not one of the four named roles.</> },
		{ body: <>Use <code>text-data-numeric</code> or <code>tabular-nums</code> wherever digits line up in a column.</> },
		{ body: <>Target line length around <strong>60–70ch</strong> in reading views.</> },
		{ body: <>Keep body text at <strong>16px</strong> with line-height ~<strong>1.55–1.6</strong>.</> },
	]}
	dont={[
		{ body: <>Hardcode a <code>font-size</code> like <code>0.875rem</code>, or a <code>font-family</code>, in a component.</> },
		{ body: <>Write new code against <code>.mds-dashboard</code>, <code>--typo-*</code>, <code>.typography-*</code> or MUI <code>variant</code>.</> },
		{ body: <>Combine the serif face with a bold weight — <code>font-serif-expressive font-bold</code> is a pairing nobody designed.</> },
		{ body: <>Use fluid serif sizes on a dashboard, where headings would reflow as the window resizes.</> },
		{ body: <>Use display faces for long paragraphs or dense tables.</> },
		{ body: <>Drop persistent UI text below <strong>14px</strong>, or use captions for critical information.</> },
	]}
/>

# Roles Layer Roles are an intent-focused abstraction above semantic tokens. Components sh...
import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import { listRoles, getRoleColor } from '../theme/roles';

<Meta title="Foundations/Roles" />


# Roles Layer

Roles are an intent-focused abstraction above semantic tokens. Components should prefer roles instead of referencing `semanticColors` or primitive tokens directly. This improves resilience when refactoring themes, adding new modes, or adjusting accessibility constraints.

## Why Roles?
- Decouples component styling from raw semantic token names
- Enables alternative mode mappings (e.g. high-contrast) without component churn
- Provides a vocabulary aligning design + engineering (fg.primary, bg.neutral.subtle, bg.success.subtle)
- Simplifies validation: we can test role → color resolution instead of every component path

## Role Directory

Below is the current role map. Dark mode values are derived automatically via semantic dark overrides (if defined for the underlying semantic color).

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th style={{textAlign:'left'}}>Role</th>
      <th style={{textAlign:'left'}}>Semantic Token</th>
      <th style={{textAlign:'left'}}>Description</th>
      <th style={{textAlign:'center'}}>Light</th>
      <th style={{textAlign:'center'}}>Dark</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    {listRoles().map(r => {
      const light = getRoleColor(r.role, { mode: 'light' });
      const dark = getRoleColor(r.role, { mode: 'dark' });
      // Translucent roles (border.subtle in dark) composite over their
      // backdrop by design — drawn on the white docs page they look like
      // nothing at all. Give those a split ground so the reader sees what the
      // value actually does in both modes.
      const isAlpha = (c) => /rgba|hsla/i.test(String(c));
      const swatchStyle = (color) => ({
        background: isAlpha(color)
          ? `linear-gradient(90deg, #ffffff 50%, #131210 50%)`
          : color,
        boxShadow: isAlpha(color) ? `inset 0 0 0 999px ${color}` : undefined,
        border: '1px solid #e2e2e4',
        borderRadius: 4,
        width: 52,
        height: 22,
        fontSize: 10,
        color: isAlpha(color) ? '#878787' : undefined,
        fontFamily: 'system-ui, sans-serif',
        display: 'flex',
        alignItems: 'center',
        justifyContent: 'center'
      });
      return (
        <tr key={r.role}>
          <td><code>{r.role}</code></td>
          <td><code>{r.semantic}</code></td>
          <td style={{fontSize:12}}>{r.description}</td>
          <td style={{textAlign:'center'}}>
            <div style={swatchStyle(light)}>{light}</div>
          </td>
          <td style={{textAlign:'center'}}>
            <div style={swatchStyle(dark)}>{dark}</div>
          </td>
        </tr>
      );
    })}
  </tbody>
</table>

## Usage Example
```tsx
import { getRoleColor } from 'src/theme/roles';

const Chip = ({ children }) => (
  <span style={{
    color: getRoleColor('fg.neutral.subtle'),
    background: getRoleColor('bg.neutral.subtle'),
    border: `1px solid ${getRoleColor('border.default')}`,
    padding: '4px 8px',
    borderRadius: 8,
    fontSize: 12,
  }}>{children}</span>
);
```

## Choosing a border role

Three border roles look interchangeable and are not:

| Role | For | Contrast obligation |
|------|-----|---------------------|
| `border.default` | The edge of an interactive control — an input outline, a button border, anything a user acts on | **Gated at 3:1** (WCAG 1.4.11). Never swap it for a quieter token to soften a design. |
| `border.subtle` | Hairline rules *inside* a surface the user is already in — table row separators, list dividers, the grid shell | None. It is decoration, not a boundary. Tracked informationally so it cannot drift so faint it stops separating anything. |
| `border.strong` | Deliberate emphasis above the default weight | — |

`border.subtle` is **translucent in dark mode** (`rgba(255,255,255,0.10)`), not a
fixed grey. A hairline has to composite over whatever sits behind it — the page,
a raised panel, a pinned cell — and one fixed value cannot be correct on all
three. Drawing light mode's `#dedbd6` on a near-black page produces the
brightest line on the screen, which is the bug this replaced.

## Choosing a surface role

`bg.raised` is a panel sitting *above* the page. In light it is the same
white as `bg.default` — paper on paper needs no lift, the border does that
work. In dark it is genuinely lighter (`#191816` against the `#131210` page), so
a grid or card reads as a surface rather than a hole cut into the background.

For a row's state, the roles are not interchangeable either: **selection** is
`bg.selected` (a brand tint — a state the user caused), while **hover** and
**striping** are `bg.neutral.subtle` (a neutral lift). Reusing the neutral lift
for selection is a mistake this codebase has already made: the old
`bg.neutral.subtle` sat one step from `bg.neutral.subtle` in light — so selected and
hovered rows rendered identically — and the two have since collapsed into the
single `bg.neutral.subtle`. Selection must be `bg.selected`, never the lift.

## Guidelines
- Introduce a new role only when multiple components share the intent and a semantic token name would leak implementation.
- Avoid duplicating semantic names as roles (e.g. no `fgPrimary` role) — prefer `fg.primary` pattern.
- Mark deprecated roles in future via metadata and surface during validation.

## Next Steps
Planned enhancements:
1. Snapshot test of role resolutions
2. Lint rule preventing direct primitive / semantic usage in components
3. High-contrast / alternative mode mapping demonstration

## Enforcement Ladder
Governance phases and current status:

| Phase | Mechanism | Status |
|-------|-----------|--------|
| 1 | Warn-only script (`npm run roles:check`) | Complete |
| 2 | Strict mode opt-in (`npm run roles:check:strict`) | Complete |
| 3 | Full CI gate (`governance:ci` in workflow) | Active |
| 4 | ESLint rule (auto-fix suggestions) | Planned |

All components now use roles (0 direct primitive/semantic references). CI fails on regressions via `governance:ci`.

## Contrast Governance
All role foreground/background pairs are enforced in contrast tests. There is no monitored backlog. Introducing a new role pair should include an enforced contrast entry from day one unless there is a clearly documented incremental plan.

_Last updated: full role contrast enforcement & CI gate active._

# Spacing Everything in this system sits on a **4px grid**. There is one grid and two ways...
import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import { spacing } from '../spacing';
import { TokenTable } from './_components/TokenTable';

<Meta title="Foundations/Spacing" />

{/*
  This page documents BOTH spacing tracks on purpose.

  The previous version described only `theme.spacing(index)` — the MUI track —
  while all 73 components in src/components/ui use Tailwind utility classes.
  A developer reading it would not have found the API their component actually
  needs. The mapping table below is generated from `spacing.ts` so the two
  tracks cannot silently diverge in this document.
*/}

# Spacing

Everything in this system sits on a **4px grid**. There is one grid and two ways
to write it, because the component set spans two styling tracks.

The important thing to know up front: **Tailwind's default spacing scale is
already a 4px grid.** That is why `tailwind.config.js` does not extend
`spacing` — it does not need to. Every step in the MDS scale is reachable with
a stock Tailwind class, exactly.

Since the v4 upgrade the whole scale derives from one variable:

```css
--spacing: 0.25rem;                    /* 4px */
.p-4 { padding: calc(var(--spacing) * 4) }   /* 1rem */
```

Practically that means the entire grid can be retuned from a single value — a
denser build could set `--spacing: 0.1875rem` (3px) and every utility follows.
Nothing here does that today, and it should not be done casually, but it is
worth knowing the lever exists.

## Which API to use

| You are working on… | Use | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Laying out children** (the common case) | `Stack` / `Inline` | `<Stack gap={4}>` |
| A component in `src/components/ui/` (shadcn/Radix) | Tailwind utility classes | `className="p-4 gap-2"` |
| An MUI-based component or an `sx` prop | `theme.spacing(index)` | `sx={{ p: 3, gap: 2 }}` |

All three land on the same pixel values. Do not convert between them by hand —
use the table below.

**Prefer `Stack`/`Inline` when you are spacing siblings.** They take the same
scale, but as a *type*: `gap={7}` (28px — not a step) is a compile error,
whereas `className="gap-7"` compiles happily and is quietly 4px off. See
**Components → Stack**.

## The scale

`spacing[i]` is **index-based**; the Tailwind class is **named for the pixel
value ÷ 4**. This is the single most common source of confusion: `spacing[3]`
is 16px, and 16px is `p-4`, not `p-3`.

<TokenTable
  columns={[
    { key: 'index', label: 'spacing[i]', width: 90 },
    { key: 'value', label: 'px', width: 55 },
    { key: 'rem', label: 'rem', width: 70 },
    { key: 'tw', label: 'Tailwind', width: 85 },
    { key: 'mui', label: 'MUI sx', width: 80 },
    { key: 'visual', label: 'Visual' }
  ]}
  rows={spacing.map((v, i) => ({
    index: i,
    value: v,
    rem: `${v / 16}rem`,
    tw: `p-${v / 4}`,
    mui: `p: ${i}`,
    visual: <div style={{ width: v, height: 12, background: '#002c77', borderRadius: 2 }} />
  }))}
  caption="All 15 MDS steps map exactly onto stock Tailwind classes — no config extension required. rem values assume the browser default 16px root, which this app does not override."
/>

### px or rem — they are not interchangeable here

The two tracks emit **different units**, and that has a real consequence:

| Track | What it emits | Under a user font-size change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tailwind (`p-4`) | `padding: 1rem` | **Scales** with the user's setting |
| MUI (`sx={{ p: 3 }}`) | `padding: 16px` | **Fixed** |

`spacing.ts` stores plain numbers and `src/theme.ts`'s `spacingFn` appends
`px`, so every MUI-spaced component is pinned to absolute pixels while every
shadcn component reflows. A user who raises their browser font size gets a
layout where half the components grow and half do not.

That matters for **WCAG 1.4.4 (Resize Text)**. It is not a defect in either
track on its own — it is a consequence of the two coexisting, and it is worth
knowing before choosing which to build a new dense layout in. Prefer the
Tailwind track for anything text-adjacent.

The `rem` column above is the conversion: divide px by 16.

## One scale, many utilities

The same 15 steps drive every spacing utility — padding, margin, gap, and the
sizing/inset families. Picking a step is one decision; which property you apply
it to is another.

| Family | Tailwind | MUI `sx` | Used here |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gap (flex/grid) | `gap-4` `gap-x-2` `gap-y-6` | `gap: 3` | **231** |
| Padding, all sides | `p-4` | `p: 3` | 90 |
| Padding, axis | `px-4` `py-2` | `px: 3` `py: 1` | 177 |
| Padding, one side | `pt-2` `pr-3` `pb-2` `pl-3` | `pt: 1` … | 42 |
| Margin, all sides | `m-4` | `m: 3` | — |
| Margin, axis | `mx-auto` `my-4` | `mx: 'auto'` `my: 3` | 7 |
| Margin, one side | `mt-4` `mb-2` | `mt: 3` `mb: 1` | 65 |
| Space between children | `space-y-2` `space-x-4` | — | 8 |

Counts are live usage in `src/components/ui/`.

### Prefer `gap` over margins

`gap-*` outnumbers every margin utility here roughly three to one, and that is
the house style rather than an accident. Gap spaces children from the parent, so
it cannot collapse, cannot double up against a sibling's margin, and leaves no
stray trailing space on the last child. Reach for a flex or grid container with
`gap-*` before adding `mb-*` to a list of items.

Margins are still right for pushing a single element away from its neighbours —
`mt-*` on a section heading, `mb-*` on a standalone block. Both are in the
system; the ordering is a default, not a prohibition.

Negative margins (`-mt-2`, `-mx-4`) exist and are used sparingly — 5 occurrences,
all for deliberate overlap such as pulling a border flush. They are legitimate
but should be commented where they appear.

### Physical vs logical properties

Tailwind offers both physical (`ml-` `mr-` `pl-` `pr-`) and logical
(`ms-` `me-` `ps-` `pe-`) directions. Logical properties flip automatically in
right-to-left locales; physical ones do not.

**Today this system uses 64 physical and 0 logical.** That is fine while every
consumer is left-to-right, and it is the single thing that would need changing
first if a right-to-left market is ever in scope. New components should prefer
`ms-`/`me-`/`ps-`/`pe-` where the choice is arbitrary, so the retrofit shrinks
rather than grows.

## Dense half-steps

Tailwind's default scale also offers **2px half-steps** (`1.5`, `2.5`, `3.5`)
that the MDS index scale does not contain. These are **permitted in dense,
list-like UI** — menu items, table rows, drawer rows, chips — where 4px is too
tight and 8px too loose.

| Class | px | rem | Where it is appropriate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `p-1.5` | 6px | `0.375rem` | Menu and dropdown items, compact chips |
| `p-2.5` | 10px | `0.625rem` | Table cells at compact density, drawer rows |
| `p-3.5` | 14px | `0.875rem` | Rare — prefer `p-3` (12px) or `p-4` (16px) first |

They are a deliberate sub-scale, not an escape hatch. Reach for a full step
first; use a half-step only when the full step is visibly wrong.

## What not to do

- **No arbitrary values.** `p-[13px]`, `gap-[7px]` and similar bypass the grid
  entirely. This is now **enforced** — see below.
- **Do not hand-convert between the tracks.** `spacing[6]` is 32px is `p-8`.
  Guessing produces `p-6` (24px) and a layout that is one step out.
- **Do not add a step to `spacing.ts` casually.** The scale is deliberately
  curated — 4px micro-steps at the small end, widening to 16px intervals at the
  large end. See the token request process before extending it.

## Enforcement

`npm run composition:check` reports, and `composition:check:strict` **fails**
CI (via `governance:ci`) on two things:

| Rejected | Why | Instead |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `p-[16px]`, `gap-[8px]` | An arbitrary value is a scale step spelled so it bypasses the scale | `p-4`, `gap-2` |
| `gap-7` (28px), `pr-9` (36px) | Compiles fine; not a value in `spacing.ts` | `gap-6`/`gap-8`, `pr-8`/`pr-10` |

`p-[var(--x)]` is allowed — reading a token is the sanctioned use of an
arbitrary value.

When the check was first run it found 20 arbitrary values and 5 off-scale
steps, including `gap-[8px]` five times. Those are fixed; the gate keeps them
fixed.

**Escape hatches:** `spacing-allow` on the line, `spacing-allow-file` in the
file. Legitimate for values derived from a control's **geometry** — the 28px
indent aligning checkbox helper text under its label, the 36px padding
clearing a calendar icon button — but not for dodging a spacing decision.
Say which in the comment.

A third check is **advisory and never fails**: physical properties
(`ml-`/`mr-`/`pl-`/`pr-`) over logical ones (`ms-`/`me-`/`ps-`/`pe-`).
Currently 61 physical, 0 logical. That number should shrink, not grow.

## Layout guidance

- Container padding: **16 / 24 / 32** (`p-4` / `p-6` / `p-8`) by breakpoint.
- Vertical rhythm in dense panels: multiples of **8** (`gap-2`, `gap-4`).
- Dashboard section gutters: **32–48** (`gap-8` … `gap-12`).
- Compact table rows: **6–10** via the half-steps above.
- Stacks and lists: a flex/grid parent with `gap-*`, not `mb-*` on each child —
  or better, `<Stack gap={n}>`, which cannot drift off-scale.
- Starting a whole page? Use the `PageShell` template rather than rebuilding
  the frame. See **Components → PageShell**.

### Control heights

Every interactive control — buttons *and* fields — shares one height scale,
defined in `src/components/ui/control-size.ts`:

| `size` | Height | Padding | Type | Icon |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sm` | 32px (`h-8`) | `px-2.5` | `text-sm` | 14px |
| `md` | 40px (`h-10`) | `px-3` | `text-sm` | 16px |
| `lg` | 48px (`h-12`) | `px-4` | `text-base` | 20px |

The rule this enforces: **a control and a button declaring the same size are
the same height.** They constantly sit side by side — filter bars, search
rows, button groups — and nothing else checks it.

It did not hold before. `size="md"` meant 48px on a Button and 40px on an
Input and Select, so the button towered over the fields in every such row.
Four more controls (Textarea, Combobox, DatePicker, InputOTP) had no size
prop at all and had drifted to 40px, 32px and 40px respectively. The scale
now lives in one file and every control reads from it; a height defined
privately inside one component's cva block is how that drift started.

Two deliberate exclusions:

- **Textarea** takes the padding and type but no fixed height — its height
  comes from content and `rows`.
- **Checkbox, Radio, Switch** sit on their own scale. They are glyphs, not
  text boxes, and stretching them to 40px would look broken.

Grouped controls cascade: `<ButtonGroup size="sm">` and `<InputGroup size="sm">`
publish the size through context, so children inherit it and a group with a
mismatched child is not expressible by accident. A child's own `size` still
wins for the deliberate exception.

### Form rhythm

Forms are the densest nesting in the system, so the steps are fixed and
deliberately **tighten inward**:

| Level | Component | Class | px |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Section — legend ↔ groups | `FieldSet` | `gap-6` | 24 |
| Between fields | `FieldGroup` | `gap-5` | 20 |
| Label ↔ control | `Field` | `gap-3` | 12 |
| Label ↔ description | `FieldContent` | `gap-1.5` | 6 |

Two constraints produced these, and both matter if you ever revisit them:

1. **Outer must be ≥ inner.** `FieldGroup` previously used `gap-7` (28px),
   which was *looser* than the `FieldSet` (24px) containing it — so fields
   read as less related to each other than to the heading above them.
2. **Inter-field spacing must stay clear of the field's own 12px internal
   gap.** At 20px the ratio is ~1.7×, enough to keep field boundaries
   legible. 16px (1.3×) was tested and rejected: it starts to blur which
   label belongs to which input.

Checkbox and radio groups collapse to `gap-3` (12px) at both levels, because
their rows are single-line and do not need field-sized separation.
- Genuinely two-dimensional layout belongs in grid utilities, not nested
  stacks — see **Foundations → Grid**.

## Corner radius

Radius uses **Tailwind's stock scale, unmodified**. Nothing is overridden; what
this system adds is *intent* — which step means what — enforced in CI.

| Class | px | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rounded-none` | 0 | Flush edges, table cells |
| **`rounded-sm`** | **4** | **The control default.** Buttons, inputs, selects, comboboxes, date fields |
| `rounded-md` | 6 | Chips, cells, menu items and other small surfaces |
| `rounded-lg` | 8 | Badges, menu items, small surfaces |
| `rounded-xl` | 12 | Cards, the data-grid shell, dialogs |
| `rounded-2xl` | 16 | Large feature surfaces |
| `rounded-full` | — | Pills, avatars |

`rounded-full` and `rounded-none` are keywords, not steps. `rounded-xs`,
`rounded-sm`, `rounded-3xl` and `rounded-4xl` are valid Tailwind but **rejected
here** — a fifth and sixth corner size is how a scale stops being a scale.

### The 2px era, and why it ended

The system ran on a **2px** radius for its first year: small, squared-off, and
a deliberate part of an institutional, precise feel. It was raised in
**September 2026** — softer surfaces, crisper contents — after a visual review
against contemporary data-grid references found the old value was the single
largest contributor to the system reading as dated.

This was a brand decision, not a tidy-up. If it is ever revisited, revisit it
as one.

### Why nothing is overridden — two failures, not one

**First failure.** `tailwind.config.js` used to rescale `borderRadius` around a
`--radius` variable, because shadcn's defaults assume `0.5rem`. It computed
`rounded-md` as `calc(2px - 2px)` = **0** and drove `rounded-sm` negative, so
roughly **110 components silently rendered square** while their class names
said otherwise.

**Second failure.** The fix for that was an `@theme` block redefining
`--radius-xs` … `--radius-xl` with this system's own values. It held the ladder
monotonic, but it made our class names disagree with the entire ecosystem:
`rounded-lg` meant 12px here and 8px everywhere else, so any snippet copied
from shadcn or the Tailwind docs rendered at the wrong size with no error. And
because `src/styles.package.css` shipped that block, it **redefined `rounded-*`
inside every consuming application** — the same category of mistake as a
library imposing its own CSS reset.

The stock scale already contains four of the five values this system needs, so
neither workaround is necessary. The fifth (10px, for popovers) had exactly two
call sites and was dropped to 8px.

**Do not reintroduce a `borderRadius` override, and do not redeclare
`--radius-*` in `@theme`.** Both are gated.

### The trade-off, stated plainly

There is no single lever any more. Moving the brand radius means a scripted
rename across ~190 call sites rather than editing one variable. That is a real
cost, accepted deliberately: a design system's radius changes rarely, the
rename is mechanical and gate-verified, and the alternative was redefining
words that belong to Tailwind.

### What is gated

`npm run radius:check` (in `governance:ci`) fails on:

- an **arbitrary** radius (`rounded-[7px]`) or the **bare `rounded`** utility —
  Tailwind inlines both, so they answer to nothing;
- a step **outside the four sanctioned ones**, inside `src/components/ui`;
- `src/index.css` or `src/styles.package.css` **reintroducing a `--radius-*`
  override**;
- **this table** disagreeing with those values.

Before this gate existed, nothing in the repo inspected radius at all — not a
script, not a test — so the 2px→6px change would have been invisible to CI.

## Where the values live

- `src/spacing.ts` — the canonical array, exported as `spacing` and consumed by
  the MUI theme's `spacing` function (`src/theme.ts`).
- `dist/tokens.json` — the same 15 steps, exported under `spacing` for Figma and
  non-React consumers.
- Tailwind — **not configured**, because its default scale already matches. If
  the MDS scale ever gains a step that is not a multiple of 4px, Tailwind will
  need an explicit `extend.spacing` entry at that point.

# Grid System

The standard grid for all new work: plain [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/grid-template-columns) grid utilities. No custom classes, no separate import — `grid`, `grid-cols-*`, `gap-*`, and `col-span-*` are built into Tailwind itself and already available everywhere in this app.

## For Designers

### What this gives you

- A 12-column grid at any breakpoint, with `col-span-*` to size an element across N columns
- A spacing scale from 0 to 24rem (`gap-0` through `gap-96`, on the same 4px base as the rest of the design system)
- Five responsive breakpoints, applied with a prefix (`md:grid-cols-4`), not a suffix
- Auto-fit/auto-fill columns for card grids where you don't know the count in advance
- A centered `container` utility, customized for this brand to cap at 1540px (matching the legacy system's own max width, so pages don't visually jump if they mix eras)

### Design tokens

```
Breakpoints (real Tailwind defaults — unmodified in this project):
  sm:  640px
  md:  768px
  lg:  1024px
  xl:  1280px
  2xl: 1536px

Container (tailwind.config.js — the one customization in this system):
  centered: yes
  padding:  16px (default) → 24px (md) → 32px (lg)
  2xl cap:  1540px  ← note: not 1536px. The container's own max-width
                       is set slightly wider than the bare 2xl breakpoint,
                       to match the legacy grid's 1540px container exactly.

Spacing scale (gap-N — 0.25rem/4px base, same grid as everywhere else in MDS):
  gap-0: 0px      gap-4: 16px     gap-12: 48px    gap-24: 96px
  gap-1: 4px      gap-5: 20px     gap-14: 56px    gap-32: 128px
  gap-2: 8px      gap-6: 24px     gap-16: 64px    gap-40: 160px
  gap-3: 12px     gap-8: 32px     gap-20: 80px    gap-48: 192px
```

---

## For Developers

### Nothing to install

Tailwind's grid utilities are generated on demand from whatever classes appear in your JSX — there's no import, no SCSS `@use`, no separate build step. Just write the class names.

```tsx
// No import needed — Tailwind scans src/**/*.{ts,tsx} automatically
<div className="grid grid-cols-12 gap-6">...</div>
```

### The one real customization

`tailwind.config.js`'s `theme.container` is customized so the `container` utility centers, applies the same 16/24/32px padding steps the rest of this app uses, and caps at exactly **1540px** at the `2xl` tier — everything else (`grid-cols-*`, `gap-*`, the `sm/md/lg/xl/2xl` breakpoints themselves) is stock Tailwind, unmodified.

---

## Grid, Stack, or PageShell?

Three tools, and picking the wrong one is the usual cause of layout that
fights back:

| Situation | Use | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Children in **one direction** with even spacing | `<Stack>` / `<Inline>` | The gap is type-checked against the DS scale; `gap={7}` will not compile |
| **Two-dimensional** layout — columns that reflow, spans, ordering | Grid utilities on this page | A grid is what this is. Three nested stacks faking one is harder to read and to change |
| The **page frame** — header, sidebar, main | `<PageShell>` | It already handles the responsive sidebar, the mobile scrim, and the `min-w-0` chain that stops wide tables scrolling the page sideways |

`Stack` and grid compose freely: a `Stack` of sections where one section is a
`grid grid-cols-3` is the normal shape of a dashboard page.

---

## Common Patterns

### Pattern 1 — Two-column layout (main + sidebar)

**When to use**: main content + sidebar layouts, the most common page shape.

```tsx
<div className="grid grid-cols-4 gap-4 md:grid-cols-12">
  <div className="col-span-4 md:col-span-8">Main content</div>
  <div className="col-span-4 md:col-span-4">Sidebar</div>
</div>
```

<div className="grid grid-cols-4 gap-4 md:grid-cols-12" style={{ border: '1px solid #e5e7eb', padding: 8, borderRadius: 6, marginTop: 12 }}>
  <div className="col-span-4 md:col-span-8" style={{ background:'#e5edf4', padding:16, color:'#1a1a1a' }}>
    <strong>Main Content</strong>
    <p style={{ margin: '8px 0 0 0', fontSize: '14px' }}>66% width from md up, 100% below</p>
  </div>
  <div className="col-span-4 md:col-span-4" style={{ background:'#c7edff', padding:16, color:'#1a1a1a' }}>
    <strong>Sidebar</strong>
    <p style={{ margin: '8px 0 0 0', fontSize: '14px' }}>33% width from md up, 100% below</p>
  </div>
</div>

---

### Pattern 2 — Responsive card grid, auto-fit

**When to use**: product cards, blog posts, image galleries — any count of cards, unknown in advance.

```tsx
<div className="grid gap-4" style={{ gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(auto-fit, minmax(220px, 1fr))' }}>
  {products.map((product) => <ProductCard key={product.id} {...product} />)}
</div>
```

<div className="grid gap-4" style={{ gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(auto-fit, minmax(220px, 1fr))', border: '1px solid #e5e7eb', padding: 8, borderRadius: 6, marginTop: 12 }}>
  {Array.from({ length: 6 }).map((_, i) => (
    <div key={i} style={{ background:'#f0faff', padding: 16, borderRadius: 4, textAlign: 'center', color:'#1a1a1a' }}>
      <strong>Card {i + 1}</strong>
      <p style={{ margin: '8px 0 0 0', fontSize: '12px', color: '#666' }}>Auto-fits at 220px min</p>
    </div>
  ))}
</div>

Tailwind doesn't ship a bare `auto-fit` utility (the column-min-width is arbitrary per layout), so this is the one pattern that reaches for an inline `gridTemplateColumns` — everything else on this page is plain classes.

---

**When to use**: analytics dashboards, admin panels with widgets of different heights.

```tsx
<div className="grid grid-cols-3 grid-rows-3 gap-4">
  <div className="row-span-2"><ChartWidget /></div>
  <div><MetricCard title="Revenue" value="$45k" /></div>
  <div className="row-span-3"><ActivityFeed /></div>
  <div><MetricCard title="Users" value="1.2k" /></div>
  <div className="col-span-2"><TableWidget /></div>
</div>
```

<div className="grid grid-cols-3 grid-rows-3 gap-4" style={{ border: '1px solid #e5e7eb', padding: 8, borderRadius: 6, marginTop: 12, minHeight: 300 }}>
  <div className="row-span-2" style={{ background:'#0b4bff', color: 'white', padding: 16, borderRadius: 4, display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'center' }}>
    <strong>Tall Widget (2 rows)</strong>
  </div>
  <div style={{ background:'#f0faff', padding: 16, borderRadius: 4, textAlign: 'center', color:'#1a1a1a' }}>
    <strong>Metric A</strong>
  </div>
  <div className="row-span-3" style={{ background:'#2f7d32', color: 'white', padding: 16, borderRadius: 4, display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'center' }}>
    <strong>Full Height (3 rows)</strong>
  </div>
  <div style={{ background:'#f0faff', padding: 16, borderRadius: 4, textAlign: 'center', color:'#1a1a1a' }}>
    <strong>Metric B</strong>
  </div>
  <div className="col-span-2" style={{ background:'#edf2f7', padding: 16, borderRadius: 4, textAlign: 'center', color:'#1a1a1a' }}>
    <strong>Wide Widget (2 columns)</strong>
  </div>
</div>

---

### Pattern 4 — Sidebar layout (fixed + flexible)

**When to use**: app shells, documentation sites, admin panels.

```tsx
<div className="grid grid-cols-1 gap-4 md:grid-cols-[250px_1fr]">
  <aside><Sidebar /></aside>
  <main><Content /></main>
</div>
```

<div className="grid grid-cols-1 gap-4 md:grid-cols-[250px_1fr]" style={{ border: '1px solid #e5e7eb', padding: 8, borderRadius: 6, marginTop: 12 }}>
  <aside style={{ background:'#f7fafc', padding: 16, borderRadius: 4, color:'#1a1a1a' }}>
    <strong>Sidebar</strong>
    <p style={{ margin: '8px 0 0 0', fontSize: '12px', color: '#666' }}>Fixed 250px from md up</p>
  </aside>
  <main style={{ background:'#edf2f7', padding: 16, borderRadius: 4, color:'#1a1a1a' }}>
    <strong>Main Content</strong>
    <p style={{ margin: '8px 0 0 0', fontSize: '12px', color: '#666' }}>Flexible width</p>
  </main>
</div>

Tailwind's arbitrary-value syntax (`grid-cols-[250px_1fr]`) covers the legacy system's `.grid-cols-sidebar` preset — there's no need for a named utility for a one-off column template.

---

### Pattern 5 — Column ordering (responsive reorder)

**When to use**: show content first on mobile, sidebar first on desktop, without changing DOM order.

```tsx
<div className="grid grid-cols-1 gap-4 md:grid-cols-2">
  <main className="order-2 md:order-1"><Content /></main>
  <aside className="order-1 md:order-2"><Sidebar /></aside>
</div>
```

<div className="grid grid-cols-1 gap-4 md:grid-cols-2" style={{ border: '1px solid #e5e7eb', padding: 8, borderRadius: 6, marginTop: 12 }}>
  <main className="order-2 md:order-1" style={{ background:'#e5edf4', padding: 16, borderRadius: 4, color:'#1a1a1a' }}>
    <strong>Main Content</strong>
    <p style={{ margin: '8px 0 0 0', fontSize: '12px', color: '#666' }}>Second on mobile, first from md up</p>
  </main>
  <aside className="order-1 md:order-2" style={{ background:'#0b4bff', color: 'white', padding: 16, borderRadius: 4 }}>
    <strong>Sidebar</strong>
    <p style={{ margin: '8px 0 0 0', fontSize: '12px' }}>First on mobile, second from md up</p>
  </aside>
</div>

Note the direction — this example deliberately shows main content ordered *after* sidebar in source but *first* visually below `md`, the opposite of Pattern 1. Reorder visually only; keep source order logical for screen readers.

## Complete Utility Reference

| Category | Classes |
|---|---|
| Container | `grid` |
| Columns | `grid-cols-{1-12}`, `col-span-{1-12}`, `col-span-full`, `col-start-{1-13}`, `col-end-{1-13}` |
| Rows | `grid-rows-{1-6}`, `row-span-{1-6}`, `row-span-full`, `row-start-{1-7}`, `row-end-{1-7}` |
| Gap | `gap-{N}`, `gap-x-{N}`, `gap-y-{N}` (full spacing scale, 0–96) |
| Flow | `grid-flow-row`, `grid-flow-col`, `grid-flow-dense`, `grid-flow-row-dense`, `grid-flow-col-dense` |
| Alignment (items) | `items-start`, `items-center`, `items-end`, `items-baseline`, `items-stretch` |
| Alignment (content) | `justify-start`, `justify-center`, `justify-end`, `justify-between`, `justify-around`, `justify-evenly` |
| Combined placement | `place-items-{start\|center\|end\|stretch\|baseline}`, `place-content-{start\|center\|end\|between\|around\|evenly\|stretch}` |
| Ordering | `order-{1-12}`, `order-first`, `order-last`, `order-none` |
| Aspect ratio | `aspect-square`, `aspect-video`, `aspect-[N/M]` (arbitrary ratios) |
| Container | `container` (customized max-width, see above) |
| Responsive prefix | `sm:`, `md:`, `lg:`, `xl:`, `2xl:` — prepend to any class above |

Any class not covered by a named utility (an unusual column template, a one-off ratio) is available via Tailwind's arbitrary-value syntax: `grid-cols-[200px_1fr_200px]`, `aspect-[21/9]`.

---

## Comparison with the Legacy Grid

| | This page (Tailwind) | [Foundations/Grid Legacy](?path=/docs/foundations-⚠️-grid-legacy--docs) |
|---|---|---|
| Use for | All new work, all `ui/*` components | Only the ~26 existing legacy MUI marketing pages/sections that already use it |
| Breakpoints | `sm:640 md:768 lg:1024 xl:1280 2xl:1536` | `sm:576 md:768 lg:1024 xl:1200 xxl:1540` — differs at every tier except md/lg |
| Responsive syntax | Prefix: `md:col-span-6` | Suffix: `mds-legacy-col-md-6` |
| Column span | `col-span-{N}` (of however many `grid-cols-N` defines) | `mds-legacy-col-{N}` (of 12) |
| Container max-width | 1540px (customized to match) | 1540px (native) |
| Gap scale | Same 4px base, `gap-{N}` | Same 4px base, `mds-legacy-gap-{N}` |
| Import needed | None | `_grid.scss`, loaded globally via `global.scss` |

Never mix the two systems' classes on the same element — they use CSS Grid differently and their column-span math doesn't reconcile (12-column vs. whatever `grid-cols-N` you set).

## 👥 For Designers

### What You Can Do

- ✅ **Create responsive layouts** that adapt from mobile to ultra-wide (4K+)
- ✅ **Build dashboard widgets** with different heights and aspect ratios
- ✅ **Design card grids** that auto-fit to any screen size
- ✅ **Control spacing** from 4px to 128px (enterprise-scale)
- ✅ **Align content** horizontally and vertically with subgrid
- ✅ **Reorder elements** visually without changing HTML
- 🆕 **Ultra-wide layouts** for the xxl (1540px+) breakpoint
- 🆕 **Consistent aspect ratios** across all components
- 🆕 **Future-proof alignment** with subgrid utilities

### Design Tokens

```
Breakpoints:
  xs: 0px      (mobile)
  sm: 576px    (tablet portrait)
  md: 768px    (tablet landscape)
  lg: 1024px   (desktop)
  xl: 1200px   (large desktop)
  xxl: 1540px  (ultra-wide)

Containers:
  .container: 100% width up to 1320px max (centered)
  .container-fluid: 100% width (full)

Spacing Scale:
  gap-1: 4px     gap-9: 36px    gap-20: 80px
  gap-2: 8px     gap-10: 40px   gap-24: 96px
  gap-3: 12px    gap-12: 48px   gap-28: 112px (new)
  gap-4: 16px    gap-16: 64px   gap-32: 128px (new)
  gap-6: 24px    gap-8: 32px    + responsive variants
  
Aspect Ratios:
  .aspect-square   (1:1)    .aspect-3-2      (3:2)
  .aspect-video    (16:9)   .aspect-21-9     (21:9)
  .aspect-4-3      (4:3)    .aspect-auto     (reset)
  
Subgrid (Future):
  .subgrid-cols, .subgrid-rows, .subgrid-both
  + responsive variants for all breakpoints
```

## 👨‍💻 For Developers

### Installation

The grid is already wired globally. Just use the classes in your HTML/JSX:

```tsx
// Grid is imported in src/global.scss
// No additional imports needed!
```

### Import in Custom SCSS (Optional)

```scss
@use '../styles/grid' as *;
```

```html
</div>
```

### Pattern 4.3: Subgrid Card Alignment (Future-Ready)

**When to use**: Card grids where headers and footers need perfect alignment

**HTML:**
```html
<!-- Parent defines row structure -->
<div class="mds-legacy-row mds-legacy-gap-6" style="grid-template-rows: auto 1fr auto;">
  <div class="mds-legacy-col-4 mds-legacy-subgrid-rows">
    <h4>Header</h4>
    <p>Variable content length...</p>
    <button>Action</button>
  </div>
  <div class="mds-legacy-col-4 mds-legacy-subgrid-rows">
    <h4>Header</h4>
    <p>Short.</p>
    <button>Action</button>
  </div>
  <div class="mds-legacy-col-4 mds-legacy-subgrid-rows">
    <h4>Header</h4>
    <p>Medium length content.</p>
    <button>Action</button>
  </div>
</div>
```

**React/JSX:**
```tsx
<div className="mds-legacy-row mds-legacy-gap-6" style={{gridTemplateRows: 'auto 1fr auto'}}>
  {products.map(product => (
    <div key={product.id} className="mds-legacy-col-4 mds-legacy-subgrid-rows">
      <h4>{product.title}</h4>
      <p>{product.description}</p>
      <button>Buy Now</button>
    </div>
  ))}
</div>
```

### Pattern 5: Sidebar Layout

**When to use**: App shells, documentation sites, admin panels

**HTML:**
```html
<!-- Fixed 250px sidebar + flexible content -->
<div class="mds-legacy-grid-cols-sidebar mds-legacy-gap-4">
  <aside>Navigation</aside>
  <main>Content Area</main>
</div>

<!-- Responsive: stacks on mobile, sidebar on desktop -->
<div class="mds-legacy-grid-cols-1 mds-legacy-grid-cols-md-sidebar mds-legacy-gap-4">
  <aside>Navigation</aside>
  <main>Content Area</main>
</div>
```

**React/JSX:**
```tsx
<div className="mds-legacy-grid-cols-1 mds-legacy-grid-cols-md-sidebar mds-legacy-gap-4">
  <aside><Sidebar /></aside>
  <main><Content /></main>
</div>
```

### Pattern 6: Column Ordering (Mobile-First)

**When to use**: Reorder content for different screen sizes (sidebar-first on desktop, content-first on mobile)

**HTML:**
```html
<div class="mds-legacy-row mds-legacy-gap-4">
  <!-- Shows first on mobile, second on desktop -->
  <main class="mds-legacy-col-12 mds-legacy-col-md-8 mds-legacy-order-md-2">Main Content</main>
  
  <!-- Shows second on mobile, first on desktop -->
  <aside class="mds-legacy-col-12 mds-legacy-col-md-4 mds-legacy-order-md-1">Sidebar</aside>
</div>
```

**React/JSX:**
```tsx
<div className="mds-legacy-row mds-legacy-gap-4">
  <main className="mds-legacy-col-12 mds-legacy-col-md-8 mds-legacy-order-md-2">
    <Content />
  </main>
  <aside className="mds-legacy-col-12 mds-legacy-col-md-4 mds-legacy-order-md-1">
    <Sidebar />
  </aside>
</div>
```

### Bootstrap-style helpers (familiarity)

We provide optional aliases inspired by Bootstrap for easier migration:

- Equal-width columns per row: `.mds-legacy-row-cols-N` (N=1..6), with responsive variants `.mds-legacy-row-cols-sm-N`, `.mds-legacy-row-cols-md-N`, etc.
- Gap aliases: `.mds-legacy-g-*`, `.mds-legacy-gx-*`, `.mds-legacy-gy-*` mirroring our `.mds-legacy-gap-*`, `.mds-legacy-gap-x-*`, `.mds-legacy-gap-y-*`.

Live preview

<div className="mds-legacy-container" style={{ border: '1px solid #e5e7eb', padding: 8, borderRadius: 6, marginTop: 12 }}>
  <div className="mds-legacy-row mds-legacy-row-cols-3 mds-legacy-g-3">
    {Array.from({ length: 6 }).map((_, i) => (
      <div key={i} style={{ background:'#f4fbff', padding: 12, textAlign:'center', borderRadius: 4, color:'#1a1a1a' }}>Col</div>
    ))}
  </div>
  <div className="mds-legacy-row mds-legacy-row-cols-1 mds-legacy-row-cols-md-2 mds-legacy-row-cols-lg-4 mds-legacy-gx-4 mds-legacy-gy-2" style={{ marginTop: 8 }}>
    {Array.from({ length: 8 }).map((_, i) => (
      <div key={i} style={{ background:'#f7f7ff', padding: 12, textAlign:'center', borderRadius: 4, color:'#1a1a1a' }}>Col</div>
    ))}
  </div>
</div>

Note: Our canonical API is the `.mds-legacy-col-*`, `.mds-legacy-gap-*`, `.mds-legacy-gap-x-*`, `.mds-legacy-gap-y-*` set. The aliases are provided for familiarity and smoother adoption.

## Enhanced Utilities Reference

### Columns & Responsive
- **Columns**: `.mds-legacy-col-1`..`.mds-legacy-col-12`, responsive: `.mds-legacy-col-sm-6`, `.mds-legacy-col-md-4`, `.mds-legacy-col-lg-3`, `.mds-legacy-col-xl-2`, **`.mds-legacy-col-xxl-*`**
- **Auto columns**: `.mds-legacy-col` (equal width), `.mds-legacy-col-auto` (content-based)
- **Custom grids**: `.mds-legacy-grid-cols-1` to `.mds-legacy-grid-cols-12`, responsive: `.mds-legacy-grid-cols-{bp}-{n}`
- **Presets**: `.mds-legacy-grid-auto-fit-{xs|sm|md|lg}`, `.mds-legacy-grid-cols-sidebar`, `.mds-legacy-grid-cols-two-thirds`

### Spacing (Enhanced Scale)
- **Standard**: `.mds-legacy-gap-1` (4px), `.mds-legacy-gap-2` (8px), `.mds-legacy-gap-3` (12px), `.mds-legacy-gap-4` (16px), `.mds-legacy-gap-6` (24px), `.mds-legacy-gap-8` (32px)
- **Extended**: `.mds-legacy-gap-9` (36px), `.mds-legacy-gap-10` (40px), `.mds-legacy-gap-12` (48px), `.mds-legacy-gap-16` (64px), `.mds-legacy-gap-20` (80px), `.mds-legacy-gap-24` (96px)
- **🆕 Enterprise**: **`.mds-legacy-gap-28` (112px)**, **`.mds-legacy-gap-32` (128px)**
- **Directional**: `.mds-legacy-gap-x-*` (column-gap) and `.mds-legacy-gap-y-*` (row-gap)
- **Responsive**: All gaps support `.mds-legacy-gap-{bp}-{n}` (including **`.mds-legacy-gap-xxl-*`**)

### 🆕 Aspect Ratios
- **`.mds-legacy-aspect-square`** (1:1) - Perfect for profile images, icons
- **`.mds-legacy-aspect-video`** (16:9) - Video players, hero images  
- **`.mds-legacy-aspect-4-3`** (4:3) - Traditional photography
- **`.mds-legacy-aspect-3-2`** (3:2) - Modern photography
- **`.mds-legacy-aspect-21-9`** (21:9) - Ultra-wide content
- **`.mds-legacy-aspect-auto`** - Reset to natural ratio

### 🆕 Subgrid (Future-Ready)
- **`.mds-legacy-subgrid-cols`** - Inherit parent's column tracks
- **`.mds-legacy-subgrid-rows`** - Inherit parent's row tracks  
- **`.mds-legacy-subgrid-both`** - Inherit both column and row tracks
- **Responsive**: All subgrid utilities support `.mds-legacy-subgrid-{type}-{bp}` variants

### Containers
- **`.mds-legacy-container`** - Responsive centered container (540px → 1800px max-width)
- **`.mds-legacy-container-fluid`** - Full-width container with consistent padding
- **🆕 Container queries**: `.mds-legacy-container-query`, `.mds-legacy-container-query-size` (future-ready)

### Alignment & Layout
- **Item alignment**: `.mds-legacy-align-{start|center|end}`, `.mds-legacy-justify-{start|center|end}`
- **Content alignment**: `.mds-legacy-content-justify-*` / `.mds-legacy-content-align-*` for grid tracks
- **Row spanning**: `.mds-legacy-row-span-1` to `.mds-legacy-row-span-6`, `.mds-legacy-row-span-full`
- **Column spanning**: `.mds-legacy-col-span-1` to `.mds-legacy-col-span-12`, `.mds-legacy-col-span-full`
- **Grid flow**: `.mds-legacy-grid-flow-{row|col|dense}`

### Offsets & Positioning  
- **Offsets**: `.mds-legacy-offset-1`..`.mds-legacy-offset-11`, responsive: `.mds-legacy-offset-{bp}-{n}`
- **Start position**: `.mds-legacy-start-{n}` to place item at specific grid track
- **Responsive variants**: All positioning supports breakpoint variants

### Visibility & Ordering
- **Hide/Show**: `.mds-legacy-hidden-{bp}`, `.mds-legacy-visible-{bp}`
- **Ordering**: `.mds-legacy-order-0` to `.mds-legacy-order-12`, `.mds-legacy-order-first`, `.mds-legacy-order-last`
- **Responsive ordering**: `.mds-legacy-order-{bp}-{n}`, `.mds-legacy-order-{bp}-first`, `.mds-legacy-order-{bp}-last`

### Breakpoints (Enhanced)
- **`xs`**: 0px (mobile-first baseline)
- **`sm`**: 600px → `.mds-legacy-col-sm-*`, `.mds-legacy-gap-sm-*`
- **`md`**: 900px → `.mds-legacy-col-md-*`, `.mds-legacy-gap-md-*` 
- **`lg`**: 1024px → `.mds-legacy-col-lg-*`, `.mds-legacy-gap-lg-*`
- **`xl`**: 1200px → `.mds-legacy-col-xl-*`, `.mds-legacy-gap-xl-*`
- **🆕 `xxl`**: **1540px → `.mds-legacy-col-xxl-*`, `.mds-legacy-gap-xxl-*`**
- Fluid container: `.mds-legacy-container-fluid` uses full width with consistent horizontal padding

### Auto-fit cards grid

When you don’t know how many cards fit per row, use the auto grid:

```html
<div class="mds-legacy-row-auto" style="--mds-grid-col-min: 220px">
  <div class="card">A</div>
  <div class="card">B</div>
  <div class="card">C</div>
  <div class="card">D</div>
  <div class="card">E</div>
  <div class="card">F</div>
  <!-- more cards -->
  </div>
```

    <div key={i} className="card" style={{ background:'#f9f7fb', padding: 12, textAlign: 'center', borderRadius: 4, color:'#1a1a1a' }}>Card {i+1}</div>

### Fluid container

Use `.mds-legacy-container-fluid` for full-width sections that still need consistent side padding.

